    - **Recovery:**
      - Append sections with transforms;
      - recovered documents chained;
      - a restored document appends its `pending_tail` on its first
        save.
    - **Deletes:**
      - the always-Rewrite rule and Full-only recovery;
      - slice 9's "signed files ask Rewrite or Cancel": the signature
        ask now offers "Append anyway".
    - **Checks:**
      - **Removed text, every feature × both strategies:** the removed
        strings are absent from the decoded bytes (a page, a mark, a
        reply, another tool's comment, a bookmark, replaced mark text, a
        replaced OCR layer, and a re-OCR over a layer saved in an
        earlier session).
      - **Appends after earlier saves:**
        - a mark color change after a Rewrite appends one object under
          the same number;
        - a bookmark rename gives a Rewrite with the old title gone;
        - delete pages, save, undo, save, reopen: `qpdf --check` passes
          and the pages show;
        - undoing to the saved state gives Unchanged and a clean
          document.
      - **Durability:**
        - three consecutive Appends, then a reopen, pass `qpdf --check`;
        - a torn append (killed by a hook) is truncated on the next
          open.
      - **The Append ≡ Rewrite property** (32 cases, default run; over
        `Edit` generators until slice 11 ports it to `Op`), including
        labels i–iii with page 4 moved before page 1, links to pages
        added in later Appends, and a live-token reorder.
      - **The removal check:**
        - a forced misclassification is vetoed and logged;
        - the same veto on a P2 fixture asks and never rewrites.
      - **Recovery:**
        - the sidecar of an encrypted file with an unsaved header
          contains no plaintext;
        - a same-length sidecar against a changed tail is rejected;
        - a restored signed file's first save appends when its sections
          removed nothing, and asks with "Append anyway" when they did.
      - **Signatures:**
        - a P3-certified fixture appends an annotation silently, and a
          P2 fixture asks;
        - a signed file with a deleted comment offers "Append anyway"
          and leaves the signed bytes untouched;
        - a page insert into a signed **hybrid** form offers "Append
          anyway", the section drops `/XFA`, and the signed bytes stay
          intact;
        - a P2-certified, UR3-enabled fixture with `/Annots /Create`
          appends a comment with UR3 and DocMDP byte-intact, and no ask;
        - Save As of a signed file copy-appends, and its byte ranges
          still cover their bytes.
      - **Files:** a change by another program before an Append gives
        `FileChanged`.
      - **Gate:** one mark's incremental save on the 500 MB scan takes
        under 50 ms.

        - a mark edit triggers no relayout;

      - **Relower and Validate:**
        - an `insert_file` whose anchor page is deleted first gives an
          error notice and applies nothing;
        - an `insert_file` during a page move elsewhere is re-lowered,

        - a crop planned while the user deletes another page commits,

        - a dialog based on V, then an OCR amend of V, then the dialog's

        - a stale blank-review `DeletePages` against a concurrently

        - a `Validate` commit whose cascades would add prims conflicts,

        pages of the heavy 7k under a "Page n of N" header gives an
        Append of at most 8 MB, planned and written in at most 1 s, and
        each visible page re-renders within the realize gate. The
        result goes in the slice notes as proposal 8's verdict; a miss
        means frozen numbers plus Update. (Greg kept the numbers live
        and accepted the misses, 2026-10-22: proposal 8's verdict.)
      - **Unencodable labels:** a label change that makes `<<label>>`
        unencodable draws `'?'` with a notice, and saving still works.
18. **OCR as content** (M; proposal 26; bug 14).
    - **The ops:** `SetOcrText` and `ClearOcrText`, in an Ocr group.
    - **Rendering:** OCR renders `content_only`, records the `PageDef`
      it rendered (`read_render`), and converts pixels with the
      render-time `Geom`.
    - **Flushes:** `Validate` per flush. A changed page's result is
      dropped and re-queued.
    - **Removing saved layers:** by the `/SheafBlock` stream marker, or
      by the `/ShOCR` marker inside merged streams. A legacy
      `/SheafOcrLayer` is removed together with its leading `q`.
    - **Re-OCR** replaces a saved layer.
    - **Deletes:**
      - `text_layer::install`, `strip` and `has_layer`, and with them
        slice 9's legacy-shape OCR emission;
      - the presence-means-unsaved remnants;
      - the plugin API's OCR overrides;
      - `/SheafOcr` as the OCR font's resource name, and
        `/SheafOcrLayer` as a written marker (new layers use `/Sh…`
        names and `/SheafBlock`).
    - **Checks:**
      - **Finding and saving:**
        - OCR, then Find, hits words before saving;
        - OCR plus an incremental save appends one stream per page, with
          the glyphless font once per file;
        - an empty layer writes nothing.
      - **Removing saved layers:**
        - replacing a saved layer gives a Rewrite with the old words
          absent;
        - `ClearOcrText` removes a saved layer, including one inside
          streams another tool merged;
        - removing a legacy layer leaves q/Q balanced.
      - **During a run:**
        - a rotate or crop during a run doesn't conflict, and the words
          land correctly;
        - a `ReplacePages` drops that page's result, which is re-queued;
        - OCR of a page with an unsaved header doesn't record the
          header's text.
      - **Undo:** an OCR run is one undo step, and undo during it stops
        the flushes.
19. **Exports, memory sources, Session and `sheaf edit`** (XL; proposals

    - **`FlattenAnnotations`,** with `PinnedAp`.
    - **The presets.**
    - **Memory sources:** blank pages, images-to-PDF, scan, the summary

    - **`Session`.**
    - **Combine** on `Session`, with the app handing the same Document
      to a new window.
    - **`sheaf edit`:**

      - JSON addressing;
      - `-o --append`.
    - **`sheaf inspect --json`.**
    - **Every subcommand** runs on `Session`.
    - **Print** goes to GDI and CUPS from bytes.
    - **The clipboard blob cache.**
    - **The content-round-trip and `temp_dir` clippy bans** (Lint
      ledgers).
    - **Deletes:**
      - **The old exports:**
        - `subset` with its fake `Snapshot`, and `prune_outline`;
        - `print_pdf`, `extract_pages`/`extract_bytes`,
          `export_clean_copy`, `export_flattened`;

    - **Checks:**
      - **Ports:** the extract, split, print, clean and flatten tests

      - **One parametrized every-way-out test** over M10 proposal 7's
        list:
        - `forms::check` is clean;
        - the open file is refused as a target by every export;
        - a clean copy has no `private::KEYS`, including a legacy

        - CLI goldens pass, with exit codes 0, 1, 2, 3 and 130;
        - `--force` only overwrites;
        - `--dry-run` prints lines;
        - a signature ask exits 3 with the Ask as JSON;
        - `-o out.pdf --append` on a signed file keeps its signatures;
        - JSON addressing by position (1-based), title path and `--with`
          works, and a bare-number `Id` ref is `Invalid`;
        - the docs' JSON examples run in CI.

        blob travels.
      - **Gate:** `FlattenAnnotations { All }` on the heavy 7k exports
        with peak RSS under 1.5× the file size plus 200 MB.
20. **Plugin API 0.4** (L; proposals 11, 18, 19 and 20; bugs 27 and
    30).
    - **The WIT:** `sheaf:plugin@0.4.0` as the only world. It has
      `edits` with the envelope, `assets.upload`, and `document` reads
      in PageSpace with view matrices. Annotations exclude widgets,
      authors are roles, and text excludes fields.
    - **Reads** record decision reads (0.2's and 0.3's from slice 12,
      into `CallOutput.reads`).
    - **The call's Tx:**
      - built lazily from the cell (the cell and the base loaded at a
        call's first read or submit are slice 12's);
      - an end-of-call `Relower` with `created` equality (slice 12
        commits 0.2/0.3 calls' first batch with `Relower`, ids pinned,
        without the equality: nothing was handed out);
      - `commit()` mid-call;
      - truncate-or-revert rollback (slice 12's `rollback_group`, which
        0.2/0.3 calls use).
    - **Events:**
      - semantic scopes;
      - merged coalescing;
      - edits triggered by an undo refused;
      - causal depth.
    - **Caps** per resolved target.
    - **The manifest:** `edit-schema` and `permissions` (`identity`).
    - **sheaf-plugin-api** gets `Op`, the `Ops` builder and the view
      helpers.
    - **The bundled plugins** are ported and bumped.
    - **Docs:**
      - `docs/plugins.md`, with the generated schema;
      - the plan-file edits (M10 slices 6+ on the new API, below);
      - `todos/m11.md`, `agent.md` and `file-contention.md` updated
        (Changes to other plans);
      - the final `docs/document-model.md` pass.
    - **A grep test** finds no lopdf `ObjectId` in sheaf-doc outside
      `source/`, `materialize/`, `serialize/`, `content/` and the forms
      facts.
    - **Deletes:**
      - `wit/0.2`, `api/v02.rs` and `api/v03.rs` (included at
        api/mod.rs:38; 0.4's host code replaces it);
      - the double bindgen and `include!(shared.rs)`;
      - `World` and per-plugin world selection, and `API_PREVIOUS`;
      - the 0.2 fixture wasm and its tests;
      - the 0.3 edit variant and the transitional adapter;
      - `edit_from_wit` and `EditBatch`/`CallOutput.batches`;
      - docview.rs's `edit_source` (set by plugins.rs; deleted in slice
        12, a plugin's own edits told by `ChangeSet.actor`) and the apply
        loop per batch (slice 12's `plugins::land`, a call's batches in
        one `PluginCall` group);
      - sheaf-plugin-api's `Batch`;
      - `DocContext`'s per-call save `Snapshot` (deleted in slice 12:
        `DocContext.cell`).
    - **Checks:**
      - **The bundled plugins** pass their tests on 0.4.
      - **Submits:** one submit adds a mark and a reply via a local, and
        a second submit references its id. An envelope with a `label`
        is `Invalid`.
      - **Rollback:**
        - a trap after two submits leaves no version and no redo entry;
        - a trap after an interleaved user edit reverts only the
          plugin's versions.
      - **Staleness:**
        - the subtotal scenario (tapes on page 3 read, the user edits a
          tape, the plugin adds a total on page 5) conflicts;
        - a user edit to an unrelated page during a call is re-lowered,
          and both land.
      - **Caps:** `InsertPages` and deleting another tool's comment are
        `Refused`.
      - **Privacy:** the plugin never receives the user's name (authored
        marks report a role, `<<name>>` stays literal).
      - **Events:**
        - a plugin isn't sent its own changes;
        - depth-2 echoes stop;
        - an undo-fighting fixture's edits after an undo are refused
          with `edit-refused`;
        - coalesced events carry the union of pages.
      - **Versions:**
        - amount-crossref refuses cached ids after a reopen;
        - a plugin declaring a newer `edit-schema` minor is refused at
          load.
      - **Assets:** an uploaded asset becomes a page-stamp mark.
      - **Build:** exactly one bindgen invocation remains.

### Lint ledgers

**Clippy `disallowed-methods`** lives in per-crate `clippy.toml` files
for sheaf-doc, sheaf-ops, sheaf-render and sheaf-app. Each ban lands in
the slice that removes its last user. Test code is allowed through
`#![cfg_attr(test, allow(clippy::disallowed_methods))]`. Two pieces of
test code build without `cfg(test)` under CI's
`cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets` and get a module-level
`#[allow]` too: `forms/fixture.rs` (the `fixtures` feature other crates'
tests enable) and `examples/roundtrip.rs`. Both bans landed in slice 19;
an integration test is a crate of its own, so each one that uses a
banned method carries its own `#![allow]` (slice 19's notes list them).

| Ban | Lands | Last users removed |
|---|---|---|
| `lopdf::content::Content::{decode, encode}`, `lopdf::Document::{get_page_content, change_page_content, add_page_contents}` | 19 (landed) | `stamps::strip`'s round trip (6; `stamps::strip` deleted 17), `forms::check`'s `da_font` (forms/check.rs:760–761, 6), stamp_lib.rs's page-to-form (stamp_lib.rs:408, 6), `watermark::install` and `read` (16, deleted), `flatten_annots` (19) |
| `std::env::temp_dir` (non-test) | 19 (landed) | the recovery temp primary (docview.rs:1024, 9), the layers panel (3; the decrypted in-memory copy that replaced its temp file went in 13, which lands no ban: the print and export temp files remain), the print and export temp files (14, deleted: print sends its job to CUPS and GDI from memory, and export's flatten already read its print file from memory, so 14 lands no ban either), the generated cache (19). Three legitimate uses get an `#[allow]` with a reason: `recent.rs`'s path check; the attachments panel's folder for opened attachments (the one user-requested file; M11 slice 1 deletes it at close); and the plugin installer's archive folder (`install_archive`, plugins.rs:529), which holds no document content and is removed after the install. |
| — | never | sheaf-instance's `socket_path` fallback (no `clippy.toml` there) |

## M10 slices 6+ on the new API

M10 resumes on `main` after **all** of M10.5 (slices 1–20; proposal 11).
Slice 20 rewrites `m10.md`'s slices to match this list.

- **6, text appearances.** A pure
  `appearance::text(field, widget, display, &FormDoc, font) -> FormRes`
  on ContentWriter and `Font`. It covers the `/DA` parser; WinAnsi,
  MacRoman and `/Differences` encoders as `Font`s; `/DR` handles from
  `SourceForm`; `/MK /R`; `WidgetProps.border`; and `/Tx BMC` with a
  clip. The emitter calls it for widgets whose appearance digest
  changed, and so does the realizer, so the screen equals the file. The
  overlay-or-pictures spike is settled.
- **7, the Unicode fallback.** `Res::Font(Fallback)`: a GID-preserving
  Noto Type0 subset, late-bound per materialization or overlay. An
  Append adds a new subset object when new glyphs appear. NFC, MaxLen by
  grapheme and the refusal live in `SetFieldValues`' lowering. It ends
  the `'?'` interim in marks and generators.
- **8, buttons, radios and choices.** Pure generators. Group `/AS`
  semantics are lowering rules of `SetFieldValues`.
- **9, saving values. It shrinks to one commit.**
  `SetFieldValues { values (by FieldId or full name), display, calculated }`
  lowers to `Put Field`/`Put Annot`. Both strategies, recovery and
  identity after a save already exist, so 9a's re-binding is deleted.
  The save rules are not per-writer code:
  - a replaced value is REPLACES_TEXT, so a Rewrite;
  - filling an empty field appends, keeping UR3 within its
    TransformParams;
  - earlier-revision values are a `SourceForm` fact that forces a
    Rewrite on the first form change;
  - XFA (tooltips to `/TU`, after `XfaHoldsValues`), `/UR3` and SigFlags
    are `rules::plan` transforms;
  - signed and certified files go through §9.3's asks, with "Append
    anyway";
  - lowering refuses edits to fields locked by a known signature
    (FieldMDP), and to signed fields themselves, with the
    `EditError::Locked { field }` this slice adds;
  - the encryption notice is gone, because encryption is kept.

  Check: a fill on a signed hybrid fixture offers "Append anyway" and
  doesn't rewrite unasked.
- **10, focus, keys and Tab order.** Hit tests on PageSpace widgets in
  `page_annots` order. **It adds `KeyPatch` with symbolic `PatchValue`s,
  and `PageDef.keys` for `/Tabs`, with a classify role row (`/Tabs` →
  FIELD_TREE, OTHER).** The `/S` order comes from kept.rs's structure
  walker over source facts. Pending UI commits flush before any plugin
  call.
- **11, the field editor. It adds `GroupKind::Typing`:** one group per
  focus session, each commit a `SetFieldValues` amend. The editor's text
  stays uncommitted, with its own Ctrl+Z. `ViewInputs` hides the focused
  widget from the realization while the editor draws.
- **12, drawing changed fields.** It becomes "marks drawn by PDFium":
  switch to `MarkDraw::ByEngine`; delete the GPUI mark painter
  (`annot_elements`), `stamp_preview.rs` and the tape pictures; and
  decide FFLDraw (recommended: appearances only, once every changed
  field has an `/AP`).
- **13, buttons and Clear Form.** `ResetFields` as one Tx. Hide is
  `PatchWidgets { flags }`.
- **14, the Fields panel, and values in search.** Model reads;
  `TextOpts { fields: true }` merges widget display text, for the app.
- **15, flatten.** `FlattenFields` shares `FlattenAnnotations`'
  machinery:
  - ensure appearances;
  - draw printable widgets by `/AS`, with no first-state fallback, into
    a `Placements` layer of `FormRef::Pinned`;
  - remove widgets through `widget.field`;
  - empty the `FormDoc`;
  - pass `removed_annots` to `keep_only`.

  **It adds `FormBring::Flatten`** for Insert and Combine, and
  `SignatureNotValidHere` fields may flatten there. Also
  `sheaf form flatten`.
- **16–17, form data.** FDF, XFDF, CSV, text and JSON importers produce
  `SetFieldValues` batches by name, resolved through calculation and
  committed `Validate`. Exporters are queries.
- **18, AF functions.** Pure Rust, in the host's resolve stage. They
  produce display and calculated values plus their decision reads.
- **19–22, scripts. They add `Actor::FormScript` and
  `PageSource::Template`** (spawning pages from templates).
  `FormsHost::resolve(&Snapshot, Vec<Op>) -> (Vec<Op>, reads)` runs on
  the formjs worker, then commits `Validate` into the user's Typing
  group. The sandbox syncs on `ChangeSet.fields` for transitions not
  made by `FormScript`. Replay never runs scripts, and a save waits for
  a running cascade's group.
- **23–26, Prepare Form.** `AddField`, `AddWidget`, `PatchFields`,
  `PatchWidgets`, `MoveWidgets`, `DeleteFields`, `DeleteWidgets`,
  `RenameField`, `MoveField`, `SetTabOrder` and `SetCalculationOrder`,
  over existing keys. **They add `FieldNode.patch`, widget patches
  (`PatchValue`) and role rows** (removing `/AA` or `/JS` → REMOVES;
  `/AP` on a widget → FILL). Multi-select is one Tx with locals.
  Deleting is REMOVES, so a Rewrite. Copies are untagged until M14.
- **27–28, detection.** Queries over the TextService and the pool.
  Accepting the proposals is one Tx.
- **29, the plugin API.** Field ops join the JSON `Op` as `Cap::Plugin`,
  with no WIT bump. Field reads are new WIT functions in
  `sheaf:plugin@0.5.0`, behind a manifest `fields` capability that also
  unlocks widgets in `annotations()`, `TextOpts { fields }` and
  `FormDraw::Appearances` for renders. Without it, plugin renders use
  `FormDraw::Redacted`.

**Edits to `m10.md`'s proposals and slices** (slice 20):
- proposal 8: delete its "Re-bound after a save" bullet and the dirty
  tracking of saved values;
- proposal 10: replace the on-screen slot-hiding bullet with
  `ViewInputs`;
- proposal 7's "every way out": point it at `rules::plan` plus the
  export preflight;
- proposal 18: becomes `FlattenFields`/`FlattenAnnotations`;
- proposal 23: renumbered to 0.5, with no 0.3 or 0.4 serving;
- slice 9: drop 9a's re-binding;
- slice 11: the Typing group;
- slice 12: "marks drawn by PDFium";
- slice 15: `PinnedAp`;
- slice 29: 0.5 with `fields`, with no 0.3 or 0.4 serving; `m11.md`'s
  plugin API becomes 0.6; `docs/forms.md` drops "encryption until M11"
  from the save rules (m10.md:1817–1834).

    (slice 17), and the lexical splice in `content/` (slices 6 and 16)

    splice, `Balance`, TextBag; §13), adds `ContentStack.rewrite` and
    `Static::Ops`, and lowers redaction as definitions evaluated at emit
    (§20).
  - **The leak check** (its proposal 8) runs over the output, not
    DocState (§20).
  - **Applying redactions** is a `Transform` on an `ExportTx`, so
    plugins can't apply them by type; "every way out asks first" is the

  - **Its plugin API bump** (proposal 15) becomes 0.6, since M10 takes

  - **Its proposal 11** (no plaintext copies on disk) is mostly met
    here: generated sources are memory blobs, and the sidecar is
    encrypted.
  - **New AES-256 encryption** (V5, R6) writes `/Length 256` in
    `/Encrypt`, in M11's encryption code or as a `vendor/lopdf` patch:
    lopdf's `Document::encrypt` leaves it out, and poppler 26.01 then
    garbles every stream. Its tests check new AES-256 output with
    poppler (M10.5 slice 2's notes).
- **[`agent.md`](agent.md):**
  - "Submit edits" (agent.md:129): sheaf-edit `Op` JSON in a versioned
    envelope, through `Document::plan(actor, base, ops) -> PlanHandle`
    and `commit(plan)`, so the approval card commits exactly what it
    showed (§20).
  - "Versions keep reads and writes honest" (:133–136): version tokens
    are `{ instance, version }`; the agent's reads are decision reads
    kept per MCP session, and it commits `Validate`, so a user edit
    elsewhere doesn't refuse it and it can write during OCR; plans
    expire on conflict.
  - The History row (:127): `VersionView` with stored lines, not
    `describe.rs` at read time; `Document::edge`'s source list is gone.
  - The author "Claude for GE" (:166–168): `Actor::Agent` is session
    provenance; nothing goes into the file except a mark's `/T`, which
    the host sets.
  - "Revert this turn" (:169–171): a revert of the turn's versions; a
    jump only when nothing came after the turn.
  - Its own transport and approval UI, not the sheaf-instance socket
    (proposal 36); semantic ops only at first (decision 6); field values
    behind its per-document consent.
- **[`file-contention.md`](file-contention.md):**
  - §3 Merge (file-contention.md:147–163): a version's steps now hold
    resolved ops and prims with before-values, so a merge applies them
    onto the other person's version by value (`Validate`) or re-lowers
    the resolved ops (`Relower`), and conflicts are explicit. Marks
    still map by `/NM`. Sheaf marks' `/NM` embeds the `AnnotId`, so it
    is unique per document (duplicates get fresh ids); others' `/NM` is
    unique per page only. `Document::edge`'s source list is gone, since
    sources are content-addressed.
  - "Someone else saved" is detected by the `FileStamp` re-check before
    every write, which asks Save As…, Overwrite or Cancel (proposal 33).
- **Plugin docs:**

## Risks

- **Scope.** The plan is 20 slices, about 68 points, with M10 paused
  throughout.
  - *Mitigations:* slices 1–4 bring value on their own (exact replay,
    measured risks, the Store, one open). M10's slices 6–9 shrink by
    about one slice (the spike, the re-binding and the per-writer save
    rules go).
- **The lazy reader must be exact** on damaged, hybrid, encrypted and
  hostile files.
  - *Mitigations:* corpus-wide lazy-against-eager equality, the eager
    fallback, fuzzing and one `Limits`.
- **Overlays on real files are unmeasured.** That covers PDFium with
  in-memory append sections on encrypted, xref-stream, hybrid,
  linearized, damaged and leading-junk bases, and widgets after a page
  is replaced in place.
  - *Mitigation:* slice 2's written criteria, with fallbacks (a
    decrypted image per source, standalone groups) decided before any
    slice depends on them.
- **The change to f64 reals** touches about 56 sites and may shift
  output formatting.
  - *Mitigation:* the save suites and a corpus round trip in slice 3.
- **The legacy projection and the adapted `rebase_to_saved`** (slice 8)
  feed the old writers while records exist.
  - *Mitigations:* they live for one slice only and cross no coordinate
    or appearance change; the replay proptest and every save suite run
    through them; both are deleted in slice 9.
- **No-rebase saves and in-place Appends** depend on the `SaveRecord`
  (`present`, owned roots, `tree`, stamps) being right across
  alternating Append, Rewrite, Save As and recovery. A mistake writes a
  broken file.
  - *Mitigations:* the Append ≡ Rewrite property in the default run, the
    delete/save/undo/save/reopen chain, `qpdf --check`, the journal, and
    stamp re-checks before every write.
- **False positives in the removal check** can force rewrites, or asks
  on signed files.
  - *Mitigations:* derived objects are judged on their inputs (exact);
    decoding goes through ToUnicode; subsets are GID-preserving; the
    corpus run counts vetoes per class.
  - *Remaining exposure:* vector geometry is out of scope, and an
    unknown encoding errs toward a Rewrite.
- **Value-validated commits plus `Relower`** are new concurrency
  machinery.
  - *Mitigations:* the commit rule is one function with a property test
    (a random Tx, a concurrent commit and an amend, then commit: the
    result is either a Conflict or a state containing both changes, and
    replay equals the snapshot), plus an explicit test for each policy
    row.
- **Live page tokens** rely on deterministic layout. A font or layout
  code change between sessions turns a reopen-and-reorder into a
  re-layout of every covered page. It still appends as `LIVE_REDRAW`,
  but it surprises.
  - *Mitigation:* the byte-determinism test and the planner's
    explanation. Proposal 8 lets Greg choose frozen tokens instead.
- **`keep_only` and the Rewrite path** still parse every reachable dict
  structurally, and 500 MB scans are unmeasured until slice 2.
  - *Mitigation:* slice 9's Rewrite gate. The port to a symbolic graph
    happens only if that gate fails.
- **The PageSpace switch** (slice 5) touches every gesture, drawing and
  hit-test site.
  - *Mitigations:* the `to_view ∘ from_view` property, and selftests on
    rotated, cropped pages.
- **Strict removal** sends more saves down the Rewrite path and asks
  more often on signed files.
  - *Mitigations:* raw passthrough keeps rewrites near I/O speed,
    "Append anyway" covers removals and form transforms, and the gate
    records Rewrite time.
- **The DocMDP, FieldMDP and UR3 mapping** rests on ISO 32000 and vendor
  docs.
  - *Mitigation:* warnings stay conservative until the Acrobat
    cross-check (Asks).
- **Interop is inferred.** Acrobat's handling of our named-property
  `/Artifact` blocks, and the `/PieceInfo` rule for its own, need an
  Acrobat round trip (slices 16 and 17).
- **Engine memory.** Each group engine parses its own xref and object
  cache over the same base.
  - *Mitigations:* LRU by measured bytes, a separate background budget,
    and geometry-only pages that need no overlay if spike C passes.
- **JSON ops over WIT** lose compile-time typing for non-Rust plugins.
  - *Mitigations:* `deny_unknown_fields`, per-kind refs with clear
    errors, the published schema and the `edit-schema` manifest check.
- **The `/SheafAnnot` v2 digest** must be computed identically on write
  and on read.
  - *Mitigations:* the canonical form, and a round-trip test for every
    mark kind, by both strategies and after a re-serialization by
    another tool.
- **Sources stay alive for the session.** Opening a huge file, deleting
  most of it and continuing keeps the whole file in memory until the
  document is closed.
  - *Accepted, and documented.*

## Not in M10.5

- **The semantic interpreter, glyph boxes, descriptors, removal
  transforms, a hard crop, the leak check:** M11.
- **The security dialog, new encryption, a permissions UI, the
  certificate refusal, `Key::Security`:** M11. (The serializer's
  encryption is here.)
- **Signing, reservations, byte-range holes, a diff per revision,
  `SigClass` SIGN and LTV, DSS:** M12.
- **Object editing, link bodies, key patches for annotations,
  `Source::users`:** M13. (The `KeyPatch` type lands in M10 slice 10.)
- **Object streams in written files, structure modeling, tagging copies,
  an embedded-font policy, PDF/A conversion, Save Optimized:** M14.
- **Batch steps, `BatesStart::Continue`, `PageSel::{Label, Matches}`:**
  M15.
- **The agent:** its transport, approval UI, `Actor::Agent` and plan
  handles are its own milestone.
- **`GroupKind::Typing`, `Actor::FormScript`, `PageSource::Template`,
  `FormBring::Flatten`, field ops, `FormDraw::Redacted`:** M10 slices
  11, 15, 19–22 and 29.
- **Joining an existing form instance on insert (`FormBring::Join`):**
  when a producer appears.
- **Three-way merges of ordered keys:** not planned; `Relower` covers
  it.
- **Persisted history, merge, OT or CRDTs:** not planned. Steps are
  serde-capable.
- **hayro as an engine:** not planned; an oracle only.
- **Shrinking `/SheafAnnot` to the keys PDF can't hold:** a follow-up.
- **The stamp library in the edit API:** not planned (proposal 29).
- **Linearization, and a balanced re-tree on Append:** later, if corpus
  tests ask for them.

## Slice notes

1. Done. History stores what each edit changed, as prims with the values
   they replaced, and rebuilds a trimmed version from them, checked,
   without running an edit again; the retired-symbols ledger starts.
   - **`prim.rs`:** `Key` (the nine transitional keys), `Val`
     (`Field(Box<Field>)`), `Prim { key, before, after }` and
     `Mismatch { key }`. `same()` is `ptr_eq` (or `Arc::ptr_eq`) first,
     then `==`. `DocState::get` and `DocState::set` are one exhaustive
     match on `Key` each, and `DocState::apply` checks the before-value
     and leaves the state alone on a mismatch.
   - **`Rec`, the recording context:** reads through `Deref`, writes only
     through `put`, and `finish()` gives the prims in key order, without a
     slot that ended as it started. `compute(&self, rec, edit)` and its
     helpers (`take_in_fields`, `copy_fields`, `bring_fields`,
     `import_marks`) write only through it. `Step` is
     `{ edit, line, prims: Arc<[Prim]> }`.
   - **Coalescing** (`coalesce`), at a batch's commit and at an amend:
     each key's net prim, from the first before to the last after, goes on
     the last step that wrote the key, and a prim that nets to nothing is
     dropped. A no-op is an empty prim list: `apply`, `apply_batch` and
     `apply_in_job` push only with prims, and the three whole-state
     comparisons are gone. `DocState` derives `PartialEq` only under
     `cfg(test)`.
   - **Checked replay:** `replay(id)` starts from the nearest ancestor
     that kept a state and applies every step's prims on the way, oldest
     first. A `Mismatch` is logged with its key and becomes
     `Damaged { version }` ("History is damaged at version N").
     `ensure_state` marks the version damaged (`Version.damaged`,
     `VersionView.damaged`), logs, and panics in debug builds. `undo` and
     `redo` return `Result<Option<&str>, Damaged>` (`Ok(None)`: nothing to
     undo or redo); `jump` passes `Damaged` up. The History panel shows
     the error as a damaged version's meta line, in `theme::ERROR`, and
     the app's undo, redo and jump say so in a notice.
   - **One `IdAlloc`** (`page`, `outline`, `field` as `AtomicU64`,
     `fields_from` by `fetch_max`) replaces `rng`, `next_page`,
     `next_outline`, `next_field`, `Ids` and the reseed per step. Mark ids
     come from `fastrand` below 2^53. A replay draws nothing.
   - **Stored lines:** `Document::step` runs `describe(&edit, &state)`
     against the state before the edit, and `view()` reads `Step.line`.
     describe's `Option<&DocState>` and its count fallback for a trimmed
     parent are gone; `pages_text` makes one pass over the pages.
   - **Immutable versions:** `replace(old, v)` mints a new id for `v` and
     puts it in `old`'s place: among the parent's children and in its
     `redo_to`, as its children's parent, and as the root, cursor or saved
     version. `apply_in_job`'s amend and `rebase_to_saved` both go through
     it. An amend that nets to nothing removes the version and the cursor
     goes back to the parent.
   - **Accounting:** `Version.snapshot_bytes` and `step_bytes`, computed at
     push, at amend and at save by `accounting(steps, state)`.
     `step_bytes` is each step's `size_of::<Step>()` with its edit's and
     line's heap, plus each prim's `size_of::<Prim>()` and its
     after-value's heap, an `Arc` (text layer, header/footer) once per
     version by pointer. `snapshot_bytes` is `size_of::<DocState>()` plus,
     for each per-page or per-field map the version changed,
     `path_copies(touched, len, fanout)`: at depth l, min(touched,
     fanout^l) nodes of fanout entries, so k slots never count more than
     the map. Whole-value keys add nothing (their values are the steps').
     `HeapSize` (prim.rs) estimates what a value holds beyond its
     `size_of`, with exhaustive matches over `Val`, `Edit` and `AnnotKind`.
     `HistoryStats` has `snapshot_bytes: Vec<usize>` and
     `step_bytes: usize`; `MemoryBudget` drops snapshots against the total
     but subtracts only snapshot bytes. `marginal` is gone.
   - **The page splice** (`splice`: one `split_off`, an `extend`, one
     `append`) replaces the per-page `Vector::insert` loops in MovePages,
     InsertPages, ReplacePages' extra pages and OutlineMove's span.
   - **The ledger** (`crates/sheaf-doc/tests/retired.rs`): `RETIRED` rows
     (a path from the crate root, and the slice) and `QUALIFIED_ONLY`
     (the plan's `Mode`, `Step`, `PageRef`, `LabelSpec`, `Widget`, and
     `ids`, `rng`, `next_page`, `next_outline`, `next_field`). Every `.rs`
     under `crates/` but not under a `target` is parsed with `syn`; a
     file's module comes from its path below its package (the nearest
     `Cargo.toml`), and inline `mod`s nest. A row fails on a definition
     at its path (an item; an impl's or trait's item, a field or a
     variant as `Type::name`); on a path, in code or a `use`, that holds
     the row's last two segments in a row after a leading `crate`,
     `self`, `super` or `sheaf_*`; and, unless the last segment is
     qualified-only, on that name as a method, a call's callee, a type, a
     struct literal's or pattern's path, or a field (accessed, in a
     literal or in a pattern). A local variable is never a hit. Macro
     bodies count where they parse as comma-separated expressions. Each
     hit prints as `file:line: row (retired in slice n)`. Slice 1's rows:
     `model::Ids`, `model::Step::ids`, `model::Document::{replay_step,
     rng, next_page, next_outline, next_field, fresh_page_id,
     fresh_outline_id, marginal}`, `model::Version::marginal_bytes` and
     `history::HistoryStats::marginal_bytes`.
   - **Docs:** `docs/document-model.md`'s "Undo/redo" section describes
     versions, steps and prims, no-ops, checked replay, immutable
     VersionIds, `IdAlloc`, stored lines and the save pins, with the
     costs measured below; the Document sketch is a tree of versions with
     a `VersionId` cursor (bug 30); the Decisions bullet on
     `HistoryStats` and the Text layers "Coalesced undo" bullet are
     current.

   Deviations from the plan:
   - **The ledger is `crates/sheaf-doc/tests/retired.rs`,** sheaf-doc's
     first integration test, walking `CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR/../../crates`:
     the root `Cargo.toml` is a virtual manifest, so a root `tests/`
     builds nothing. Slice 2's `tests/gate_7k.rs` has the same problem.
     It needs `proc-macro2`'s `span-locations` beside `syn` (both
     dev-dependencies) for the hits' lines.
   - **The ledger matches a run of the row's last two segments anywhere
     in a path,** not only at its end, so `incremental::Mode::Append`
     hits the row `incremental::Mode` (slice 9's). Trait items, pattern
     field names and macro bodies are matched too; the plan names none of
     them, and without them `assert_eq!(d.marginal(), ..)` or
     `let Version { marginal_bytes, .. }` would pass.
   - **The ledger reads an `include!`d file as the module of its own
     path:** sheaf-plugin's `api/shared.rs`, `v02.rs` and `v03.rs` are
     `api::shared` and so on, not the modules that include them. Slice
     20's rows for them must use those paths.
   - **`Ids`'s fields have no rows of their own:** they can't be defined
     without `model::Ids`, which has one. No other named symbol went in
     steps 1–6; the in-place amend, describe's `Option` parameter and the
     parent lookup in `view()` were code inside functions.
   - **The bench needed fixes the slice's bullets don't list:** `splice`
     (the reorder was 262 ms, 189 ms of it the per-page insert loop) and
     a one-pass `pages_text` (describe of 3,500 ids was 24 ms, an
     `index_of` per id), required once describe runs at apply.
     `pages_text` keeps a sorted, deduplicated Vec and `binary_search`
     rather than a HashSet: faster at every size measured at 7,000 pages
     (one id: 35–48 µs against 142–196 µs; 3,500 ids: 172–175 µs against
     276–281 µs). A list naming a page twice now reads as its pages; the
     count stays for an unknown id (bug 11), more than 4 runs and an
     empty list, and counts each page once.
   - **Prims are stored per step, coalesced across the version:** §8.1
     keeps prims on the Step and §6.2 coalesces at commit, so each key's
     net prim goes on the last step that wrote it. Every step keeps its
     edit and line, with or without prims. Each key is then in one prim
     per version, so the order of replay doesn't matter, and a 7,000-op
     batch stores one Pages value, not 7,000. Coalescing runs at amend
     too (§6.2), so a job's version can net to nothing.
   - **`Mismatch { key }` and `Damaged { version }`:** `DocState::apply`
     returns the first, as §6.2 has it; the history-level error carries
     the version and becomes `EditError::Mismatch { version }` in slice
     11. `DocState::set` returns `Result<(), Mismatch>` too, so the check
     that a value fits its key is in the one match; `Rec::put` treats a
     misfit as a bug in `compute` and panics.
   - **Five kinds have no no-op:** OutlineInsert, OutlineDelete,
     AnnotAdd, AnnotDelete and ConnectorAdd always make or remove
     something, or fail. "Each kind's no-op pushes nothing" covers the
     other 16; the x → y → x batches (rotate, labels, header, move) are in
     `a_batch_that_puts_things_back_pushes_nothing`.
   - **`undo` and `redo` return `Result<Option<&str>, Damaged>`;** the
     `Option<ChangeSet>` is slice 12's. Tests that undid to check
     something was undone still check it (`.unwrap().unwrap()`, or
     `Ok(Some(..))`).
   - **`IdAlloc` has atomics but no `Arc`:** nothing else owns it until
     slice 11's `LowerCx`. `compute` takes `&self`.
   - **A Field prim's values are copies** (`Val::Field(Box<Field>)`):
     `DocState.fields` holds fields by value until slice 8. Boxed, or
     clippy's `large_enum_variant` fires. Its snapshot copy is counted in
     `snapshot_bytes` too.
   - **`rebase_to_saved` gets a new id under the same parent,** and its
     steps' prims still lead to the state before the save, so it's never
     replayed: `keeps_snapshot` pins every version with saves, and (a fix
     the plan doesn't list) the children of one. A child made from the
     cursor before a save has prims whose before-values are the pre-save
     state, so undo, save, then redo mismatched once replay was checked
     (`replay_step` used to recompute another state silently, bug 6).
     `rebase_to_saved` now rebuilds the cursor's children's states before
     re-expressing it. A save at the opened version replaces the root's
     id. The property test saves too; only its fold from the root skips a
     version with a save on its path, since that fold mismatches across a
     save.
   - **`set_initial_*` (through `opened_state_mut`) still change the
     opened version's state in place** before the first edit: the one
     exception to immutable versions until slice 4 deletes them.
   - **Two parts of §8.4's amend rule come now:** the guard gains
     `saves.is_empty()` (a replaced id mustn't keep save notes for content
     it doesn't have; `saved != cursor` alone allowed it) and
     `parent.is_some()` (found in review: pruning past `MAX_VERSIONS` can
     make the job's version the root, as after 999 edits, a save at the
     tip, a jump back to the opened version and an OCR batch; the next
     batch then panicked on the missing parent, in release too), and an
     amend that nets to nothing removes the version. The parent becomes
     the cursor without a replay (`p.state.get_or_insert(state)`, the
     state just computed, equal to the parent's by value), and its
     `redo_to` is cleared if it named the removed version. A no-op job
     batch no longer relabels the version or adds a step to it.
   - **An amend moves `unlogged_sources` into the new version** (found
     here): an amend left a source `add_source` registered for the next
     version, though `add_source` says the next version records it.
   - **`CommentsDelete` writes `RemovedOf(page)` only when a name is new**
     (found here): names that were all deleted already, or none, put
     `Some(empty)` over `None`, pushing a version and marking the page
     dirty.
   - **Accounting beyond the plan's formula:** `path_copies` shares the
     nodes near the root (min(touched, fanout^l) a level, not touched ×
     depth), or an OCR job over 1,000 pages would count about 2.3 MB
     against a map of about 25 KB; fanout is im's own, 32 for HashMap and
     64 for OrdMap (`fields`), not 32 for all. `rebase_to_saved`
     recomputes its version's `snapshot_bytes`, since the pages and
     fields it re-expresses are new allocations no prim shares.
     `Edit::SetTextLayers` counts only its Vec's buffer (its Arcs are its
     prims'), a small under-count when a later step of the job takes that
     prim back. `AnnotKind` has 25 variants, not 26.
   - **A whole-value prim over-counts** (found in review, documented, not
     fixed): a Pages, Outline or Labels prim counts its whole value,
     walking it, though im shares all but the changed path with the
     parent's, so `step_bytes` isn't the plan's "uniquely retained" bytes
     for those keys: 168,740 bytes for a one-page rotate at 7,000 pages,
     375,627 for renaming one bookmark of 2,000. About 690 such renames
     put the steps alone over 256 MB, and `MemoryBudget`, which can only
     subtract snapshot bytes, then drops every snapshot it may on each
     trim (undo still works, replaying from the nearest kept one).
     Counting the changed chunks would be transitional code for keys
     slice 8 deletes, so `docs/document-model.md` and `accounting` say
     so instead.
   - **`HistoryStats.undone_source_bytes` stays 0** (slice 3), and
     `Edit` payloads don't count source bytes.
   - **The bench is an ignored sheaf-doc test,**
     `history_at_7k_pages_and_20k_marks`, run with `--release`: the gate
     harness comes in slice 2. Medians over 21 AnnotAdds and 5 reorders.
   - **The app:** `DocView::refresh_history()` clears the History panel's
     row cache on a damaged undo, redo or jump, since its key
     `(version, dirty)` doesn't change when a version is found damaged. A
     failed jump says "Can't go there: History is damaged at version N".
     The panel keys `expanded` and `open_branches` by VersionId, so an
     expanded row collapses when an amend or a save replaces its version;
     accepted.
   - **Tests replaced:** `replaying_the_log_rebuilds_every_version` (7
     kinds) by the property test, and `noop_edit_adds_no_version` by the
     no-op table's RotatePages row. `marginal_counts_layer_bytes` became
     `history_counts_the_layer_a_step_holds`.
   - **The property test's runs:** a job action sends 1–3 batches with
     one job (a new one 1 time in 4), half of them SetTextLayers or
     ClearTextLayers, so 64 runs give about 69 amends and 2 jobs that net
     to nothing. A save action (found in review: the save path changed
     most and had one fixed scenario) calls `rebase_to_saved` and records
     the version it makes; versions whose path from the root has a save
     skip the fold from the root but not the jump, and the "snapshots
     were dropped" check needs a run without saves. Inserted and
     replacing ranges are at most 4 pages: a saved file has all the
     document's pages, and inserting all of them doubled it each time (a
     2,600-action run reached 3.5 million pages). Taking out
     `rebase_to_saved`'s rebuild of the cursor's children fails the 4,096
     cases (not always the 64); taking out either save pin in
     `keeps_snapshot` fails the 64.
     `prims_rebuild_every_version_past_max_versions` is one seeded run of
     2,600 actions with no jumps (with them, pruning only ever takes
     branches) that moves the root forward past `MAX_VERSIONS`, with
     saves on the way. Each run seeds `fastrand` (mark ids), and the
     builder never iterates im's HashMaps, so a failure reproduces.
     `a_run_applies_every_kind` counts a kind only when its edit made a
     version. Beyond the plan, the runs check that verification's replays
     and jumps draw no ids (the `IdAlloc` counters are unchanged), and
     each jump follows a `trim()`, so it's a real replay. Making
     `coalesce` keep each step's own before-value fails the 64 cases (a
     seed for it is in `proptest-regressions/model/history_tests.txt`;
     it still fails it with the save action, and shrinks to one batch).
   - CI needed no change: `cargo test --workspace` runs the ledger.

   Measured (release, 7,000 pages, 20,000 marks, `default_policy`):
   - **AnnotAdd:** 1.1 ms before, 0.69–0.70 ms after (median; limit

2. Done. The overlay design is measured, and the five numbers slice 13
   builds on are set: encrypted sections (A) pass, overlays on real files
   (B) pass on every class but damaged bases (which realize standalone by
   design), render-time crops (C) fail, and GROUP is 128 pages with
   scoped group sections, the screen's LRU 6 group engines in 96 MB, the
   background budget 2 engines in 32 MB, and the thumbnail fill rate
   310 pages/s. The planning scripts, the heavy and scanned 7k
   generators and the 7k gate harness with today's baselines are
   committed; the spike code is deleted.
   - **`bench/`:** `gen.py` makes the fixtures
     (`gen.py synthetic|heavy|scanned N out.pdf`, through argparse
     subcommands, written to `out.pdf.<pid>.tmp` and moved into place, so
     a killed run leaves no partial file and two runs share no temporary
     file). `bench.py`, `real.py`, `warm.py`
     and `form.py` time PDFium through ctypes, with the libpdfium to time
     as their first argument, and share `pdfium.py`'s bindings. Each
     docstring says what it measures and what the planning run measured.
     `pool-sample.txt` is the planning sample, corpus-relative, in its
     original order: 400 of the corpus's 1,935 pool PDFs of 4 MB or more
     (4.2–5.0 MB, up to 1,050 pages), plus `forms/safedocs/0174624.pdf`
     and `0043009.pdf`. `README.md` lists each file and fixture with its
     command, the corpus lookup and the harness command. Standard library
     only, run with `python3 -I` from the repo root; `real.py` finds the
     corpus as the tests do (`$SHEAF_CORPUS`, then `../pdf-corpus`) and
     says it skipped without one.
   - **The synthetic 7k** is byte-identical to the planning run's, so
     proposal 16's numbers re-run on the same input: 3,510,145 bytes,
     sha256
     `297917810fe2447c611d20bf8de377184cf641a122f49ab5357be5fd2008142c`
     (with `img_every` 1, 4,123,353 bytes,
     `4ee9f637d3c96a9bd515c67bfeb77762d7ec504a6a47288797486d60847dfd9a`).
   - **The heavy 7k** (`gen.py heavy N out.pdf [--font PATH]`): 70
     sections of 100 pages, each its own `/Pages` node under the root
     and its own embedded subset font (a simple `/TrueType` font,
     `/WinAnsiEncoding`, `/Widths`, a Flate `/FontFile2`, BaseFont like
     `AAAAAB+DejaVuSans`). Six section words in each heading vary the
     glyphs: the 70 subsets come in 58 glyf sizes. About 50 lines of
     Flate text a page and three annotations: a `/Link` to a page in
     another section (`/XYZ` or `/Fit`); a markup in turn `/Square`,
     `/Highlight` (with `/QuadPoints`) and `/Text`, each with `/AP /N`,
     `/NM`, `/T`, `/Contents`, `/M` and `/P`; and a merged field and
     widget, a `/Tx` whose `/AP /N` shows its `/V`, every tenth a check
     box with `/AS` and `/Yes` and `/Off` appearances. `/AcroForm` lists
     all 7,000 fields. One bookmark a section with 28 children,
     `/PageLabels` in three ranges, every non-stream object packed 100 to
     a Flate `/ObjStm`, one `/Type /XRef` stream and no table, under
     `%PDF-1.7`.
   - **The scanned 7k** (`gen.py scanned N out.pdf`): one image XObject a
     page, 1275 × 1650 8-bit DeviceGray, Flate, copied from a seeded pool
     of 32 pseudo-scans (white paper, speckled rows, word-shaped ink;
     about 70 KB a page), drawn by `q 612 0 0 792 0 0 cm /Im0 Do Q`. One
     flat `/Pages`, a classic xref, no text layer, streamed to disk.
   - **The gate harness,** `crates/sheaf-ops/tests/gate_7k.rs`: five
     ignored tests, run with
     `cargo test -p sheaf-ops --release --test gate_7k -- --ignored
     --nocapture --test-threads=1`.
     - `gates_on_the_synthetic_7k`, `_heavy_7k` and `_scanned_7k` find
       their fixture in `$SHEAF_GATE_DIR`, else `target/gate-7k/`, as
       `<kind>-7000.pdf`, and make one that is missing, older than

     - Each runs in two child processes of the test binary, the second
       for the flatten alone, and each child writes a file once its rows

       away from `--exact` can't pass with nothing run.
     - Each prints one table, a row per measurement: now, slice 2's

     - Times are medians, of 3 runs for whole-file work and 5 for the
       warm render. RSS calls glibc's `malloc_trim(0)`, writes 5 to

       edit as a `new_from_prev` delta: the base's xref kind, `/Prev`,
       `/ID` kept, `/Encrypt` repeated and every new object encrypted by
       `encrypt_object`; new objects numbered above `/Size`; on leading
       junk, the section built against `base[h..]`, so offsets count
       from the header (§11.7). The reference was lopdf's Full write of
       the same delta.
     - **The edit:** three pages (the first, middle and last) replaced
       in place: `/Contents` became `[q, originals…, Q + a filled block
       and Helvetica text]`, `/Resources` resolved through inheritance
       plus the text's font, and `/Annots` the page's own plus a Square
       with `/AP /N`, scaled to the page's visible box. Two pages left
       alone were compared too.
     - **Loading:** `Segments`, a `Read + Seek` over
       `[base Arc, section Arc]`, through pdfium-render's
       `load_pdf_from_reader` (`FPDF_LoadCustomDocument`).
     - **Comparing:** BGRA pixels at 1,024 px, exactly, two ways:
       appearances only (each annotation's print flag set to whether it
       shows, PDFium's flatten, then a render, as sheaf-render's
       `render_appearances` does), which decided the criteria, and live
       (`FPDF_FFLDraw`, as the page view draws). PNG pairs of every
       mismatch were kept. Corpus bases ran in child processes, 16 at a
       time with a 60 s cap, so a PDFium crash or hang cost one base;
       the built bases ran alone.
   - **Docs:** `docs/document-model.md` gains "Rendering edited pages:
     the spikes (M10.5 slice 2)" after "Saving" (it had no section on
     rendering edited pages): what an overlay is, how the spikes ran,
     each criterion and result, the fallback taken, the five verdicts
     with their rules, and what the spikes found. The history bench's
     reference in "Costs and how they're bounded" points at the harness.
     `bench/README.md` points at the section.

   Deviations from the plan:
   - **The harness is `crates/sheaf-ops/tests/gate_7k.rs`,** not
     `tests/gate_7k.rs`: the root `Cargo.toml` is a virtual manifest
     (slice 1's note), and sheaf-ops already depends on sheaf-doc and
     sheaf-render and has open and crop.
   - **The history bench moved into it** (slice 1's "left for slice
     2"). sheaf-doc's private helpers `src` and `square` became
     `SourceInfo` and `Annot` struct literals, and `history_tests.rs`
     lost the test, its `Duration`/`Instant` import and the module doc's
     "And, ignored, the timing at 7,000 pages." The 200-OCR-versions
     row is measurable today, model only, so it was added as a baseline
     without an assert.
   - **Baselines are consts in the harness,** printed beside each run
     with a ratio, and below, naming the machine. The plan didn't say
     where; slice 9 deletes today's writer, yet its gate is relative to
     it. Each is the median of three full runs: single runs differed.
   - **Each fixture test runs in processes of its own** (the test
     binary re-runs itself for that test, `--exact`, once for the edit
     rows and once for the flatten, with `SHEAF_GATE_FIXTURE_PROCESS`
     naming the file the child writes when done and `SHEAF_GATE_PART`
     the rows; the model-only tests stay in the parent). In one process
     the memory a fixture freed stayed resident and fragmented: the
     synthetic's ready peaked at 47 MB alone and at 160 MB after the
     heavy and scanned tests. With a process each, full and
     single-fixture runs agree within 1–2%. `malloc_trim(0)` before
     resetting `VmHWM` keeps a row from counting what earlier rows freed
     (the heavy's flatten started at 806 MB without it, 248 MB with).
     The flatten got its own process after review: behind the crop and
     Bates rows the heavy's started at 248–279 MB, and on the file
     opened again in the same process still at 240–293 MB (heap the
     edits fragmented, which `malloc_trim` can't return); in its own
     process it starts at the document as opened, 139 MB.
   - **The table has a gate column** beyond now, baseline and ratio,
     with the Gates table's threshold and the slice that asserts it.
     Render and crop print two lines each (cold and warm; total and the
     edit alone), and Rewrite prints its output size as a row of its
     own.
   - **Each RSS measurement prints two rows,** its peak and what it
     added to the RSS it started from, and both are baselines. The
     plan's "≤ 1.5× its RSS" for Rewrite is read as what the Rewrite
     adds: most of today's peak is the eagerly opened document, which
     slices 3 and 8 shrink, so a ratio of peaks would let the new writer
     use twice today's writer's own memory, and slice 9 deletes today's
     writer, so its share can't be measured again later. Slice 19's
     limit stays on the flatten's peak, as the Gates table words it.
   - **Rows time what the app does,** not only the sheaf-doc call: the
     incremental save writes the file (`save_to_path` over the copy the
     document was opened from, which `same_file` needs), crop opens a
     `RenderHandle` on its copy as page_insert.rs does and writes the
     copy each run (the generated cache is emptied first; `store` would
     otherwise read the old copy back and compare it), and Bates runs
     `set_header_footer`'s `strip_stamps` and `apply_batch`, which load
     every source with lopdf. A first version timed the bytes, the cache
     hit and the bare `SetHeaderFooter` (0.007 ms against < 50 ms).
   - **Gate rows with no counterpart today aren't in the harness:**
     realize + open + render an edited page, engines after 200 groups
     and the thumbnail strip (slice 13), the live-token reorder (17),
     and idle CPU (the app's, 12 and 13). The module doc names the slice
     that adds each.
   - **No rows in the retired ledger,** and no `cargo check` for deleted
     symbols: `crates/sheaf-doc/tests/retired.rs` walks `crates/` only,
     the spike code never entered `crates/` or git, and moving a test is
     not a retirement. Nothing under `crates/` referred to `bench/spike`.
   - **The scripts:** `bench/pdfium.py` is new (the four timing scripts
     repeated about 25 lines of ctypes declarations each; their timings
     are unchanged), and `bench/.gitignore` ignores `__pycache__/`.
     `bench.py` keeps the planning run's row letters (A load, with the
     size walk under it; B render; C text; D a concatenated section; E
     two segments; F a scratch PDF; G `GenerateContent`). `gen.py` lost
     a dead `leaves = []`, its local imports moved to the top (output
     byte-identical), it takes a subcommand, and it refuses N < 1, which
     made a broken file. Its summary line is now
     `<fixture>, N pages: B bytes in S s` and counts, for the synthetic
     too (it printed `3510145 bytes 7000 pages`). `real.py` reports files
     it couldn't read or PDFium couldn't load (none in the sample)
     instead of skipping them.
   - **A standard-library TrueType subsetter, not fontTools:** this
     machine has no fontTools, pikepdf or qpdf, and gen.py stays stdlib
     only. It keeps glyph ids, empties the glyphs a section doesn't use
     (following composites), and drops `fpgm`, `prep` and `cvt` and also
     `GDEF`, `GPOS`, `GSUB`, `MATH`, `kern`, `FFTM` and `gasp`, which a
     PDF never reads; `post` becomes format 3. Glyph instructions are
     stripped too, since without `fpgm` they would call functions that
     no longer exist. It reads a short or long `loca` and writes a long
     one. The subset tag is 0-based (section 1 is `AAAAAA+`) and the name
     is the font's PostScript name. A font it can't read exits 2 naming
     `--font`.
   - **The heavy 7k's bytes depend on the font,** by default
     `/usr/share/fonts/truetype/dejavu/DejaVuSans.ttf` (sha256
     `b4c632e3cdf9acc7f28758fb5a323c8524d7fc6660d46904d9b6cbe2809c419c`),
     so the harness only warns when its length differs. `/AcroForm /DR`
     has `/ZaDb` beside `/Helv`, for the check boxes' `/DA`. Bookmarks:
     every fifth section's entry is open, some children have `/C` or
     `/F`, and non-ASCII titles are UTF-16BE. Labels: roman for 12 pages,
     decimal from 1, and the last N/35 pages `A-1` on (no appendix under
     35 pages).
   - **The scanned 7k's images are Flate gray,** not JPEG or CCITT: gen.py
     can't depend on PIL, the only imaging library here. Its header is
     `%PDF-1.4`. Both new fixtures carry `/Info` and an `/ID` (the md5 of
     the fixture's name and N); the synthetic still has none.
   - **`IncrementalDocument` as planned, adjusted:**
     - lopdf's reader drops `/XRefStm` from the loaded trailer and
       `/Encrypt` from a decrypted document's, so `new_from_prev` clones
       neither. The spike removed both anyway, and a stale
       `/DecodeParms` an xref-stream base's trailer carries.
     - The synthetic base got an `/ID` before `Document::encrypt`, since
       RC4 and AES-128 keys depend on `/ID[0]`; the previous document was
       loaded with its password, since `IncrementalDocument` refuses an
       encrypted one; and the Full write took `/Encrypt` out of the
       trailer before `save_to`.
     - The AES-256 base got `/Length 256` in its `/Encrypt`, as Acrobat
       writes it; without it poppler can't read lopdf's AES-256 file at
       all (found below). PDFium and lopdf don't care.
     - New objects are numbered above the largest of `/Size` − 1,
       lopdf's `max_id` and the xref's highest entry (found below).
   - **Appearances only is a flatten, not `render_form_data(false)`:**
     with `FPDF_ANNOT` and no `FPDF_FFLDraw`, PDFium draws no widgets at
     all, form environment or not (checked on the heavy 7k's page 0), so
     a plain render leaves them out. The spikes flattened what shows, as
     `render_appearances` does, and compared live renders beside it;
     live ran first, since the flatten changes the loaded page.
   - **Checks the criteria don't name:** an edited page must render
     differently from the base (in at least one mode, since a widget over
     a whole page hides an edit live) and an untouched one identically,
     or a pass where neither side shows the edit would count; spike A's
     section must hold neither of the edit's strings in plain text (the
     Full write is checked to hold them); and where `pdftoppm` is
     installed, poppler renders spike A's overlay and Full write alike
     (PDF interoperability is a fixed constraint, and this found the
     AES-256 `/Length`).
   - **Spike A also ran on 50 encrypted corpus files:** inventory rows
     with `encrypted=1` and status ok, in file order, at most 15 an
     algorithm, stopping at 50 files (75 rows), each decrypted with the
     empty password.
   - **Spike B:**
     - Writer artifacts are separated per page: where overlay and Full
       write differ, the base is compared with lopdf's write of it with
       no edit, on that page and in that mode, and if those differ too
       the page is the writer's, not the overlay's.
     - Classes: classic table and xref stream are the newest section's
       kind (lopdf's `cross_reference_type`, the kind the section is
       written in); hybrid means `/XRefStm` in the bytes; linearized,
       `/Linearized` within 1,024 bytes of the header; damaged, lopdf's
       `xref_start` is 0 or lopdf and PDFium count different pages;
       encrypted, lopdf decrypted it with the empty password.
     - An untestable base (lopdf can't load it or write a section, or
       PDFium can't load the base) is listed and left out. If PDFium
       can't load or render the overlay, all its sampled pages count
       against the overlay; if the Full write fails, against the writer.
     - Memory was weighed on every base, not just the pool sample and
       the 7k fixtures; the cap's rule uses the pool sample's p99, and a
       class passes on memory if its p99 is within the cap.
     - Cold is the first render in a fresh engine, in a process that has
       already rendered the base once (PDFium's global fonts are
       loaded: the app is never cold); warm is the next render. Opens
       are medians of 5.
     - The synthetic and scanned 7k were compared, not only weighed, so
       slice 13's synthetic gate got an early read. The SafeDocs forms
       were drawn from 3,976, leaving out the one already in the pool
       sample. The sample already had 22 hybrid and 216 linearized
       files, so no pool picks were needed for those.
     - **A top-up run for damaged and leading junk,** 3 and 2 bases in
       the first run, mostly built: 90 pool files outside the sample, in
       inventory order, the first 50 with `%PDF-` past offset 0 and the
       first 50 whose `startxref` leads to no xref (by a scan of each
       file's head and tail; 10 are both), through spike B's driver with
       only those bases. The class rows are both runs' together. The
       review's reruns (this, the fill and the budget walks) rebuilt the
       spike from its sources outside the repo; `bench/spike/` stays
       gone.
   - **Spike C** compared two more edits, the crop with a 90° turn and
     the turn alone through today's rotate parameter, since §10.1's job
     transform carries rotation deltas too; the criterion was judged on
     all three. The matrix was solved to compose bit for bit in PDFium's
     f32 arithmetic (`CFX_Matrix`'s product as chromium/7881 computes
     it), nudging each translation by ulps; a plain f64 inverse is
     mostly an ulp off. The written page went through
     `FPDF_RenderPageBitmap` at the page view's bitmap size, not
     pdfium-render's matrix path, which scales differently.
     Appearances-only comparisons were re-solved against the flattened
     pages' boxes (PDFium's flatten moves inherited boxes, found below),
     and pages were reloaded after the flatten (pdfium-render's stale
     handle, found below). Failures were sorted into writer, flatten
     moved the box, widgets live, inexact matrix, edge rounding,
     annotations outside and rotation.
   - **The fallbacks taken:** C failed, so crops realize as overlays
     (§10.1). B failed on damaged bases only (the top-up below), which
     realize standalone, as §10.1 has them by design. A needs none.
   - **What the spikes found stays in these notes,** not in "Found while
     planning": that list is the bugs planning found, each with the slice
     that fixes it, and these are measurements and rules for later
     slices, listed under "Left for later slices" by the slice that uses
     each. The one for another milestone, lopdf's AES-256 `/Length`, went
     into "Changes to other plans → m11.md", and `todos/m11.md` waits for
     slice 20 as that section says.
   - **GROUP measures a scoped variant, a departure from §10.1:** the
     section's root `/Pages` lists only the group's pages and its
     AcroForm only the top-level fields with a widget on them. §10.1 has
     edited pages keep "their page index, AcroForm, OCProperties,
     inherited attributes and shared resources"; scoped, they keep the
     last three. In place no G fits the rule, because the heavy's engine
     loads all 7,000 fields. What scoping gives up, which slice 13 takes
     on (the docs list it too): the page tree is flattened, each page's
     `/Parent` still naming its own node, whose `/Kids` and `/Count`
     aren't rewritten (inherited keys resolve because PDFium walks
     `/Parent`; or write them out and re-parent, as §11.6 does for
     duplicates); `PageView.index` is the page's place in its group's
     engine, so whatever reads an edited page from its realization,
     §10.5's text included, goes through it; destinations into other
     groups resolve to no page in the engine (sheaf reads links from the
     file, not from engines); and a field whose widgets span groups is
     listed in each, with `/CO` and scripts blind to fields outside the
     group. Spike B gained a scoped pass and was re-run; its in-place
     results matched the first run's exactly. G was measured up to 256,
     so the rule's upper bound is measured; "near the base open" is
     within 0.5 ms, and an engine fits the cap with every page of its
     group previewed (the strip's state), not one.
   - **The LRU count counts group engines only, pinned ones included,**
     for both panes of a split window. §10.3 caps "others", the
     unpinned, by count, but a count read from what is visible sizes the
     pinned set, so the verdict caps them together: two groups a pane,
     two panes, two for the strip. That never closes a visible group's
     engine, and with one pane keeps the 2 groups last left. The first
     verdict, 4 engines in 64 MB, left out the split view; the fill and
     the budget walk were run again at 6 engines and 96 MB with two
     panes pinned. Each visible source's base engine is pinned and
     outside the count (and grows without bound, found below).
   - **The thumbnail fill rate is defined here,** since the plan doesn't
     define it; the review that added it said "the thumbnail strip fills
     at N or more pages per second within the engine byte cap". It is
     320 px previews (`PREVIEW_W`, docview.rs:70) of all 7,000 pages in
     order, every page behind a scoped group overlay with a header, a
     watermark and the crop in the section, through the screen's LRU,
     over the time spent in engine opens and renders: lopdf's section
     building is not slice 13's assembly. Slice 13's strip gate counts
     its own assembly in the time, which at 310 pages/s leaves about
     10 ms a group of 128 on the heavy. The scanned 7k isn't held to it
     (about 150 pages/s on the bare base, decoding its images).
   - **The background budget's rule is two consumers at once.** The
     first rule, one OCR walk that opens no group twice, held for 1
     engine as well, so it didn't pick 2. Two walks taking turns (from
     the first page and from the middle, 1,024 pages each) reopen at
     every turn with 1 engine and never with 2, which is what 2 is for;
     three at once would share it. A document runs OCR, a job, a plugin
     run and a Trim White crop each on its own, so more than two can
     run, and 2 is recorded as chosen for two, not measured enough for
     more. The walks render at 300 dpi, sheaf-ocr's default, while the
     screen holds 6 engines pinned (groups 26 and 27 in one pane, 12
     and 13 in the other, 0 and 1 in the strip); groups the screen
     holds serve the walks without a second open.

     and `FPDF_FFLDraw` takes no matrix: a render-time box edit can't
     draw live widgets (C's main failure, 676 of 1,046 widget pages).
     This bears on §10.1's `FormDraw`.
   - **Object numbers start above `/Size`, not lopdf's `max_id`:** on
     `pool/safedocs/5801/5801985.pdf`, lopdf's `max_id` and merged xref
     stop at 76, `/Size` is 78 and the newest xref stream is object 77.

     pdfium-render hands each PDFium block request to one `Read::read`,
