   Found:
   - **A widget that is its field's object, where the field has other
     widgets or the widget shows twice,** is written apart from its field
     by every save (`emit::form`'s split), so an opened file's map has no
     number for the widget's key and an Append that writes its page
     refers to an object the file hasn't got: 34 of the corpus's one-mark
     saves rewrite for BaseObjectsMissing (0003532's radio parent is
     itself a widget with two kids; 0218989's signature widget is listed
     on two pages). Correct, and only slower; an Append could refer to the
     merged object as the widget, which the Rewrite's split would then
     have to match (unbudgeted).
   - **Dropping usage rights on an Append is always vetoed:** a comment on
     a file whose rights allow only filling in (211 corpus files, with
     Reader's usage rights and no other signature) plans DropUr3, which
     unlinks the `/UR3` signature dictionary, whose strings the removal
     check finds gone; the save rewrites for RemovalCheck, as DropXfa's
     does. A decision for Greg (below).
   - **qpdf passes every one-mark Append of the corpus** (3,770 files,
     run once, not kept as a test): none checks worse than its original.
     2,107 check clean as their originals do; 1,546 originals warn,

   For Greg:
   - **An Append that writes form keys checks the whole file's form**
     (finding 18): 1,036 ms and 1,577 MB added for a one-page form
     inserted into the scanned 7k, against one mark's 22 ms. The check
     is a real post-condition and stays; reading only what the newest
     revision reaches, lazily, is unbudgeted. Greg (2026-10-19): keep
     the check; a scoped one is a follow-up (Left for later).
   - **Deleted means deleted runs on every corpus file by default** (the
     review's finding 2, against step 8's every fourth file): 434 s, and
     `cargo test --workspace` went from 419 s to 783 s. Greg
     (2026-10-19): moved to the ignored tier, still over every file;
     each slice's Verify and Commit run it.
   - **§9.3's mapping is conservative** until the Acrobat cross-check:
     `/P` 2 allows only filling in (so a P2 + UR3 comment asks), an
     approval signature with no MDP allows filling in and comments, a
     signature that can't be read is `/P` 1, FieldMDP's includes lock the
     nodes over a name too. 284 corpus forms are GPO certifications with
     `/P` 1, so every save of them asks, Appends included (360 of the
     corpus's one-mark saves ask). The picked files are in Asks.
   - **Planned drops the removal check vetoes:** DropXfa on a hybrid
     form's Append and DropUr3 on a file whose rights a change exceeds
     unlink objects with text (the XFA streams, the `/UR3` signature), so
     the save rewrites (211 corpus files' comments) or a signed file asks.
     Should a planned transform's unlinked objects be allowed drops?
   - **The command line copy-appends** a signed input saved to another
     path when the signatures allow it (the `materialize::save` ledger
     row), until slice 19's flags.
   - **Save As over the original signed file after a Rewrite** no longer
     asks: the saved file's signatures don't hold.
   - **UR3-only files count as signed for CopyOf,** so Save As keeps their
     rights when a change is within them.
   - **Another tool's comment edited into a sheaf mark always rewrites:**
     its old dates and strings don't survive an Append.
   - **An unknown encoding** is the raw bytes' hash: the same text in
     another encoding counts as differing.
   - **A field rename counts as replaced text,** so it rewrites.
   - **An XFA copy comes back** on an Append when save policy keeps it
     again (the fields as the file had them), refused when a Rewrite
     pruned its streams.
   - **Held refusals** (a primary object whose number the file gives
     another record) rewrite rather than renumber in place.
   - **Recovery:** the removal check runs on sidecar sections only to set
     `removes`; sidecar flags carry classes and fields; a Full restore
     can't copy-append on Save As (NoSaveRecord: a Rewrite that asks); a
     restored file with an approval signature appends silently when its
     tail removed nothing, and asks with Append anyway when it did,
     saying only "what the recovered changes removed".
   - **Writes:** an I/O error while appending cuts the file back at once,
     and `undo_torn` restores the file's time, so a sidecar written
     against the file still holds. A forced Append (Append anyway) applies
     Append-mode transforms and checks only what the newest revision's
     form reaches: unlinked widgets are what "stays readable".

   After the commit (a review of cabd8e8; each finding fixed in a
   follow-up, with a test that fails with the fix switched off):
   - **An Append's new numbers and a dangling reference** (finding 5):
     `number::appended` numbered new keys past the file's `/Size`, its
     cross-reference streams, its map and `present`, but not past the
     primary numbers the section names, as `number::stable`'s `named`
     does, so a primary object's reference to a number nothing is
     (another tool's damage, which `Saved::own` passes as the file's), at
     or past `/Size`, could be taken by a new object and name it; and
     `verify::section` passed a reference to any number the primary never
     used, a new one the section doesn't write too. Now the new numbers
     start past every primary number the section names: copy 0 of the
     map's identity blob among its keys and placeholders, what
     `Emission::owned` writes at, and what the primary's objects it
     writes as they are (`SymObject::Raw`, read before numbering now)
     refer to, none past `NUMBERS`. When only those leave too few numbers
     the Append is refused (`Refused::Unsound`), so the save is a
     Rewrite, which numbers it for itself. And `verify::section` fails a
     reference at or past the first new number (below `NUMBERS`) to what
     the section doesn't write, as `links`' `given` does. Tests:
     `a_dangling_reference_stays_dangling_past_the_new_numbers` (a page
     naming its `/Size` and four past it, a mark added and three pages of
     another file inserted, planned as an Append; and the Rewrite of the
     same edits), `a_reply_written_as_it_was_keeps_its_dangling_reference`
     (another tool's reply naming the `/Size`, written raw beside its
     mark's new appearance), `numbers_named_near_the_last_refuse_the_append`
     (the refusal, and the planned save's Rewrite stopping as its own
     numbering does, nothing written), and verify's
     `a_reference_to_a_number_the_section_gave_and_doesn_t_write_fails`.
     Switched off, each failed: without `named` the first two found their
     references naming new objects (`12 0` and `16 0`; `12 0`) and the
     third wasn't refused; without the raw objects' numbers only the
     reply's test failed; with a plain error for the refusal, the third;
     without `given`, the section's check passed `101 0`.
     Deviations and what's left: the raw objects' references count too,
     which `stable` doesn't count of a Rewrite's; the Rewrite is
     unchanged, its bytes the same. So what a number at or past `/Size`
     that nothing is can still come to name a new object from is what
     neither counts: a Rewrite's primary objects as they are, and the
     file's objects outside an Append's section (any update numbers from
     the file's `/Size`, and finding such references means reading every
     object); the Rewrite's half would change its bytes, so it's left for
     Greg. An object both strategies build that names a number so
     near 8,388,607 that the new objects don't fit past it now stops the
     save: the Append is refused and the Rewrite stops, as it always did
     (the Append used to write it). The corpus didn't move:
     materialize_corpus's identity 4,389 of 4,392 written, 2,269,722
     surviving, 919,479 copied, 436 changed by `keep_only`, 0 failed (the
     other five rows as before); append_corpus 3,770 appended, 259
     rewritten (34, 14 and 211), 360 asked, 0 failed; encrypted_corpus 573
     kept by the Rewrite, 572 by the Append and one declined; deleted
     means deleted (ignored tier) as before, the first Append declined by
     28, 68, 68, 68, 0 and 30, 0 failed.
   - **A crop's copy made copy 0 by a move** (finding 6): `emit::shown`
     makes the first in order of a page's derived copies its copy 0, so
     moving the duplicate of a cropped page before the original made the
     duplicate the page's copy 0, the owner of the primary object's
     number, while neither page was written (one node holds both). An
     Append numbers a key by the file's map first, so that number still
     held the original, and what names the page by number (the second
     page's link, which the section writes again; the catalog's
     `/OpenAction`, which it keeps) went to it, where a Rewrite claims the
     owned numbers first and writes the duplicate there. `append::held`
     checked only the keys the section writes. Now it checks every key of
     `Emission::owned`: one the section doesn't write is where the map has
     it (else at its own number, as `Saved::number` finds it), and one
     anywhere but its own number refuses the Append (`Refused::Held`,
     `BaseObjectsMissing`), as another key the file holds there that stays
     did. Tests: `append_rewrite_a_crop_s_copy_made_copy_0_by_a_move_rewrites`
     (the review's scenario, the second page's link going to the first)
     and `append_rewrite_an_open_action_to_a_crop_s_copy_made_copy_0_rewrites`
     (the catalog's `/OpenAction` going there instead), each reopened as a
     Rewrite of the same state after both saves; the reopen compares where
     the open action goes now (the property's files had none until the
     second round below gave them one). Switched off (only the keys
     written checked), the open action's test failed (the Append's going
     to the second place, the Rewrite's to the first); the link's still
     passed, as finding 7's check refuses it too, and with both switched
     off it failed the same way.
   - **Page references the relinking didn't judge again** (finding 7):
     finding 16's fix judged again only other tools' links with an object
     of their own, by their explicit destination. What else the file has
     that names a page of a source, which a copy's reference names
     otherwise now (a widget's action, a field's, a link written straight
     into `/Annots`, an annotation the records don't hold), kept the page
     it named when it was written. Now `deps::closure` finds such a holder
     the section doesn't write again (`Closure::stale`) and `append`
     refuses (`Refused::Stale`, `BaseObjectsMissing`), so the save is a
     Rewrite. `Relinking` keeps both states' written pages; `moved` says
     whether a reference resolves otherwise, as `copy::page_named` (the
     copy closure's, shared now) resolves it, or from the primary's copy 0
     by its number: it named a page then and another or none now (one that
     named none names the page that came, which `held` keeps at the
     number). The holders, each read as its emitter reads it: every page's

11. Done. Edits are ops (proposals 20 and 25; bugs 8, 11, 12, 25, 27 and
   29): a caller says a change as `sheaf_edit::Op`s, a transaction (`Tx`)
   resolves each op's references against the state it finds, checks the
   actor's capability, lowers it into prims with the cascades, declared
   once, run to a fixed point, and `Document::commit` makes the ops one
   version at the cursor, with what they made (`Commit.created`), their
   lines, effects, cascades and typed notices. sheaf-edit is the
   vocabulary, types and JSON with a committed schema, and builds for
   wasm32-wasip2; sheaf-core is split, what stays renamed sheaf-util. A
   source is its blob (`SourceId = BlobId`) and each insert, replace and
   duplicate is a form instance of its own, so the registrations and
   slice 10's form-shift refusal are gone. The app, the plugin host
   (through the transitional WIT 0.2/0.3 → Op adapter), sheaf-ops, the
   command line and every test build ops, and Combine is one
   transaction. `Edit`, `compute`, `EditOutcome`, the registration layer,
   `form_notice`, `insert_runs`, the app's id guesses, `sign_marks` and
   `keep_unseen` are deleted. At 7,000 pages `Tx::check` of deleting every
   page takes 0.39 ms and draws no id; an AddMark and a full reorder, now
   transactions, take 0.022 and 1.0 ms; the Rewrite is 1.12× slice 8's
   writer on both fixtures; the corpus counts hold.
   - **sheaf-util and sheaf-edit** (step 1). sheaf-core is `git mv`ed to
     `crates/sheaf-util` and keeps `checksum`, `checksum_hex`,
     `Checksum`, `read_file` and `read_file_and_metadata`, twox-hash its
     only dependency. `crates/sheaf-edit` (0.1.0, published; serde and
     schemars, serde_json for tests) holds `ids` (`PageId`, `OutlineId`,
     `AnnotId`, `FieldId`, `Local` written `"$n"`, `BlobId` written
     `"b<32 hex>-<len>"` with `stem`/`from_stem`, and `SourceId =
     BlobId` from step 2), `page` (`Rotation`, `PageSize`, `DestView`,
     `TextStyle`), `geom` (`Pt`, `Box2`, `Vec2`), `tape` (moved whole;
     its calculator `Op`'s schema is `TapeOp`), `measure` (`Measured`,
     `Scale`, `points_per`), `text_layer` (`TextLayer`, `OcrWord`),
     `header_footer` (`HeaderFooterSpec`, `Margins`, `BatesSpec`),
     `labels` (`LabelStyle`, `PageLabelRange`), `mark` (`Color`, `Style`,
     `MarkKind`, `NewMark`, `MarkPatch`, `Imported`, `Anchor`), `refs`
     (`PageRef`, `BookmarkRef`, `AnnotRef` over one hand-written visitor:
     a number is an id, a string a local, an object `{"pos"}`,
     `{"path"}` or `{"nm", "page"}`; `BlobSel`, `PageSel`, `ScopeSel`,
     `RangeSet` written `"1-3,5"`), `patch` (`Patch<T>`: absent keeps,
     null clears, a value sets), `op` (the 21 ops, `Turn` as 90/180/270,
     `Sibling`, `Delta`, `BookmarkPatch`, `PageSource::File`, `Bring`)
     and `envelope` (`Envelope`, `VERSION` "1.0", its reader refusing
     another major or a later minor as soon as it reads `v`).
     `deny_unknown_fields` is on every op-layer type, and (the review's
     finding 1) on the moved `TextStyle`, `DestView`, `TextLayer` and
     `OcrWord`, which nothing stores as JSON. The record types
     `/SheafAnnot` stores inside its lenient `Annot` keep the serde they
     had: `Pt`, `Box2`, `Scale`, and `Tape` with its `Line`, `Row` and
     `TapeLook` (strict, a mark another sheaf wrote with a field more
     would read as another tool's comment; tape's own test reads old
     tapes). Their fields but a line's note and the look are required, so
     a misspelling there is still an error and only an extra field is
     ignored; `Measured` is a unit enum, already strict. sheaf-doc
     re-exports each moved
     type at its old path; `BlobId::of` became `store::blob_id`, and
     `TextLayer::from_engine`, `upright_box`, `unrotate_from_upright` and
     `line_of` functions in `text_layer`. `PageIndex` went to
     sheaf-render; ocr, ops, app, plugin and print use sheaf-util,
     sheaf-edit and sheaf-render; sheaf-ui's dependency went. Every crate
     but sheaf-edit and sheaf-plugin-api is `publish = false`. ci.yml
     gains "sheaf-util stays byte helpers" (its tree exactly sheaf-util
     and twox-hash) and "sheaf-edit stays types only" (no other sheaf
     crate under it, and `cargo build -p sheaf-edit --target
     wasm32-wasip2`).
   - **Sources are blobs, one form instance per insert** (step 2). The
     registration layer is deleted (`SourceId(u32)`, `SourceInfo`,
     `Document.sources`, `next_source`, `unlogged_sources`, `add_source`,
     `register_source`, `unregister`, `Version.sources`,
     `Snapshot.sources`, `PageBase.source`); records hold their `Src`,
     `PageBase { src, index }` and `FormInst { src: BlobId, copy }`.
     `Store::read_file(path, password) -> (Src, FileStamp)`,
     `store::file_name`, `Store::sources()` (what `find_stamp` and
     `find_file` look through, the primary first), `Document::new(store,
     primary, name, …)`, `Came::Read { path, stamp }` and `Came::Restored

     `FormInst`, its copy the next its blob has in the state (copy 0 of
     the primary's kept for its own instance), named by the op; the join

     issued one insert per file from here). The emitter indexes an
     instance by `inst.copy`, so `FormCopies`, `deps::Closure::form_shift`
     and `append::Refused::FormShift` are deleted, and the old FormShift
     test is inverted (`a_form_instance_keeps_its_objects_across_saves`).
     `deps::Closure::stale` reads a widget and a field as `inst.copy` of
     their blob, as the emitter does, and `Relinking`'s primary and the

     Derived copies' origins are a side table, `Document.derived:
     Arc<HashMap<BlobId, Derived>>` (`add_derived`, `derived()`), which
     `Snapshot` and `SaveInput` carry with the primary; `DerivedSource {
     src, derived, pages }` with `note` and (step 7) `bases`. Each
     `Version` notes once, at push and amend, the blobs its steps bring
     (`blobs`), so `undone_source_bytes` walks no step. Scripts count per
     instance. The app keys engines by `BlobId`, so the same bytes share
     one.
   - **The transaction** (`crates/sheaf-doc/src/tx/`, step 3).
     `Document::lower_cx(actor)` (the only constructor of `LowerCx`: the
     store, the primary, the `Arc<IdAlloc>`, `HostAttrs` and the actor),
     `Document::tx(actor)`, `Tx::{apply, apply_batch, check, read,
     reader, pin, grant, grant_named, state, set_page_base}`,
     `Document::commit(tx, CommitOpts)` and `apply_in_job(job, tx,
     label)`. `apply` resolves (`tx/resolve.rs`: `ResolvedOp`, the
     `Resolver`), checks caps (`tx/caps.rs`), lowers by family
     (`tx/{pages, bookmarks, marks, content, forms}.rs`) and settles the
     cascades (`tx/cascade.rs`), all or nothing; `apply_batch` is all or
     nothing over an im-backed checkpoint, and a canceled op leaves the
     Tx as it was. `check` resolves and checks caps only. Lowering reads
     are kept by value (`seen`), decision reads through `read`/`reader`
     (`Reader`: `order`, `page_at`, `pos_of`, `def`, `geom`,
     `annot_ids_on`, `marks_on`, `bookmark_pages`, `annot`, `bookmark`,
     `outline_roots`, `labels`, `form`, `field`). `EditError::{NotFound,
     Invalid, Ambiguous, Refused(Cap), NotReady, Cancelled, Mismatch {
     version }, Internal}` and `Notice::{FormRenamed, CopiesRenamed,
     SignatureNotValidHere, ScriptsOff, Unencodable}` with `notice_text`
     (`tx/error.rs`). `Commit { version, amended, created, effects, lines,
     cascades, notices }`; `Created { ops, locals }` with `made`, `pages`,
     `bookmarks` and `annots`. `Step { op: Arc<ResolvedOp>, prims,
     effects: StepEffects, line, cascades }`; `Version` records its
     `Actor` beside its author; `VersionView.edits` is `Vec<describe::Line
     { text, removes }>` with `actor`. Undo, redo and jumps return
     `EditError` (`Mismatch`, `NotFound` for a version no longer kept).
     `Document::set_identity(Identity { person, initials, date_format,
     time_format })` replaces `set_author`; `HostAttrs::now` formats the
     date and time with chrono.
   - **Lowering** (step 3), every slice-11 op, ported from compute's
     arms: ids and `/NM`s, dates from `HostAttrs.now` (one a
     transaction), the default author (the person, or a plugin's id for
     its marks), the identity tokens (`stamp_lib::fill`, moved from
     `sheaf_ops::stamps::fill`; `<<name>>` and `<<initials>>` left as
     written for a plugin), clamps and kind filters, `Imported`, a
     connector's partner, a reply's parent `/NM`, a stamp's and an
     attachment's stem and an attachment's size from its asset, and a new
     header's date and file. The form helpers are lowering's (`take_in`,
     `copy_forms`, `apart`, `instance_copy`, `turn_scripts_off`,
     `signed_in`, `scripted_instances`). `MoveBookmarks { with_pages }`
     puts `Order` (OutlineMove's arm). An insert's marks, links, comments
     and outline come from its source's facts by `Bring`
     (`bring_annots` and `merge_outline` as lowering). Insert, replace,
     duplicate and delete report progress by page. describe.rs is
     rewritten over `ResolvedOp`, its page numbers by `pos_of`;
     `describe::lines` collapses a run of one kind into one line, and the
     internal page base's line names its flow (bug 8). effects.rs gains
     `StepEffects { effects, pages, keys }` and `ClassifyCx::of_step`.
   - **Cascades and validation** (step 4). Seven rules in `Rule::ALL`:
     `page.annots`, `annot.thread`, `annot.partner`, `widget.field`,
     `page.bookmarks`, `page.labels` (`labels::anchored`: a range starting
     on a gone page starts at its range's next page, keeping `first`, or
     goes) and `page.generators` (`Generator::on_pages_left`; a header
     left on no page goes). One trigger pass a round (`Gone::of`, an
     exhaustive match on `Key`), rounds capped at `MAX_ROUNDS` (8,
     `Internal` past it). Validation moved into resolve, so `Tx::check`
     sees it; unknown ids are `NotFound` in every op (bug 11).
     `check_invariants` adds label anchors, the header's page scope,
     symmetric connector pairs and sheaf replies to a comment on their
     page; `open/annots.rs`'s `pair_connectors` and `save::subset` keep
     them. DuplicatePages draws mark ids across the op, renames a copied
     thread's replies to the parent copy's `/NM` (other tools' replies
     too) and pairs copied connectors (bug 12), and a copy joins the
     header's scope after its original.
   - **The Op JSON fuzz target** (step 4): `source::fuzz::op_json`
     (`fixtures`), `fuzz/fuzz_targets/op_json.rs`, `fuzz/op.dict` and the

     envelope to a four-page document with a form, every kind of mark,
     other tools' comments, bookmarks, labels and a header (one op at a
     time when the batch fails), then commits, undoes and redoes,
     checking the invariants each time. `write_fuzz_seeds` writes 57
     seeds (the fixture as one envelope, each op alone, and an
     `applying` envelope whose 49 ops all apply);
     `fuzz_bodies_survive_mutated_fixtures` mutates them as JSON and as

     `fixtures` feature).

   - **The app** (step 6). `DocView::commit(tx, opts) -> Result<Commit,

   - **Plugins** (step 6). `api::shared::Adapter` is the transitional

   - **sheaf-ops, sheaf-render and the command line** (step 7). Combine

   Deviations from the plan (the planner's list first, as resolved):
   - **The Mark record is kept** (`Mark { annot: Annot, src, file,
     stamp }`): replies name their parent by `/NM`, the connector's
     partner is an `AnnotId` in `AnnotKind::Connector`, and stamp and
     attachment stems are in the kind, where §3.6 has `reply_to` and
     `partner` by id and a kind without host fields. `NewMark.kind` is a
     new `sheaf_edit::MarkKind` (AnnotKind's creatable variants without
     partner, parent and stems), which lowering fills from `AddMark`'s
     `reply_to`, `AddConnector` and `NewMark.asset`; threads and the
     duplicate's remap match by `/NM` on the page, as `thread_of` does.
     The public surface is final, so the record's restructure is
     internal: recommended as a follow-up (For Greg).
   - **Ops deferred to the slices that lower them,** a scope deviation:
     `SetPageBoxes` (15), `SetWatermark`/`RemoveWatermark` with
     `WatermarkSpec`/`WatermarkContent` (16), `RemoveHeaderFooter`'s
     `include_authored` (16–17), `FlattenAnnotations`,
     `PageSource::{Blank, Images}`, `Transform` and `ExportTx` (19; their
     only consumer is `export::run`). Shipped now, they would parse and
     then fail to lower; the schema's additive rule makes adding them
     later safe. Refs and selectors ship now (`PageSel::{Span,
     Positions, Bookmark}`, `BookmarkRef::Path`, `BlobSel::With`), since
     resolving them is this slice's and they're tested; their producer is
     slice 19's command line.
   - **API whose consumers are later,** deferred with them: `Tx::preview`
     and `Preview`, `read_render`, `mark_handed_out`,
     `EditError::{Conflict, GroupEnded}`, `CommitOpts.{base, stale,
     group}` and `Commit.change` (12), `JobKind::Trim` (15).
     `EditError::Content` has no producer until an op lowers content
     (16–17), though slice 6 asked this slice to map `ContentError`; its
     other half, a stem that names nothing, is `NotFound` at resolve.
     sheaf-plugin-api doesn't depend on sheaf-edit until WIT 0.4 (20);
     only existing crates got `publish = false`. The app has no
     `can_apply` yet, so `Tx::check`'s consumers are its unit test and
     the gate. The envelope is defined in sheaf-edit as the schema's root,
     read by the schema test; its producers are `sheaf edit` (19) and
     WIT 0.4 (20).
   - **Geometry is the kind's:** the design's `NewMark.geometry` would
     duplicate what each kind carries, so `MarkKind` carries it and
     `MarkPatch.kind` replaces the kind whole, geometry included, beside
     the named style and contents fields.
   - **Effects:** `effects::Effects` stays `Copy { flags, sig }`, which
     `judge` relies on; a step's are `StepEffects { effects, pages, keys
     }` (`Arc<BTreeSet>`s), judged on the step alone
     (`ClassifyCx::of_step`), with no whole-document `shown` walk: a page
     or layer a step took away counts as removed even if another page
     also shows it. `Commit.effects` is the union of its steps'.
   - **Names:** the op's label range is `PageLabelRange` (labels.rs keeps
     `LabelRange`, 0-based positions); tape's calculator `Op` stays
     `sheaf_edit::tape::Op`, its schema `TapeOp`.
   - **The join branch went in step 2** with page-set inserts, not step
     3: with `FormInst.src` a `BlobId`, the same bytes inserted twice
     would have joined one instance. Inserting a file twice gives two
     forms renamed apart (materialize_corpus's 1,098 still write).
   - **Scripts per instance** (§3.7): `scripted_instances` counts
     instances, not distinct sources, so every insert keeps today's
     behaviour and a scripted page's duplicate now turns scripts off
     (`a_scripted_page_s_duplicate_turns_scripts_off`).
   - **`Damaged` and `NotReady`** are `EditError::Mismatch { version }`
     and `EditError::NotReady`; the History panel and the app's open
     follow.
   - **`SourceInfo`'s parts:** an instance's name is the op's `name` (the
     primary's from its open path); `Derived { from: Src, pages }` is in
     the document's table by `BlobId`; the record's path travels in
     `Came`. `BlobId::of` needs the checksum, so it's sheaf-doc's
     `store::blob_id`; `BlobId` had no serde, so its string form changes
     no persisted format.
   - **Identity tokens** moved into sheaf-doc (`stamp_lib::fill`), since
     lowering fills them; `HostAttrs` carries the person, the initials,
     now as a PDF date, and the date and time as dynamic stamps write
     them. `Document::set_identity` takes an `Identity` struct; an
     invalid strftime format from settings falls back to the defaults.
   - **Stems become grants:** WIT 0.3 names stamps and attachments by
     stem and the design refuses a plugin's raw `BlobSel::Id`, so the
     host resolves a stem (the generated-cache arm included until 19)
     into a grant on the Tx (`Tx::grant`, `BlobSel::Asset(n)`). Grants
     live on the Tx, not in `LowerCx` (an `Arc` made only by
     `lower_cx`); `Grant` is `Blob(BlobRef)` or `Stamp { stem, form }`,
     since a `FormRef::Base` has no stem.
   - **Attachments decoded before lowering:** `resolve::incoming` and
     `ready_to_insert` decode and intern what an inserted file's marks
     hold, off the UI thread in the app, and the caller pins them. An
     attachment whose decoded bytes' id differs from the mark's stem now
     holds no file (compute held the mismatched blob).
   - **retired.rs:** moved helpers got new names where a bare call of the
     old name would hit (`thread_of`, `outline_from_flat` and `nest`
     moved under their names and are live, so they have no rows);
     `Edit`'s variants are retired with their enum, since a variant row
     would hit WIT's `Edit::OutlineInsertTree`; the sheaf-core crate's
     retirement is its absence and the CI tree step, as a `sheaf_*`
     prefix is stripped before matching.
   - **The new-bookmark guess** was a sibling-index lookup
     (outline_panel.rs), not the pre-order bug 25 describes, and right
     whenever the edit succeeded: with it put back,
     `a_new_bookmark_is_the_one_selected`'s refused half fails (it
     selected an existing bookmark, which the panel would rename); a
     pre-order guess fails its success half.
   - **The 7k harness's history rows** stay O(what the op names):
     describe numbers pages by `pos_of`, and `undone_source_bytes` reads
     each version's blob set noted at push.
   - **fuzz/Cargo.lock** was updated with `cargo update --workspace
     --offline` (sheaf-util, sheaf-edit, and sheaf-doc's `bitflags`, which
     an earlier slice had left stale); the fuzz build can't run here.

   Deviations found while building:
   - **Step 1:** `NewMark.turn` (default R0, left out of JSON at R0), the
     rotation a mark reads upright in, which producers set (markup on
     turned text, marks on a rotated page, paste); `MarkKind::
     FileAttachment` has no `size` (lowering sets the asset's length);
     `MarkKind::Reply {}` is a struct variant so it refuses extra keys;
     `BlobSel`'s Deserialize is derived (all its forms are objects);
     `RangeSet` is non-generic `u32`; `Turn`, `Sibling`, `Anchor`,
     `AddConnector { label, style }` and `HeaderFooterSpec` (no font
     until 17; date and file the host's) are shaped here; `Bring { marks,
     form: New, outline: None | MergeByTitle }`, comments and links
     always coming; `TextLayer::text()` reimplemented in sheaf-edit;
     `measure` moved only its types and `points_per`.
   - **Step 2:** `next_copy` reserved copy 0 of the primary's blob even
     when the state doesn't hold it, as `FormCopies` did, so today's
     flows' copies equal the old indexes and the corpus wrote the same
     bytes; deps' "other files" are the non-primary blobs, so a
     self-insert isn't another file (the emitter already worked by
     blob), and the emitter's `others` are in `BlobId` order (it matters
     only for `/DR` renames with two or more other files whose fonts
     clash; no test or corpus case has one); `brought()` counts a page's
     source only when a prim changes which source it shows; a non-primary
     first page's FDF `/F` and the untagged note name the blob's first
     origin (`Blob::origin_name`); `graph::load` became `graph::eager`;
     `RebasePages` looked each source up once an edit (crop's edit went
     from 12.6 to 16.6 ms without it). Test changes:
     `append_rewrite_widgets_whose_objects_moved_rewrite` appends now
     (a page replaced by its own page is an instance of its own) as
     `append_rewrite_a_page_replaced_by_its_own_page_is_a_form_of_its_own`;
     `missing_objects_on_a_signed_file_ask_and_write_nothing` drops a
     mark's key from the record (`forced_lacking`) instead of relying on
     FormShift; the waiting-registration parts of three history tests
     went with unlogged sources.
   - **Step 3:** cascades share one trigger pass a round (`Gone::of`),
     `annot.thread` finds a whole thread in one run, `Cascade` is `{
     rule, objects }`; the app's "removed N pages and M bookmarks" notice
     compares counts before and after (`Had`), since a delete's pages and
     a bookmark delete's subtree are the ops' own work; replacing a
     header keeps its frozen date and file, and `RemoveHeaderFooter`
     narrows the scope (All becomes a page list); `ReplacePages` ignores
     `bring.outline` (Replace never merged an outline, and refusing the
     default would refuse default Op JSON); there's no `wrote` set (a
     slot is unwritten while it holds its base value); `locals` and
     `seen` are im collections; a `PatchMarks` that changes nothing, or
     a `MoveMarks` by zero, makes no prim; the Edit→Op shim translated
     every old edit for steps 3–6, among them `CommentsDelete` to the
     foreign comments' ids and an `AnnotAdd` naming another tool's
     comment to Adopt plus a patch; `AdoptAnnotations` resolves a
     `PageStamp` stem through `find_stamp`, its generated-cache arm a
     file read inside lowering for that one case until 19; describe
     collapses runs at view and commit time, the last line of a run
     shown for labels and header ops; `Version.author` stays beside
     `actor`.
   - **Step 4:** two refusals beyond the list (moving a thread's mark to
     another page, and patching a connector into another kind, are
     `Invalid`, since threads are by `/NM` per page and pairs must stay
     pairs); an undeclared local is `NotFound`; the connector invariant
     is that both ends name each other, which open's `pair_connectors`
     makes true of files; the reply-parent invariant is narrowed to
     sheaf's Reply and Status marks (files hold orphans and cross-page
     `/IRT`; the debug-built corpus runs found no file that breaks the
     narrowed form); `page.labels` keeps a re-anchored range's `first`,
     so its pages renumber within it, as for a middle page deleted;
     `page.generators` removes a header left on no page; `save::subset`
     produces states that keep the new invariants, so an extract whose
     label range started on a page left out changes; the fuzz body is
     `cfg(any(test, feature = "fixtures"))` and sheaf-edit lists itself
     as a dev-dependency for its own tests; the 8-round guard is a unit
     test of `rounds()`; three proptest regression seeds were kept (the
     review deleted them: see Found).
     materialize/deps.rs changed beyond the list: `Deps::annot` writes
     the page when an annotation becomes or stops being a Replace mark,
     since its StrikeOut is listed beside it (found below).
   - **Step 5:** comment import grants each asset by its stem
     (`BlobSel::With`), since a stamp found as a source's form can't be
     named by id; a target is by `Nm { nm, page }` unless that page has
     the name twice (then by id, since `Nm` would be `Ambiguous`); a
     reply whose comment is neither on its page nor in the import is
     left out and counted (`orphans`, "N replies left out"), where the
     old import kept it pointing at nothing; another tool's comment is
     matched only on the imported comment's own page and only if
     holdable; `DocView::commit` came ahead of step 6 for the import;
     BATCH applies each generated op to the Tx and skips the ones that
     fail; OCR jobs run as `Actor::Job(Ocr)`; move-bookmarks falls back
     to add-bookmark with fewer than two bookmarks; delete-pages never
     selects by span or bookmark (a bookmark's span could be every
     page); `a_run_applies_every_kind` retries a kind up to 8 times; the
     no-op table follows the ops (no no-op for inserts, replaces and
     adds; empty lists for the list ops; the same layer `Arc` for OCR;
     a set-page-base Tx of no pages); `edit_serde_round_trip` went with
     `Edit`'s serde.
   - **Step 6:** the plugin-update Check's test is in sheaf-plugin's
     api/mod.rs (`a_plugin_update_keeps_what_it_cant_see`), since the
     WIT bindings are crate-private there; the app's plugins.rs holds the
     identity test (`a_plugins_marks_are_its_own_and_never_name_the_user`);
     a plugin's marks are authored by its id; `EditBatch` is `{ label,
     ops, held, invalid }`, a tree whose depth skips a level carried as
     the error `lowered` fails with; AnnotDelete and AnnotUpdate ignore
     the record's page; an update's stem is ignored (the old shim refused
     a changed one); a plugin connector's ends read upright in their
     page's rotation now; `DocView::apply`/`apply_batch` return
     `Option<Commit>` (the error shown centrally); status replies write
     "{state} set by <<name>>"; "Delete comment" deletes by id every
     same-named comment of another tool's on the page;
     `reveal_new_bookmarks` runs on every commit's created bookmarks;
     Bookmarks from Pages and pattern hits append with `Sibling::Last`;
     additions used by callers: `PageSel::ids`, `From` for the refs,
     `Turn::by`, `Created`'s accessors, `Reader::{marks_on,
     bookmark_pages}`, `mark_changes`, `ready_to_insert`,

   Found:
   - **By the property at 1,024 cases, fixed in the slice** (each a test
     that fails with its fix reverted): `annot.thread` took the replies a
     `ReplacePages` brought in, whose parent's `/NM` was the removed
     comment's (a thread now starts only from names no annotation on the
     page still has, and `thread_of` stops at a name another annotation
     outside it still has); adopting a duplicated or inserted copy's reply
     named the file's parent, not the record's (`summary.parent`); an
     adopted replacement whose StrikeOut was deleted earlier appended
     without its new StrikeOut (`deps::Deps::annot` writes the page when
     an annotation becomes or stops being a Replace mark; a step-3
     regression); `RemoveHeaderFooter` of pages outside the header's
     scope turned an All scope into a page list and pushed a version (the
     no-op table); and the removal check's `says()` for another tool's
     reply left out the name it replies to, so adopting a reply,
     appending, undoing and saving as another file made the Rewrite
     oracle see a derived removal
     (`append_rewrite_a_reply_made_editable_then_undone_removes_nothing`;
     one line in materialize/removal.rs). Of the proptest regression
     seeds saved in the slice, only append_rewrite's `6dfbb569` is kept:
     step 5's change of the action alphabet made step 4's three replay
     unrelated runs, so the review deleted them (the bugs they found
     have tests of their own). Slice 10's fixes' append_rewrite seed
     (`b7c3ef0b`, a page base set and a forced Append in slice 10's
     alphabet) went for the same reason: over the `Op` generators it
     replays an unrelated run, and so did two that proptest saved while
     the rebase's fault checks failed the property on purpose. A change
     to a property's alphabet invalidates its saved seeds.
   - **A wrong widget `/P` after a replace, an Append and an insert,
     fixed** (not this slice's: it failed at 121d4a3 and with the slice 10
     fixes, 99c7685). Open `files(false)`, Save As (a Rewrite, the fifth
     page at its own object, 13), replace the fifth page by form.pdf's
     second and force an Append, which writes the replacement over 13, the
     number the file's map has for that page; insert the primary's fourth
     and fifth pages before it (copy 0 of the fifth is free again), and
     the inserted fifth page, the primary's object (`Emission::owned`),
     takes 13 at the next Append, the replacement a new number; but the
     closure didn't write what names the replacement by number, so its
     widgets' `/P` still said 13, the other page. In the files: after the
     forced Append the replacement's widgets (86–89) said `/P 13 0 R`;
     after the next, the tree listed the inserted page at 13 and the
     replacement at 94, the widgets unchanged. With the primary's first
     page inserted too, the section wrote form keys and the post-condition
     stopped the save ("the written form has widgets with the wrong /P",
     form.form1[0].kind/print/sig/state); without it nothing of the form
     was written, so the form wasn't checked and the Append wrote the bad
     file, which the property's reopen didn't see either (it didn't read
     `/P`). Inserted at the end, the replacement came first in the
     emission, kept 13, and `held` refused (a Rewrite). The fix, fail
     closed: `deps::closure` finds the pages the file has at the number of
     a primary page that another page is copy 0 of now
     (`Closure::renumbered`) and writes each as a page that shows another:
     with no place in the saved tree (spliced), its annotations (widgets
     with their fields), the bookmarks to it, the links to its source
     page, and its source page moved for `stale` (`Relinking::moved`), so
     a copy's reference to it the section doesn't write again refuses the
     Append. `number::appended` gives an owned key its own number whatever
     is emitted first (the key the file has there takes a new one), so the
     pages' order no longer decides; `append::held` lets another key leave
     an owned key's number only when it's a page of `renumbered` the
     section writes elsewhere (before, any key written elsewhere); and the
     section's form is checked whenever it writes a page at another number
     than the file has it at. The property's `Reopened` compares each
     page's `/Annots` entries whose `/P` is another page. Tests, each a
     planned Append that reopens as a fresh Rewrite does, the
     replacement's number changed and no `WrongPage` in the file:
     `append_rewrite_a_page_appended_over_a_primary_page_gives_its_number_back`
     (the sequence above),
     `append_rewrite_a_page_appended_over_a_primary_page_writes_its_widgets_again`
     (without the first page: the bad file) and
     `append_rewrite_a_page_appended_over_a_primary_page_gives_it_up_wherever_it_comes`
     (at the end: refused before, appended now). With deps.rs, number.rs
     and append.rs as they were, all three fail (the post-condition; the
     reopen's other `/P` on four widgets; a Rewrite); with the closure's
     annotations of a renumbered page left out, the new form check stops
     all three saves; with `number::appended` as it was, the end case is a
     Rewrite. The seed the property found it with used step 4's numbering
     of actions and was never saved, and over the `Op` generators it no
     longer replays the sequence. With the fix, the 1,024-case property
     passed four runs in release (64–67 s each); no corpus count moved
     (IDENTITY, MARKED, ORACLE, the DELETED tier's declined [28, 68, 68,
     68, 0, 30], encrypted); the workspace suite: 1,169 passed, 31
     ignored, 0 failed; clippy and fmt clean.
   - **The emitter's own field rule** (emit/form.rs's `gone` and
     `showed`: a field shown nowhere that showed as read isn't written)
     mostly duplicates `widget.field` now; step 4 hash-checked that the
     cascade's removal writes the same bytes over the 2,901
     first-page-delete outputs. Simplifying the emitter is left until a
     byte-identity check says it's safe.
   - **`/DR` renames are still decided at emit,** not at lowering and
     recorded in `FormDoc` as §6.5 says (records.rs's comment said
     "until slice 11"): the emitter merges the instances' files' `/DR`,
     in `BlobId` order, deterministically. Nothing reads `FormDoc`'s
     `/DR` yet; left for the slice whose appearances read it.

12. Done. One funnel and the history budget (proposals 13 and 19; bugs
   9, 25, 26, and 27's version check): a transaction made on an earlier
   version lands on the current one, checked by value against what it
   read and wrote and then by the cascades and the uniqueness and
   reference rules (`Stale::Validate`), or lowered there again with the
   ids it drew (`Stale::Relower`), or is a Conflict naming the edit in
   the way and changes nothing. Every transition gives a `ChangeSet`,
   made from the slots it changed. An OCR run and a plugin call are
   groups of versions that undo as one step: edits between split them
   into "(continued)" fragments, an undo stops them (`GroupEnded`),
   History undoes all of one (`revert_group`), and a failed call rolls
   back (`rollback_group`). Every change reaches the app's one refresh,
   `on_change`; the user's, planners', dialogs' and plugin calls' commits
   go through `DocView::commit`, OCR's flushes commit on the model in
   their run's group (Deviations); and a mark's edit lays nothing out.
   Inserts, crop, watermark, header and footer, labels, blank review and
   comment import plan on a snapshot, off the UI thread or in their
   dialog, and land on its version. A plugin call reads the document
   from a cell that swaps at every change, and its batches land as one
   undo step on what it read. History is pruned to its 256 MB
   budget: the saved version detaches into an anchor, the first version
   kept drops its prims, and a push walks no history. The job API, the
   app's three funnels and relayout per edit, `reveal_new_bookmarks`'
   outline walk, the `NoProgress` paths and slice 11's refusal of commits
   off the cursor are deleted. 200 OCR versions of a 1,000-page scan hold
   at most 256 MB (4,254 MB of steps before); a snapshot takes 0.2 µs at
   7,000 pages; the last 100 of 1,000 mark adds take what the first 100
   do; the Rewrite is 1.11× slice 8's writer on both fixtures; the
   corpus counts hold.
   - **ChangeSets and version keys** (step 1). `change.rs`: `ChangeSet
     {from, to, cause, actor, label, keys, order, pages_added,
     pages_removed, geometry, content, annots, fields, outline, labels,
     form, generators }` and `Cause::{Opened, Commit, Amend, Undo, Redo,
     Jump, Saved, Rollback, Revert}`, re-exported from the crate's root.
     `ChangeSet::of` reads the keys only, a slot lookup or two a key
     (`Page(p)`: None→Some added, Some→None removed, Some→Some content;
     `Geom` geometry; `PageAnnots` and an `Annot`'s page in either state
     annotations; the rest their flag or list); `empty` (a no-op commit, a
     save) and `opened` (every flag, every page and field, no keys).
     `Version.keys` is its coalesced steps' prims' keys, sharing its one
     step's `effects.keys` `Arc` when it has one; `edges_between(a, b)`
     walks up from both ends until the lines meet, and `path_keys` and undo,
     redo and jump (`move_to`) take its versions' keys (`keys_along`).
     `Commit.change`; `undo`, `redo` and `jump` return
     `Result<Option<ChangeSet>, EditError>` (a jump to the current version
     `Ok(None)`); `record_save`, `record_unchanged` and `Written::record_in`
     return `Result<ChangeSet>` (`Saved`, from and to the current version,
     "Save"); `ready` returns `(ViewFacts, ChangeSet)`.
   - **Stale bases** (step 2). `Base { Current, At(VersionId) }`, `Stale {
     Validate, Relower }`, `CommitOpts { label, base, stale, group }` with
     `Default`, `labelled(label)` and (step 6) `based(v, stale, label)`;
     `Preview { lines, effects, created }` and `Tx::preview()`;
     `EditError::Conflict { key, by: Option<Arc<str>> }`;
     `Document::tx_at(snapshot, cx)`. A transaction keeps its ops as entries
     (`Entry::Op { op, drawn, positional }`, `Entry::Base` for
     `set_page_base`) and draws every id through `Lower` (`page_id`,
     `outline_id`, `field_id`, `annot_id`, `gen_id`: the next pinned first,
     then the allocator, the rng or `GenId::draw`, each recorded), where
     tx/pages.rs, tx/forms.rs, tx/bookmarks.rs and tx/content.rs drew their
     own; `outline_from_flat` and `nest` take an id-drawing closure.
     `model/stale.rs`'s `onto_cursor`, called by `settle` before it
     coalesces: a base the caller states wrongly is `Internal`; every
     decided read must hold by value (`prim::same`); `Validate` checks
     `seen` and the first before of each written key, then `merge` puts the
     steps' prims on a `Rec` over the current state (a misfit a Conflict),
     says each line again and works its effects out again, and runs the
     post-merge check (`cascade::unsettled`, one round of every rule over
     what the merge wrote; `DocState::unique_after`: one generator per kind
     and place by `GenSpec::same_place`, a source page's copy shown once,
     `/NM` per page, full names; `resolves_after`: what written slots name
     is there); `Relower` needs the base's order unchanged when an entry
     resolved a position, then lowers the entries again on a fresh
     transaction with the same context, grants, names and pins, each op's
     drawn ids pinned. `conflict()` names the newest edit on the current
     line, down to where the base's line meets it, whose keys hold the slot.
     The refusal in `settle` is deleted.
   - **Groups** (step 3). `GroupId`, `GroupKind::{Ocr, PluginCall {plugin
     }}`, `Document::{begin_group, end_group}`, live groups only in
     `Document.groups` (`Group { kind, label, latest }`), `Version.group`
     and `VersionView.group` (the id and the group's label),
     `CommitOpts.group` and `EditError::GroupEnded`. `joins()` (GroupEnded
     once the group's latest isn't the current version or before it, or the
     group ended; Internal for an actor its kind doesn't take), `amends()`
     (the current version is the group's, childless, never saved, not
     sealed, not the saved version, and has a parent), `amend()` (the old
     job amend, its change the commit's own keys, `Cause::Amend`; netting to
     nothing goes back to the parent, `latest` the nearest of the group's
     before it) and `of_group()` ("{first label} (continued)").
     `revert_group(g, label)`: the group's versions on the line
     (`group_line`), their inverse prims applied newest first on a `Rec`
     with every before checked, coalesced by `Rec::finish` into one step of
     `ResolvedOp::Revert { label }`, then `merge(steps, made, ours, theirs)`
     with `theirs` the state before the group's first version on the line,
     `conflict` skipping the group's own versions; pushed as "Undo all of
     {label}" by the user, `Cause::Revert`, and the group ends.
     `rollback_group(g)` truncates when the group's only version is the
     current one and `amends()` holds, else reverts by the group's actor
     (`Cause::Rollback`), a saved version staying; `Ok(None)` with nothing
     on the line; a Conflict leaves the group live. Amends count their new
     steps' bytes only when their keys don't meet the version's (`join`,
     `step_bytes`, `steps_bytes`, `keys_bytes`). The app's OCR run holds its
     group and the run's start snapshot: each flush is `tx_at(base)`,
     `tx.read(Key::Page(p))` per page, `SetOcrText`, committed with
     `Validate` in the group; a Conflict retries page by page and counts the
     changed pages (", N changed during the run (their text wasn't added)");
     GroupEnded cancels the run ("OCR stopped: its results were undone");
     `end_group` on Finished and Aborted. History's version rows of a group
     (not undone, not damaged) have "Undo all of {label}".
   - **The history budget** (step 4). `HistoryStats.droppable`,
     `untrimmable_bytes()`, `HistoryPolicy::{could_act, prunes}`
     (`MemoryBudget::prunes` is `untrimmable_bytes() > budget`;
     `MemoryBudget::trim` stops at `droppable`). `trim()` weighs history
     only when the policy could act, prunes one version at a time while past
     `MAX_VERSIONS` or the policy prunes (weighing again after each), then
     drops snapshots. `prune_one()` takes the oldest leaf off the line,
     never the saved or a sealed one, else `advance_root()`: never past the
     current version or a sealed root, nor while a branch off the root holds
     a sealed version; it detaches the saved version when it's the root or
     on a branch going (`SavedVersion::{At, Detached(Box<Anchor { state,
     record, keys_to_root }>)}`, a version made in memory detaching to
     None), adds each new root's keys to a detached anchor, clears a group's
     `latest` it passes, and empties the new root's prims, its bytes counted
     again. `input` and `recovery_input` give path keys of `keys_to_root` ∪
     the root-to-v keys, the root's own edge left out; `saved_at()` is the
     in-tree id, and every reader of the saved version handles the anchor.
     `Held { snapshots, snapshot_bytes, step_bytes, undone }` is kept by
     `insert_version`, `take_version` and `set_state`, through which every
     change goes; `Version.on_line` is set by `move_to` along both sides of
     the path (`sides()`); and `stats_for`/`droppable` went over the held
     snapshots only, then (step 8) became one pass, `weigh`.
   - **The app's one door and one refresh** (step 5). `DocView::lower`,

   - **Planners and dialogs** (step 6). `DocView::run_planner(name, work,

   Deviations from the plan (the planner's list first, as resolved):
   - **Already done in slice 9:** `keeps_snapshot` for every version with
     saves (it keeps the root, the current, the saved and sealed versions)
     and older records reduced to `SaveNote`s; slice 12 extends the latter
     to the anchor, which the next save replaces.
   - **Relower resolves the ops again,** with position reads checked by
     value: an op whose resolve read the order (a position, positions, a
     span, every page, a bookmark's span, an `/NM` with no page) makes the
     transaction positional, and under `Relower` the base's order must equal
     the current one's, else `Conflict { key: Order }`. Conservative: a
     stale "rotate every page" after an insert conflicts. Each entry keeps
     its own drawn ids, so a relowered op draws its own even when an earlier
     one draws a different number now. Under `Validate` the order is in
     `seen` already.
   - **The Conflict's shape** is `Conflict { key, by }`, one slot and the
     label of the edit that changed it, where §6.4 has `Conflict { since,
     keys }`. A uniqueness or reference conflict names the other side's slot
     (the generator, annotation, node or page already there), so `by` names
     the edit that made the clash; an undo-caused one has `by: None`.
   - **The budget rule** is `untrimmable_bytes() > budget` (snapshots that
     must stay + steps + undone sources), where §8.7 has `step_bytes +
     blob_bytes`: `blob_bytes` counts every blob, the primary included, so a
     500 MB scan would have pruned all history. Slice 3's note gives the
     intent: what pruning frees. Versions are pruned first, one at a time,
     then snapshots trimmed, so the budget holds by construction unless the
     snapshots that must stay exceed it alone. `could_act` builds no stats
     when no policy could act.
   - **Anchors off the line:** the saved version also detaches when it's on
     a branch the root advance removes, so save, undo and new edits can be
     pruned; off-line leaf pruning never takes it, so a branch whose only
     leaf is the saved version stays until the root reaches its branch
     point, then goes whole. The enum is `SavedVersion`, since
     `model::Saved` is a slice-9 row. A saved version made in memory has no
     record and detaches to None (NoSaveRecord, dirty).
   - **Split counters:** `Doc.version` keyed the comments panel's and
     History's caches too, so it split into `changes` (every change) and
     `layout` (order, geometry, or a page now shown from another source
     page: `set_base` onto a same-size copy writes no `Geom` prim, and a
     layout's refs hold each page's source, so the geometry-only rule would
     keep drawing the old source). `Doc::new` fills `shown` from the model's
     pages, so the rule works from the first change.
   - **Plugin batches after the first** are committed at the current version
     in the group (`Base::Current`), joining the first's version: WIT
     0.2/0.3 batches arrive only at the end of a call, so only the first can
     be stale (§14.3's "the next Tx based on the committed version"). A call
     that read nothing commits its first batch at the current version too.
     The batches stop at the first failure: a call is all or nothing, where
     each batch landed or failed alone before.
   - **Slice 20 items done early:** docview's `edit_source` (a plugin's own
     edits told by `ChangeSet.actor`), "Reads record decision reads" for
     0.2/0.3, "built lazily from the cell" and `DocContext`'s per-call
     `Snapshot`; slice 20's list says so. Bug 27's version check, which
     slice 11 left here, is the first batch's decision reads.
   - **Watermarks aren't generators until slice 16,** so the "two watermarks
     of the same z" check is two header/footers from one base, and the rule
     is per (kind, place): a header and footer has no z.
   - **`Tx::read_render` is slice 13's:** OCR's and blank review's decision
     reads are `Tx::read(Key::Page(p))` on the snapshot their pages were
     rendered from, so a crop during OCR conflicts until slice 15 (ledger
     rows).
   - **Deferred:** `Tx::mark_handed_out`, `handed_out` and ChangeSet
     `depth`, which have no consumer until WIT 0.4 (slice 20); Relower still
     pins ids. Dialogs' rendered previews (slice 13): only the labels dialog
     has a model preview line.
   - **OCR's flushes commit on the model,** not through `DocView::commit`
     (§14.1 lists `apply_in_job` among the funnels that become one): the
     door's notice would replace the run's own each flush, and a
     page-by-page retry's conflicts (pages changed since the run began,
     left out and counted) would each be told as an error; OCR makes no
     bookmarks to reveal. Every flush's change still goes to `on_change`,
     so the one refresh holds; `DocView::commit`'s doc and
     docs/document-model.md say so. Found by the review (below).
   - **Additions:** `ChangeSet.label` and `Cause::Opened`;
     `ChangeSet::{empty, opened, is_empty}`; `CommitOpts::{labelled, based}`
     (the 13 `CommitOpts { label }` literals use `labelled`);
     `GroupKind::takes`, which makes a commit in a group by another actor
     `Internal` (so no group inserts pages, which need `Cap::User`);
     `DocView::{lower_in, forget_planners, lowering_now, undo_group}`;
     `Preview` without caps or consequences. From the review:
     `Snapshot.instance` (§8.5's "instance", a process-wide counter per
     `Document`, kept by `Tx` and `TxParts`), `Document.cut_groups`,
     `Imported.reads`, `Workspace::close_dialogs_of_another` and
     plugins.rs's `plugin_event`.
   - **Reads through `Rec`'s Deref aren't recorded** (`NextCopy`, the
     generators lookup, the cascades), so the post-merge check also scans
     page copies, and `resolves_after` (a reference check the plan didn't
     list) catches what a stale transaction's slots name that the current
     version no longer has: without it the 4,096-case property found a label
     range on a page deleted since.
   - **The `--script` Check** is the headless
     `each_transition_is_one_change` (the harness needs a display), plus the
     `"version"` and `"changes"` dumps and a recorded run.
   - **The sidecar skip key** is the `VersionId` alone: an amend mints an id
     now, so `edits` served nothing else.
   - **The cell holds a `Snapshot`, not `(Snapshot, LowerCx)`** (§14.1): a
     call's transactions are lowered with `lower_cx` of the plugin's actor
     when it lands. The cell is the `Doc`'s, one per document, and
     `land_call` checks `Arc::ptr_eq` against the view's current cell:
     `VersionId`s are counted per document, so a `Base::At(v)` from another
     document could otherwise land on one whose cursor is `v`. From the
     review the model refuses that too (`Snapshot.instance`), as a bug;
     the check keeps a call on a replaced document a plain refusal.
     `CallOutput.base` is an `Arc<Snapshot>`.
   - **Two plugin reads beyond §14.3's:** an update's `Annot(id)` (the
     0.2/0.3 patch keeps the base mark's tape rows, look and a 0.2 line's
     start arrow) and `page_text_layer`'s and a renderer's `Page(p)`. Frame
     mappings (`page_frame`, a Region's rect, an outline edit's frame)
     record nothing.
   - **Trim White** (the crop dialog's method) takes no explicit
     `read(Key::Page(p))`: `Validate` checks the before of every `Page` and
     `Geom` slot it writes, and the pages it doesn't rebase don't change.

   Found while building (each in its step's notes):
   - **Step 1:** `ChangeSet::of` looks a `Page(p)` slot up in both states
     only when `Key::Order` is among the keys (every page is in the order),
     a debug_assert checking presence;
     `a_page_s_slot_is_judged_by_whether_the_order_changed`, fault-checked;
     the 7,000-op OCR commit went from 7.45 back to 5.9 ms. `geometry` takes
     every `Geom(p)`, added and removed pages too; Saved changes go from and
     to the current version. A jump to the current version returns before
     touching `redo_to`. `Version.keys` counts in `step_bytes` unless it
     shares its step's set (4,254 → 4,257 MB on the 200-OCR bench before the
     budget).
   - **Step 2:** the op in an entry is unboxed
     (`#[allow(clippy::large_enum_variant)]`): boxed, the 7,000-op row was
     lowered 40.5 ms and committed 6.9; unboxed 39.6 and 6.31; with no
     entries 39.0 and 5.9. `TxParts` carries `base_state` and `cx`; its
     `actor` field is a method. Validate checks the first before of every
     key the steps write before coalescing, a key put back included. `/NM`
     and full-name uniqueness can't be reached by any op today (each add
     also writes `PageAnnots` or `Form`, which conflict first), so they're
     unit-tested on states built for them.
   - **Step 3:** an amend keeps its version's label (the group's first
     commit's, or "… (continued)"), and "(continued)" also follows a sealed
     or saved version (`an_amend_on_a_sealed_version_makes_a_child`,
     `a_group_never_amends_a_saved_version`). Revert and rollback end the
     group on success; on a Conflict it stays live and the caller ends it.
     Both are labelled "Undo all of {label}", a rollback's by the actor of
     the group's latest version. The amend's per-step byte count (700
     flushes went from 1,235 ms, 3.34 ms a flush at the end, to 79 ms,
     0.137): `accounting` dedups `Arc`s within a step, not a version, a
     documented over-count that leaves the 200-OCR bench unchanged. The OCR
     flush refreshes whenever the document moved, an amend that nets to
     nothing included. The History row's meta line is a flex row with the
     link.
   - **Step 4:** the cached undone bytes are cleared on every cursor move
     and whenever a version bringing sources comes or goes; per the spec,
     leaf pruning never takes the saved version.
     `pruning_keeps_the_saved_branch_whole` became
     `pruning_takes_the_saved_branch_last`. Two kinds of memory are
     uncounted by design: the values the root's state holds (only its
     marginal estimate counts) and the anchor's state; so RSS growth on the
     200-OCR bench (324–328 MB) is above the 256 MB estimate. `push` went
     from a walk of history to O(snapshots held): the last 100 adds 0.134 →
     0.040 ms.
   - **Step 5:** `on_change` schedules no autosave for `Opened` either, or a
     sidecar found at open would be replaced before the reader answers the
     Recover prompt. `refresh_history` stays for error paths: History's rows
     key on `(changes, is_dirty)`. A no-op commit and a revert with nothing
     to undo still emit one `Changed`. `DocEvent::Saved { path }` follows a
     save's `Changed`, since plugins' `saved` needs the path.
     `invalidate_tiles` bumps only `layout`. The notice's bookmark count is
     the O(1) `bookmark_count()` difference (ChangeSet has `outline: bool`
     only); `reveal_bookmarks` maps kid → parent from the commit's
     `Bookmark` keys, else `DocState::bookmark_place`.
   - **Step 6:** dialogs hand their snapshot over through `opened()` rather
     than in each event; `PlannedInsert` (not `Incoming`, a slice-11 row);
     the labels preview lowers on the UI thread at each render after a
     change (one `SetPageLabels` is cheap), "already" read from
     `Preview.effects.keys.is_empty()`; Remove Header & Footer from the
     dialog names pages by id; `forget_planners`, so a planner can't land a
     `Base::At(v)` on a recovery's document; the planner's start notice is
     its label and an ellipsis ("Insert x.pdf…").
   - **Step 7:** see the cell, the reads and the batches above; a
     pre-existing dead-code warning (`add_panel`) shows in the
     no-default-features build only.
   - **Step 8:** a push weighed history in two passes of four lookups per
     held snapshot (`droppable`, `stats_for`, `keeps_snapshot`): 20 µs at
     200 snapshots, so the blank 7k's last 100 adds took 1.8× its first 100
     (0.034 against 0.019 ms) and the new flatness gate failed. `weigh` is
     one pass with one lookup each (2 µs): 0.021 against 0.019 ms. It yields
     the same order and bytes, which `counted()` checks against an
     independent recount after every action of the history property; with
     the off-line and on-line halves swapped, the property and
     `a_run_applies_every_kind` fail.

     - *`Snapshot` has no instance* (two findings): true, and a dialog's

       `forget_planners` also drops blank review's pages, and the

       app's own guards.

       "changes elsewhere don't matter"*: true; both now say a rollback's
       edits stay once the user changed them, and that listing the pages
       reads their order.

       first fragment* (major): true, reproduced as described. Fixed with
       `Document.cut_groups` (a group whose version or first-kept prims
       pruning took): `revert` and `rollback_group` refuse it as
       `Invalid` ("older than the history kept"), and its rows offer no
       link. The history property's `REVERT` and `ROLLBACK` now check a
       landed one against every version the run saw made, pruned ones
       included (`Run.ever`, `taken_back`); with the check put back as it
       was, the 4,096-case run fails, and the same check then found a
       second path: `rollback_group`'s truncate of the only version left
       on the line, after pruning took the earlier one, also took back
       only part (shrunk to GROUP, two ops, PRUNE, GROUP, ROLLBACK),
       now refused too. `a_revert_of_a_group_pruning_cut_is_invalid` and
       `a_rollback_of_a_group_pruning_cut_changes_nothing`; eight 4,096-case
       runs pass.
     - *`connectors_on` makes the Append closure quadratic* (two findings):
       true, and worse: with the gate row the review asked for (a
       connector pair on every two pages of a 7k fixture, one group, every
       page turned, then the incremental save), the closure overflowed the
       stack, since each connector taken took its group again,
       recursing as deep as the group is long. `Deps` now takes a group
       once (`connected`, `every_connector`), which writes the same keys:
       the corpus counts, Append ≡ Rewrite at 1,024 cases and the DELETED
       tier hold. `append_rewrite_a_long_connector_group_is_taken_once`
       (2,000 connectors on a 1 MiB stack) aborts without it in debug and
       release; the gate row is informational (708–928 ms).
     - *The comment import decides without reads*: true; two imports of
       one file planned together both added its comments. `import` now

       destination page's `Geom` and `PageAnnots`, each comment updated)
       and `ops_in` reads them;

       fails without the reads.

   For Greg:

     undo step on the document as the call read it; a change by the user to
     anything it read (the pages it listed, a page's annotations, text or
     render, the outline) refuses the whole call, with "“X” changed the same
     data"; a later batch's failure takes the earlier ones back.
     docs/plugins.md and the 0.3 WIT doc say so; wit/0.2's doc, frozen until
     slice 20 deletes it, still says a batch each.
   - **What users see change:** an insert, crop, watermark, header and
     footer, labels change, blank-page delete or comment import planned
     while they edit lands on their edits, or says what it conflicts with
     and changes nothing; several can run at once, and Escape stops the
     newest; OCR results for a page cropped during the run aren't added ("N
     changed during the run"), until slice 15; undoing OCR stops it; History
     has "Undo all of …" for an OCR run or a plugin command, whose parts
     after an edit say "(continued)", until pruning takes part of it
     (then neither the link nor a failed call's rollback can take it all
     back, and a failed call says its edits were kept); long sessions
     keep within 256 MB, the oldest versions going (the History panel
     shows fewer of a long session's versions); a mark edit no longer
     lays the pages out again.

13. Done. Realizer, pool, render keys, view inputs (proposal 16; bugs 22
   and 24): PDFium draws the model. Each consumer passes what a page
   should draw (`ViewInputs`: the screen's, print preview's, OCR's
   `content_only`, a plugin's), and a page's `RenderKey` is a digest of
   what it draws under them, computed only for the pages drawn. The
   realizer sends a page that draws as its base page does (`untouched`,
   checked against the emission) to its source's base engine, and any
   other to its group's overlay: an in-memory append section over the
   source's bytes, scoped to the group's pages, written by the save
   emitter in a new overlay mode and the save serializer, encrypted with
   the source's key, numbered by an allocator a source; a damaged base's
   group is a file of its own, and a layers choice a catalog-only patch.
   One `EnginePool` thread serves every engine of the process (visible
   engines pinned, 6 group engines in 96 MB, a background budget of 2 in
   32 MB, liveness, failures remembered), in place of a `RenderHandle`
   thread a source. The app's tiles and previews are found by render key,
   a page keeping its last image until its new one lands; hiding is data;
   print preview, OCR, plugins, text and search, opening, inserts and the
   Header & Footer dialog's new preview draw through views. The hide
   replays, `drawn_marks`, `foreign_hidden`, the layers panel's decrypted
   copy, the GPUI header overlay, `drop_stale_images`, the global
   `invalidate_tiles` and `RenderHandle` with `Doc.handles` are deleted.

   accepted in place of the planned 1.7× its warm render (2026-10-20), the
   Rewrite is 1.13× and 1.11× slice 8's writer, and the corpus counts
   hold. Greg's rulings of 2026-10-20 are in (deviations): that gate,
   the pixel tier's anti-aliasing allowance, and a base PDFium refuses
   drawn from its realizations.
