   Deviations from the plan (the planner's list first, as resolved):
   - **Where the types live.** sheaf-render doesn't depend on sheaf-doc and
     sheaf-doc mustn't pull in PDFium, so `EngineKey`, `GroupKey`,
     `PageView`, `RenderKey`, `ViewInputs` and `Realizer` are sheaf-doc's
     (`realize`), `EnginePool<K>` is generic over its key, each request
     carries an opener and a liveness probe instead of a `Weak<Source>`,
     and the glue (`Views`, `ViewPages`) is sheaf-ops'. `PageView.index` is
     a `u32`. `(key, opener, budget)` are bundled into `Target<K>` (flat
     parameters put `search_page` past clippy's argument limit); the opener
     is an `Arc<dyn Fn>` a search walk can open again, and says whether
     its engine is a base engine (the pool can't read sheaf-doc's key).
   - **`Base::of` is retired** (slice 9); the overlay's base is the new
     `serialize::append::Base::over(&Source)`.
   - **`EmitScope::Pages` over a state.** `emit()` takes `&DocState` and
     the primary and derived table moved into `EmitBase::Rewrite` and
     `Saved`, rather than a detached `SaveInput` with a meaningless
     version; an overlay refuses a page of another source.
   - **The overlay always writes its pages** (a new `/Parent`), so the
     base-or-overlay choice is a model predicate (`untouched`) checked
     against the emission compared modulo placement, not "the emission
     writes nothing".
   - **Derived copies** (crops, watermarks, stripped headers until 15–17):
     an overlay over a copy takes the page as the copy has it, passing no
     derived table; the records draw its widgets, the copy's widget
     entries are left out (a widget outside the form on the original page
     isn't drawn there, which the Rewrite keeps: transitional, row 5660),
     and, from step 8, its form lists only the records' fields (Found).
   - **Spike outcomes:** A passed, so sections are encrypted with the
     source's key and no decrypted copy is made; B failed on damaged bases
     only, so standalone groups are for `!base_sound()` bases; C failed, so
     no box edit is drawn on a base engine and `JobXform` carries only the
     turn.
   - **Scoped groups, written out:** each page's four inheritable keys
     written and `/Parent` the group root, as §11.3 and §11.6 do; the
     AcroForm scoped more tightly than "the top-level fields with a widget
     on the pages": each node's `/Kids` cut to the scope, so a one-root
     form loads only the group's fields, in field id order.
   - **Deltas by `(PageId, RenderKey)`,** not `RenderKey` alone: a delta
     names its page's own keys, which a duplicate with the same key
     doesn't share; duplicates still share images. A group is emitted as
     per-page deltas plus a frame (`EmitScope::Frame`), since the group's
     root, catalog and form are built over all its pages; a source number
     claimed twice goes to the first, the other renumbered and read again.
   - **The heavy's realize gate is < 25 ms** (Greg accepted it,
     2026-10-20), asserted in the gates run as the synthetic's < 15 ms is
     (`REALIZE_GATE_HEAVY`, `Kind::realize_gate`); the row prints the
     ratio to the warm render as information. The plan's ≤ 1.7× the warm
     base render isn't met by any design that opens an engine for an
     edited page (slice 2: the heavy's scoped open and cold render alone
     are 2.9×). Greg: "it's more important to get it correct. we can
     optimize performance once the algorithm works properly" (Left for
     later). `the_heavy_realize_gate_as_planned`, `REALIZE_RATIO_HEAVY`
     and `REALIZE_PROPOSED_HEAVY`, which held the plan's ratio until he
     ruled, are deleted.
   - **The pixel tier's anti-aliasing allowance** (Greg, 2026-10-20):
     `realize_corpus`'s pixel tier passes a page when at most 16 pixels
     differ from the Rewrite (`ANTI_ALIASING_PX`). Its differences were 1
     to 9 pixels of PDFium's edge anti-aliasing, on pages whose dictionary
     and content streams are the same in both files, and which pages
     differ changes with what the process drew before (PDFium's caches),
     so they aren't sheaf's output. Past 16 fails as before; every page
     within it is printed (file, page, engine, count), and the class table
     says "N of M pages differ, K of them within the anti-aliasing
     allowance". `SHEAF_REALIZE_ONLY` (corpus paths, comma-separated)
     narrows a run by hand; unset, as the tiers run, every file is checked.
   - **A base PDFium refuses draws from its realizations** (Greg,
     2026-10-20). Why PDFium refuses 4422502: the file is a first revision
     whole (its catalog 2248, trailer `/Root 2248 0 R /Size 2250`, its
     table at 599,350 and its `%%EOF` at 644,504), then the tail of a
     second revision's table, its trailer (`/Root 2252 0 R /Size 2254`)
     and `startxref 600541`: the revision's objects 2250–2253 and the head
     of its table were cut out. `startxref` leads into the middle of the
     first table, so PDFium rebuilds the cross-references, takes the last
     trailer, finds no object 2252 and fails with `FPDF_ERR_FORMAT` (qpdf
     says the same: "recovered trailer has no /Root entry"); sheaf's
     reader rebuilds them and finds the catalog the file has. Moving that
     `startxref` to 599,350, or that `/Root` to 2248, makes PDFium open it
     (5 pages). `serialize::fixture::revision_cut_out` builds the same
     shape (a lopdf file, a trailer naming a catalog past every object, its
     `startxref` 20 bytes into the first table), which PDFium refuses the
     same way, so no test seam was needed. A file sheaf reads as sound can
     be refused too: more than 1,024 bytes of junk before `%PDF-` (sheaf
     finds the header anywhere, PDFium in the first 1,024 bytes alone), so
     a section or view patch over its bytes may be the first engine to
     fail. The behavior: the pool tells a source when an engine over its
     bytes fails to open with a load error (its base engine, its view
     patch, or a group's section over a sound base;
     `sheaf_render::OpenError::Refused`: any PDFium load error but a
     password, `Opener::on_refused`), at the open and at each request told
     of the remembered failure after (a second document on the same bytes
     learns it); the source keeps it for its life (`Source::base_refused`,
     `refuse_base`), costing nothing for files PDFium opens. Then no page of
     it is on its base (`on_base`): every page renders from its group, a
     file of its own (`assemble::standalone`, `realize::standalone`), the
     group's digest and the found-groups cache keyed by it, so an engine
     the pool remembers as failed isn't asked again under its old key. A
     render already asked of an engine over the source's bytes renders
     from the page's view found again (`Req::fallback`, a `Fallback<K>` the
     pool runs once on a refusal, which `Views::draw` gives every such
     view), by the same job; such an overlay asked for after the refusal
     by a view made before it fails as refused without opening
     (`Views::target`), so its fallback runs too. A section PDFium refuses
     over a base it reads would be drawn standalone too, unseen in the app;
     `realize_corpus`'s pixel tier fails on one instead. The consumers:
     the screen, the strip, print preview, OCR, plugins' renders and the
     Header & Footer preview all draw through `Views::draw`, so none sees
     the failure; a render key is what a page draws, not where from, so the
     image lands under the key the next frame's view has, and no blank
     image is kept. The notice at the form type's ask says the pages are
     drawn from sheaf's copy and Find and selection don't work on it.
     What reads the base engine or the file in PDFium still fails: its
     queries, printing, Remove Blank Pages and Trim White (For Greg).
   - **No `form_draw`; `foreign: bool` added; `print(markup: bool)`.** No
     consumer draws appearances alone on a shared engine (the flatten
     mutates the page), there is no `PrintOpts`, and print preview without
     markup and `content_only` draw no annotations, which no listed field
     could say. Whole classes go by render flags (`Draw { annots, forms }`)
     not overlay filtering: widgets draw only through `FPDF_FFLDraw`, and
     the matrix path with neither places pixels as the `FFLDraw` path does
     (`annotation_flags_draw_widgets_alone`, every rotation, tiles, A4).
     Overlays still write widgets whatever the flags.
   - **`content_only`** is the page's own content at its shown box, no
     annotations, generators or OCR; "over the whole MediaBox" is Trim
     White's (15). Blank detection and Trim White keep their own engines
     (`sheaf_ops::engine_for`, no threads) until 14 and 15.
   - **OCR's `PageSource`** takes the `OcrPage` (`text_len(&OcrPage)`,
     `render(&OcrPage, width)`, no rotation: `ViewPages` turns the page by
     its view), with one source a run; the adapter is a named struct
     (`ViewPages`), as a tuple impl breaks the orphan rule. `OcrPage` lost
     `source` and `render`; `OcrSource::recognize` and `RenderSource::render`
     take the call's snapshot and page; `TextSource` takes `&Src` (the
     pool's base target needs the source to open). sheaf-render moved to
     sheaf-ocr's dev-dependencies.
   - **Plugin text, search and recognize** read base-engine text until
     slice 14, so their reads are `render_reads(p, content_only)`
     (`Page(p)`); `page_text_layer` keeps `Key::Page(p)`; `render_reads` is
     a free function, since `HostState` isn't a transaction.
   - **The layout** holds no source page (`pane::Shown { id, geom }`) and
     is made again only on the order or a geometry; a same-size rebase
     changes keys only.
   - **Keys from per-Arc digests,** not `ChangeSet.content`: keys are
     computed for the pages drawn, and no cache is invalidated by a
     ChangeSet; position, count and Bates come from lazily built per-state
     tables (bug 24: the GPUI overlay computed every Bates number for each
     page drawn).
   - **Stamp and tape pictures** stay as they are (stamp_preview.rs renders
     a one-page in-memory PDF on an engine it drops; M10 slice 12 deletes
     them, D53): slice 6's "through the realizer" is met as not needed.
   - **The Mark record** isn't restructured before render keys read marks
     (slice 11's For Greg): keys digest marks only under `ByEngine`, as the
     record is, through its `AnnotKind`'s `Debug`.
   - **The form type** comes from a pool query on the primary's base engine
     at install (`ask_form_type`, `doc.forms.form_type`), and `open_time`
     went; a PDFium-only open failure is the document's notice at that
     first open ("The pages can't be drawn: …"), and `needs_password` asks
     only the model's reader.
   - **retired.rs** gains `QUALIFIED_ONLY` `handle`, `handles`, `primary`,
     `take_in`, `shown`, `index`, `render`, `base` and `input`, each with
     its reason, checked with probe files. The root `Msg` has no row: the
     ledger matches a one-segment row by a path's first segment, and the
     pool's own `Msg::Render` would hit it; `Msg::HideAnnots` and
     `Msg::SetHidden` are rows, and `impl PageSource for RenderHandle` is
     covered by `RenderHandle`'s.
   - **Pages listing sheaf's marks** in their own `/Annots` realize as
     overlays under `ByHost` even unedited, as §10.4 has it; the docs say
     so.
   - **Weights are an estimate**, the pool's (`OPEN_BYTES` + `PAGE_BYTES` a
     page loaded + the segments an engine alone holds), and the base
     engine's bound is cap-driven: it closes, pinned or not, only when the
     screen's engines pass 96 MB with nothing unpinned left and it weighs
     over 16 MB (a fixed 16 MB bound would reopen the heavy's about every
     166 pages, 0.7 s each). The gates measure RSS.
   - Further choices, each in its step's report: `Views::draw` (a view the
     caller holds, by a job as its engine draws it) and `Views::target`;
     `Doc.drawn` keyed by `(PageId, Rotation)`; image keys by the composed
     turn; `ocg_off` only once the Layers panel has chosen
     (`layers_chosen`); the pool a `OnceLock` in docview; the strip unpinned
     while its panel is hidden; `set_inputs` also in `follow`;
     `show_all_but` inlined into `ocg_patch`; a source's dead links in the
     key, and an `Order` read and the target page's `Page` read for a page
     drawing another tool's link (`LinkTo`); the
     predicate ignores a field's value (no save writes `/V` before M10
     slice 9) and compares boxes without the turn; `SourcePatch` only for a
     source with `/OCProperties`, an untouched page of a damaged layered
     base going to its group; standalone groups keeping four catalog keys;
     an inserted form's `DA`/`Q` pushed down in overlays as saves push
     them; the liveness probe a `Weak<Source>` (`Src::downgrade`,
     `upgrade`), the realizer's `Realization` without it; failed opens
     remembered in the pool (`Unopened`); Find,
     Patterns and selection in the screen's budget (the background's would
     reopen a 7k base engine every ~380 pages); print preview without
     markup leaving others' comments out (as `print_pdf` prints); the
     header preview's own realizer, no pins, marks not drawn; the thread
     test's baseline taken after a first insert and crop (lopdf's rayon
     pool starts once); `RenderRequest` kept as `Rendered.request`, its
     page and job alone (the review retired its format and priority).

   Found while building:
   - **The delta cache wasn't bounded** (step 8, step 3's code): `Part::
     weight` counted 128 bytes an object and nothing for its dictionaries'
     entries, the placeholders or the owned map, about 680 bytes a header
     page's delta against 11.1 KB of RSS each, so 32 MB "by estimate" held
     about 48,000 deltas, some 520 MB. The 200-groups gate's RSS row found
     it (317 MB added on the synthetic). `weight` now counts each object's
     allocations (`held`, `dict_held`: entries and index grown by doubling,
     each key and value, a chunk header an allocation), the vector's
     capacity, the placeholders and owned keys: 11.6 KB a delta by the
     estimate (14.7 KB on the heavy), and the cache at its cap holds about
     its 32 MB of RSS. `an_object_weighs_its_entries_and_what_they_hold`.
   - **A derived copy's group form listed every field of the file** (step
     8, step 2's code): over a crop's copy, `form::prepare` found the
     copy's form unmodeled (the records model the original's), so the frame
     kept the copy's whole `/Fields` (7,000 on the heavy) beside the
     group's own, and PDFium's form environment loaded all of them at each
     group's first page (0.6 s a group: the strip filled at 108 pages/s).
     An overlay over a derived copy now treats its form as the records'
     (`modeled`), listing only the scoped fields: 344 pages/s, the realize
     of a group 240 → 44 ms, and the cropped pixel test unchanged.
     `a_derived_copy_s_page_is_emitted_as_the_copy_has_it` checks the
     form's `/Fields`, and fails without the fix (fault-checked).
   - Steps 1–7's own (each in its report): the dead-link flag in the key
     and reads; `render_appearances`' inherited box; the overlay push-down
     of an inserted form's defaults; the forms-off matrix path needing no
     truncation fix; failed opens tried once.
   - **The predicate missed a widget's `/Parent`** (the review, step 3's
     code): `realize_corpus`'s predicate tier, run over every corpus form
     and under each consumer's inputs (the sample's 545 pool files had
     checked only a plugin's), found 136 page-and-inputs disagreements in
     9 forms (1822407, 0050247, 0056356, 2429543, 1538204, 1525600,
     1312748, 1062413, 0262114), each "untouched" where the overlay wasn't
     the base: a field a parent's `/Kids` lists whose own `/Parent` is
     missing or names another object (or one the parent lists under no
     `/Parent` at all). The model's tree comes from the `/Kids`, the
     emitter writes each `/Parent` from it, and PDFium draws a widget with
     what it inherits up the `/Parent`s, so such a page showed its base
     engine's drawing instead of the overlay's. `untouched` now checks
     each drawn widget's `/Parent` chain (merged, its field's) against the
     model's parents (`tree_kept`): 0 of 242,055 disagree.
     `the_predicate_agrees_with_the_emission_in_every_case` has the two
     shapes and fails without the check (fault-checked).

   For Greg:
   - **Decided: the heavy's realize gate is < 25 ms** (Greg accepted
     < 25 ms, 2026-10-20), asserted beside the synthetic's < 15 ms; the
     plan's ≤ 1.7× its warm render is no design's that opens an engine.
     Making it faster is a later perf pass's (Left for later).
   - **The synthetic's < 15 ms has little room on a loaded machine:**
     12.1 ms at a load of 1.5, 14.8 ms in a whole run started behind the
     workspace tests (Measured). Run the gates on a quiet machine; the
     same perf pass would widen it.
   - **`ViewInputs.foreign`** (others' comments and links) is new, **and
     there's no `FormDraw`**: whole classes are left out by PDFium's render
     flags; nothing draws appearances alone on a shared engine.
   - **`EnginePool` is generic** over its key, in sheaf-render, with the
     realizer's types in sheaf-doc and the glue in sheaf-ops.
   - **Deltas are cached by `(PageId, RenderKey)`,** images by
     `RenderKey`.
   - **Render flags rest on widgets drawing only through `FPDF_FFLDraw`,**
     proved pixel for pixel; `content_only` and `print(false)` draw no
     annotations by flags, not by smaller overlays.
   - **OCR reads a page's content alone** now: no widgets, comments or
     unsaved header (the app's OCR and plugin `ocr.recognize`), so OCR of
     form pages may change.
   - **Plugin renders draw sheaf's marks, the unsaved header and other
     tools' comments,** as the saved file will, in the file's orientation
     (docs/plugins.md); a render's reads follow what it drew.
   - **Print preview without "Comments and markups"** leaves other tools'
     comments out, as printing does.
   - **PDFium no longer gates the open:** a file lopdf reads and PDFium
     can't opens with a notice; the XFA-only form bar waits for the first
     engine's answer (milliseconds). When PDFium refuses the file (a load
     error, not a missing library), its pages draw from sheaf's copy
     (deviations; Greg, 2026-10-20), and the notice says so: "PDFium can't
     read this file as saved, so its pages are drawn from sheaf's copy,
     and Find and text selection don't work on it". Wording yours to
     change.
   - **A source PDFium refuses has no text yet:** Find, Patterns,
     selection, plugin text and OCR's "skip pages with text" read the base
     engine, which fails (OCR with that option on fails each page's text
     check; off, it recognizes them). Slice 14's text service reads text
     from realizations. Printing such a file fails too while print opens
     the file's path in PDFium (`PdfiumEngine::open(path)`, slice 14), and
     so do Remove Blank Pages and Trim White, which open the source's
     bytes in an engine of their own (`sheaf_ops::engine_for`; "PDFium
     can't read the file") until slices 14 and 15.
   - **The base engine reopens** once the screen's engines pass 96 MB with
     nothing unpinned to close (about every 1,256 distinct pages by the
     estimate), a 0.7 s pause on the heavy 7k; the heavy's base engine
     weighs about 35 MB once its form loads, against the 4 MB counted.
   - **One process-wide pool** counts every document's group engines
     against 6, and pinned ones are never closed, so two split documents
     can hold more; a `Base(blob)` engine is shared by documents opened on
     the same bytes.
   - **Two changes still don't conflict with a render read,** though they
     change the key: a generator added after the read (its id is drawn at
     random, so no read names it; adding the first header while a plugin
     decides from pixels lands beside it), and a link leading nowhere that
     a replace makes lead to a page again. Each needs a table-level key
     (all generators; the page map), which §6.3 doesn't have.

14. Done. Text service; print, preview and page images from bytes (bugs
   22 and 24): a page's text is read from what it draws, as its pixels
   are. PDFium's characters arrive in PageSpace with their angles, the
   16× device gone, and lines group in the direction the text runs. A
   `TextService` (`sheaf_ops::text::Text` over the views) reads each
   page's characters on the pool's worker from the engine and page its
   view renders from, under its caller's inputs, cached by render key,
   through a pool query that falls back as a render does; Find and
   Patterns walk the document's order page by page, each on its own
   engine. Find, Patterns, selection, calculator picks, text markup,
   plugin text, OCR's "skip pages with text" and blank detection all read
   through it, so inserted, duplicated, cropped, unsaved-OCR and
   unsaved-header pages have their text, and so does every page of a
   source PDFium refuses (slice 13's leftovers: its text, Find,
   selection, plugin text, OCR's check, printing and Remove Blank Pages
   now work; Trim White stays slice 15's). Printing sends its print file
   from memory (CUPS `lp -` on stdin, GDI `open_bytes`), and
   `PdfiumEngine::open(path)` is gone. The asserted 7k gates hold (the
   Rewrite 1.11× and 1.08× slice 8's writer), Find over 7,000 pages is
   measured (no gate), and the corpus counts hold.
   - **PageSpace text** (step 1, sheaf-render, sheaf-doc). `EngineChar {
     ch, rect: Option<Box2>, angle }` (`PageCharList`): PDFium's loose
     bounds as they come, PageSpace, no box for a generated character,
     the angle counter-clockwise. `PageChars::from_engine` takes `(ch,
     rect, angle)` with no `Geom`; `upright` is the quarter turn most
     boxed characters are drawn at (`most_drawn`: R0 with none, the
     lesser turn on a tie), lines grouped on `Affine::upright(upright)`.
     The `SCALE`/`points_to_pixels` code in `page_chars` is gone.
     `frames.rs`: `char_boxes_lie_within_a_sixteenth_of_a_point_of_
     pdfium_s` (every turned or offset corpus page) and
     `char_boxes_on_a_turned_page_off_the_origin_are_pdfium_s`
     (a lopdf `/Rotate 90` page, CropBox [36 48.5 560 740], a line across
     and one up the page), the three corpus drivers sharing `none_differ`.
   - **The text service** (step 2). sheaf-doc: `TextHit` moved to
     `page_chars` (the root re-export kept), `Query::{Literal, Pattern}`,
     `PageChars::find` and `text_len`, `TextService` and `TextOpts {
     inputs }`. sheaf-render: `EnginePool::query(target, page, fallback,
     f)` on a private `ask` (`Msg::Ask` carries the fallback; a free
     `fall_back` shared with `render`). sheaf-ops: `text::{Text,
     CHARS_KEPT}` (64 pages by render key, the first read the first let
     go), `Text::{new, chars, cached}`, `impl TextService for Text`;
     `Views::locate` (the render path's target, index and fallback, now
     shared), `Views::target` private, `views::answered`.
   - **Find and Patterns** (step 3). `EnginePool::walk(count, item, work,
     tx)` and `Walked::{Scanned, Done}` (`WALK_CHUNK` pages a turn
     between renders, each on its own engine, falling back as a query
     does, the engine of its last page held; a page whose item or work
     fails or panics passed over, logged), `EnginePool::opened`; `text::Found::{Hits, Scanned, Done}`
     and `Text::search`; the app's `Doc.text` (the screen's budget),
     `start_search`/`start_pattern_search` on it, `Hit::on(position,
     page, hits)`, `scanned` a count of positions. The gate harness's
     Find rows.
   - **Selection, calculator picks, markup, the notice** (step 4).
     `cached_chars` is `doc.text.cached`, `with_chars` asks `doc.text.chars`
     and reads a page again when its render key changed while it was
     read; `TextSel.chars` keeps the characters a selection was made in,
     which its paint, Copy, markup and Text Edits read (the review); the

   Deviations from the plan (the planner's list first, as resolved):
   - **`TextOpts { inputs: ViewInputs }`**, not §10.5's `{ fields }`:
     what a page's text is read under is the inputs it's realized with
     (§10.4), and §10.5's `fields` (fields' display text) is M10 slice
     14's. Plugin privacy holds without it: PDFium's text page never reads
     a widget's appearance (`plugin_text_leaves_field_values_out`).
   - **The trait carries `chars` only,** and the document walk is
     `Text::search`, a stream: §10.5's trait has `search` too, but the one
     caller that searches a whole document, the app, can't block, and a
     blocking per-page trait method on the worker would wait for itself.
     Both `Text::chars` (a receiver, the UI's) and `TextService::chars`
     (blocking) are named `chars`.
   - **One cache, by `RenderKey`,** where §10.5 has untouched pages cached
     by (source, index) beside realized ones: an untouched page's key
     digests its base page, so one cache serves both, and a duplicate or
     a page in another state that draws the same is read once. It holds
     64 pages, the first read let go first (a hit doesn't refresh), and a
     search neither reads nor fills it, so a 7k walk never evicts the
     screen's selection characters.
   - **`EnginePool::query`,** generic and public, with a fallback: the
     pool's `ask` was private and sheaf-render can't name `PageChars`, so
     `Text` builds them on the worker in a closure. It's built on a
     private `ask(target, Option<PageIndex>, fallback, f)`, since
     `form_type` loads no page; `form_type` has no fallback, so a refused
     file still learns of it there (the notice).
   - **Blank detection's text is read with recognized text** (`{
     ocr_over: true, ..content_only() }`), its pixels under
     `content_only()`: §10.4 says `content_only()`, but unsaved OCR text
     counted before and is the page's (recognized text is invisible, so
     the pixels are the same either way). A failed text read still counts
     as no text, the pixels deciding; pages are walked in document order,
     and the render's width comes from the page as it shows
     (`snap.geom(id).shown()`), the same for an untouched page.
   - **Plugin text reads under `plugin_text()`,** not `content_only`:
     §14.3 says text "as the file will draw it", so a call's text has the
     page's own text, the unsaved header and recognized text. It has no
     annotation's text (marks', comments', fields'): PDFium's text page
     reads a page's content, never an annotation's appearance, so
     `plugin_text()` is `plugin()` without marks, widgets or other tools'
     annotations, and its reads are that page's `render_reads` under it
     (`Page`, every `Generator`, and the order where a page-numbering
     header calls for it). The step's code read under `plugin()` and
     recorded `PageAnnots` and each drawn `Annot` too, which nothing the
     call saw depended on (the review); `recognize` keeps `content_only`.
   - **`lp -` without `--`:** CUPS reads stdin for the file `-`; every
     option before it is generated and `-t`'s title a separate value, so
     no `--` is needed (cups.rs passed `-- <path>` before).
   - **The export temp file was already gone:** `export::flattened` opened
     `print_pdf`'s bytes with `open_bytes` before the slice (the plan's
     export.rs:113), and the only file export writes is its output's, the
     TIFF through a same-directory `.part`, which atomic writes may
     (§10.6). The Delete was met before the slice; its Check is
     `printing_previewing_and_exporting_write_no_temp_file`, and a fault
     sending `flattened` through a temp file fails it.
   - **`upright` from the characters' angles,** not the page's `/Rotate`
     (`PageChars::from_engine` took the base's turn): the characters are
     then independent of `/Rotate` and the crop box (they're in
     PageSpace; the render key, and so the cache, still has the boxes,
     and a turn only where a generator is laid out in the turned page),
     and text running down the page selects a line at a time, ending
     slice 5's limit ("selects,
     picks and underlines a character a line"). Pages whose text reads
     upright as shown behave as before (`Affine::upright(r)` is `to_view`'s
     linear part for every r). PDFium's `FPDFText_GetCharAngle` turned out
     to be clockwise (text drawn up the page by Tm `0 1 -1 0` came back as
     270), so `EngineChar.angle` is (360 − PDFium's) mod 360; the fixture
     test pins it (fault F3).
   - **Matching is `PageChars::find`'s,** not `FPDFText_Find`'s. A
     literal is one regex, compiled once per search by `Query::literal`:
     the query's words escaped and joined by `\s+`, case-insensitive
     unless it matches case. So its words match where the page's are
     apart by any whitespace (a line break, two spaces, a no-break
     space), as `FPDFText_Find`'s did (it splits the query into words and
     takes any run of space, CR, LF or no-break space between them), and
     a phrase wrapped onto the next line is found, with a rect on each
     line; matches don't overlap. A pattern runs over the text as it
     reads (words apart by a space, lines by a newline), its byte offsets
     mapped to characters with its groups; a literal takes the same
     path. The step's literal compared the query's spaces with the
     page's characters one by one, so a wrapped phrase wasn't found (the
     review); the OCR layers' own search had that rule. The fix first
     matched word by word by hand; Greg's regex form replaced it before
     the commit (less code, one path with Patterns, and the regex
     crate's case folding instead of a per-character lowercase).
     docs/plugins.md says what a search matches.
   - **`PdfiumEngine::open(path)` is deleted,** not kept for tests: its 21
     test and example callers read the file and call `open_bytes`, as
     `open` did inside; the gate's two cold opens time the same work.
   - **`Views::start()`,** new: the CLI (no sheaf-render dependency) and
     tests make views over a pool of their own for blank detection.
   - **The notice** drops "and Find and text selection don't work on it":
     "PDFium can't read this file as saved, so its pages are drawn from
     sheaf's copy".
   - **Crops read from their derived copy's base** (the plan-vs-code note
     said a derived page is never untouched): until slice 15 a crop is an
     untouched page of the derived file, viewed as `EngineKey::Base` of
     that source; its text is what that file draws, equal to the
     original's within 1/16 pt.
   - **`EnginePool::walk` takes the caller's sender** (`tx:
     UnboundedSender<T>`, `T: From<Walked>`) rather than returning a
     progress receiver, so a page's hits, `Scanned(n)` and `Done` come in
     order on one channel; `work` returns a `Result`, logged like a
     failed item. The new walk keeps the name `Walk` (`Msg::Walk`), so
     retired.rs retires the old one's fields, not the name.
     `EnginePool::opened` (engines opened, counted in `Look`) is new for
     the gate's reopen count.
   - **`with_chars` reads a page again** when its render key under the
     screen's inputs changed while it was read, rather than handing back
     a stale answer or `None` (a pick saying "No number there" after an
     edit mid-read).
   - **Text in draw order:** a page with recognized text and a header
     selects as the page's own text, then the recognized words, then the
     header ("page 5\nTotal 42\nDraft"); `from_layer` gave an OCR'd page
     the layer's words alone.
   - **A selection keeps the characters it was made in** (`TextSel.
     chars`): characters are cached by render key, and the step's
     selection read them from the cache, so on a page whose key changed
     without its text changing (a foreign comment on it hidden or edited,
     a field typed into, a page deleted under a "Page <<1>> of <<N>>"
     header; a turn only where a generator is laid out turned) it painted
     nothing, Copy fell through to copying marks, U picked the Highlight
     tool, and a Text Edit's replace did nothing, until a hover read the
     page again (the review). `CharsKey` changed only with the source,
     index or OCR layer. A selection on a page whose text did change (OCR
     recognized under it) keeps what was selected; one on a page deleted
     still goes.
   - Step-level choices, each in its step's report: the frames check
     counts and skips characters drawn FAR (2^17 pt) or more off the
     page, which PDFium's i32 device can't map (106 on
     forms/safedocs/4427660.pdf, about 2^31 pt up, which only the
     every-page variant the review dropped reached; the moved-pages test
     skips none); OCR words checked inside the layer's word box within a
     quarter point (the Glyphless font's loose box reaches about 0.21 pt
     above a 14 pt word); `Text::cached` computes the render key directly
     rather than viewing; `runtime::TextMatch` and `text_match_to_wit`
     deleted too (their only producer was `TextSource`), and
     `text_layer::line_of` (only `hit_from_span` used it);
     `HostState::page_base` returns `(&DocContext, &Snapshot, PageId)`;
     the fixture plugin's `find` reports boxes; sheaf-ocr's `pdftext`
     example searches through `PageChars::find`; the idle-CPU test runs on
     every platform, its tick check Linux-only; the gate's Find rows one
     run each (a walk takes seconds); blank detection's header test uses a
     real header and footer (a 10 pt "Draft" alone is Blank by its
     pixels); `a_source_pdfium_refuses_prints` in realize.rs beside the
     other refused-source tests, checking a mark prints too;
     `pixel_format.rs` builds its page in memory; the app test's `TMPDIR`
     is unwritable (0555), so a temp file made and deleted fails it too;
     cups.rs's `said` shared by `run` and `send`; a plugin's text reads
     count against its call's time limit, unlike its OCR and renders
     (text has no per-call cap, so crediting it would let a loop over
     `page-text` run forever); retired.rs has no
     `sheaf_render::Rect` row (a one-segment row matches a path's first
     segment, and `geom::Rect::new` is called as `Rect::new`).
   - **Slice 8's "search over `ContentStack`'s text"** is met by reading
     realizations: the realizer draws the stack (the unsaved OCR layer,
     the header), so its text is the page's.
   - **Slice 5's leftovers for 14** (PageSpace text ending the 16× trick
     and the conversions where PDFium's text arrives, the base-frame line
     grouping, `merge_source_hits`, the plugins' `TextSource` frame) are
     done.

   The review of the slice's changes (15 findings, each checked against
   the code; fixed unless said):
   - **Find missed a phrase wrapped onto the next line** (major): the
     literal now matches `FPDFText_Find`'s way (deviations, Matching).
   - **Find Blank Pages reopened its base engine every ~380 pages**
     (major): blank detection reads in the background's budget, which
     held a base engine to its 32 MB like its group engines; on the
     synthetic 7k 19 opens in 13.1 s. Measured first (the new gate test),
     then fixed in the pool rather than in blank detection: the
     background's base engines grow into what the screen's engines leave
     of `SCREEN_BYTES` and close past it by the base engines' rule
     (`close_heaviest_base`, shared with the screen's), never the
     screen's own; their group engines keep 32 MB, and 2 engines in all
     still bound the count. 6 opens, 12.3 s, against 10.4 s for the old
     path's one engine and `page_text` (11.3 s with `page_chars`, which
     the slice reads; a throwaway test, deleted). The review's estimate
     of 12 to 13 s on the heavy doesn't arise: every page of the heavy
     7k has annotations, so blank detection reads none. The memory bound
     stays about the screen's 96 MB and the background's 32 MB: what a
     background base engine grows into the screen's engines no longer
     use.
   - **Find thrashed past pinned engines** (major in effect, found by the
     review's reading): with `SCREEN_ENGINES` pinned, the walk's group
     engine closed after every page; 6,232 opens and 37.5 s (synthetic)
     and 88.0 s (heavy) over the headed 7k with six groups pinned. A walk
     now holds the engine of its last page (`Worker.held`, by walk id):
     `close_lru` skips it, as it does a pinned engine, until the walk
     reads elsewhere or ends, and its end settles the budget again. 49
     opens, 12.1 and 9.0 s, as unpinned. A walk past six pinned engines
     holds a seventh, as a pin would.
   - **A selection lost its characters on a key change** (minor): it
     keeps them now (deviations).
   - **Plugin text was read under `plugin()`** (minor, with the notes'
     and the code comment's claim that marks' text was in it): now under
     `plugin_text()`, with reads to match (deviations).
   - **The notes misstated the turn and the crop** in the render key
     (minor): reworded here and in docs/document-model.md.
   - **`realized_glyphs` skipped a file whose `ready` failed** (minor): a
     failed `ready` is a difference now, and the 780,238 characters are a
     floor on the full corpus (`REALIZED_GLYPHS`). A file sheaf's store
     doesn't open, or PDFium refuses, is still not compared.
   - **The ignored every-page frames variant** (390 s) is dropped: a box

   For Greg:
   - **The refused notice** now reads "PDFium can't read this file as
     saved, so its pages are drawn from sheaf's copy". Wording yours.
   - **An unsaved header is text:** Find, Patterns, selection and the
     calculator read what the screen draws, so a header or footer not yet
     saved is found and selectable, and an OCR'd, headed page selects as
     the page's text, then the recognized words, then the header.
   - **Plugin text conflicts with header edits:** a call's text reads
     record what of the page the file will draw as text
     (`plugin_text()`): the page, every generator and, under a numbering
     header, the order, so an unsaved header's edit conflicts with a call
     that read the page's text (§14.3's "as the file will draw it"); a
     comment's doesn't, since PDFium never reads an annotation as text
     (the step recorded `PageAnnots` and each `Annot` too; the review
     dropped them). docs/plugins.md says so. Slice 20's 0.4 reads may
     narrow the generators to those that can come onto the page.
   - **Find is about 1.2× slower a page** than `FPDFText_Find` (Measured):
     11.4 s over the synthetic 7k and 8.0 s over the heavy as opened, 12.2
     and 9.1 s with a header on every page, on the worker between renders.
     A faster read (one FFI call for a page's boxes, say) is a later perf
     pass's.
   - **Matching is `PageChars::find`'s** (a literal is its words joined
     by `\s+` in one regex, case-insensitive unless it matches case, so
     a phrase wrapped onto the next line is found, as `FPDFText_Find`
     found it), for Find and plugins alike.
   - **Blank detection counts unsaved OCR text** (deviations), where §10.4
     says `content_only()`; recognized text saying "intentionally left
     blank" still marks a page so.
   - **A selection keeps the characters it was made in:** after an edit
     that changes how its page draws (a comment hidden, a page deleted
     under a numbering header) it still paints, copies and marks up as
     it was; after one that changes the page's text (OCR recognized
     under it) it keeps what was selected until a new selection.
   - **The pool's budgets changed** (the review): the background's base
     engines grow into what the screen's engines leave of 96 MB rather
     than its own 32 MB, and a walk holds the engine it reads on past the
     screen's count (a seventh beside six pinned). Find Blank Pages opens
     its base engine 6 times over the synthetic 7k, not 19, and Find past
     six pinned groups 49 engines, not 6,232. Both rules yours to change.

15. Done. Crop as geometry (proposal 27; bugs 16 and 28): a crop is a
   box edit of the page's `Geom`, one op (`SetPageBoxes`), with no copy.
   An Append of a crop writes the cropped pages' dictionaries alone, an
   OCR flush no longer conflicts with a crop of its page, and a cropped
   page realizes in its source's group overlay. Trim White is a resolve
   stage through the views on a measuring state, so it works on a source
   PDFium refuses and opens no engine of its own; the app runs it as a
   planner that measures again on a Conflict. The Crop Pages dialog
   previews its page through the realizer, on the Header & Footer
   dialog's preview, now shared. A crop of all 7,000 pages commits in
   9.6–9.9 ms, and in 14.6–15.7 ms validated after a delete (asserted
   < 200 ms on every fixture; 445–2,326 ms before M10.5), the strip still
   fills at the gate rate after it, and the corpus counts hold.

   Deviations from the plan (the planner's list first, as resolved):
   - **Trim White measures a state, not a new input.** §10.1 has
     `content_only()` draw "over the whole MediaBox"; slice 13 ruled it
     the page's content at its shown box and left the whole box to Trim
     White. A `whole_media` input would have reached the render key, the
     untouched predicate and the emission. Instead Trim White builds a
     measuring transaction at its snapshot that crops each page back to
     its file's own crop box and renders that state under the existing
     `content_only()`: the measurement never depends on sheaf's crop, and
     a page whose only change is its crop is untouched there (its base
     engine). Its decision read stays `read_render(p, content_only)`,
     which is `Page(p)`, as §8.5 says. `ViewInputs`, the key, the
     predicate and the emission are unchanged.
   - **The file's own crop box, not the whole MediaBox** (for Greg): the
     whole media box would show what the file's `/CropBox` hides
     (printer's marks, bleed), which Trim White would take for content
     and crop to about the media box. The own box is the base page's
     (`Source::geom(index).crop`, a fact of the source, not a read), the
     media box for a page with no `/CropBox`. Switching is one line in
     `measuring` (`geom.media` for `own`) and one test
     (`trim_white_stays_within_the_file_s_crop_box`).
   - **`BoxSpec`,** which §6.1 names but never defines, is
     `{ Margins(Margins), Rect(Box2) }`, kebab-case and
     `deny_unknown_fields`: margins off the visible box as the page shows
     after its `/Rotate`, as `crop::plan`'s were; a `Rect` in PageSpace.
     `Patch::Clear` makes the crop the media box and the other boxes
     absent.
   - **Invalid, never clipped:** §3.3's "a crop outside media is ignored"
     is how PDFium reads a file; §6.4 says an op fails and is never
     repaired. A `Rect` off the media box (± 0.01 pt), a non-finite value,
     a negative margin, or a box under `MIN_SIDE` on either side is
     `EditError::Invalid` naming the page; only float noise is clipped.
     `MIN_SIDE` is checked on the box as its caller states it (for
     margins, the kept box in the shown frame; for a `Rect`, its w and h),
     so conversion or noise clipping can't push an exact 18 pt box under.
   - **`MIN_SIDE` moved** from sheaf-ops' crop.rs to `geom::MIN_SIDE`, so
     it has no retired row.
   - **Deletes met before the slice:** "the forced rewrite for crops"
     (bug 13's id-based `removes_content` went in slice 10, and the
     planner's `Why` has no crop arm; the page-dicts-only Append tests are
     its check, since a derived crop's Append did write the copy's
     content); "its O(N²) id lookup" (bug 28: `crop::plan` already used
     O(1) `def()` lookups and `PageSel::Ids` resolves in O(n); it went
     with `plan`, and the 7k crop gate is its check); "the
     `generated::store` calls" (derived copies have been memory blobs
     since slice 3; only combine.rs calls it, which isn't crop's). "The
     pool engine each derived crop source took" went with the copy
     (text.rs's group assertion, and Trim White's 0 group engines at 7k).
   - **The gate's "crop all pages, the edit" row is gone,** with
     `Baseline.crop_edit_ms` (1.65, 1.70 and 1.71 ms, which a dead field
     would fail clippy on): it timed the edit apart from the copy, and no
     copy is left. "Crop all pages" now times what the dialog does (a
     transaction at the opened version, the op, the `Validate` commit),
     and "validated after a delete" the same after the user deleted the
     last page; both compare with slice 2's whole crop (`crop_ms`).
   - **Trim White re-plans at most three times** (`TRIM_ATTEMPTS`):
     nothing in the app re-planned before (`DocView::commit` returns the
     error and sets the failure notice), so the land matches
     `EditError::Conflict`, measures again on `model_snapshot()` with the
     ids still present and returns no notice, the new planner's notice
     replacing the conflict's; past three, or on another error, the
     commit's failure notice stays.
   - **Op JSON stays 1.0,** `schema/ops-1.0.json` regenerated in place
     (`SHEAF_SCHEMA_UPDATE=1`; it only grew, the boxes `Patch` with
     `serde(default)`): nothing is persisted until slice 19's `sheaf
     edit`. tests/ops.rs's envelope test used `set-page-boxes` as an op
     from a newer version; it uses `set-watermark` (slice 16's) now.
   - **Trim White can widen a margins crop:** it measures within the
     file's own box, so a page cropped too tightly by margins is trimmed
     back out to its content (`trim_white_measures_the_page_as_its_file_
     crops_it`), never past the file's box.
   - **An OCR flush during a Trim makes the Trim re-plan:** `read_render`
     records `Page(p)` by value, and `SetOcrText` writes it, so a flush on
     a page after Trim White measured it is a Conflict
     (`a_trim_conflicts_with_a_change_of_what_its_page_shows`), and the
     app measures again. A long OCR run could use up the three tries;
     none did in the tests.
   - **The retired row for `Derive::Crop` is `tx::resolve::Derive::Crop`,**
     not the instruction's `tx::Derive::Crop`: a definition is matched at
     its file's module path (resolve.rs), and a path naming it by its
     last two segments either way. `crop_dialog::CropContext::size` has a
     row too (the dialog takes the page's size from its preview);
     `size` is already qualified-only.
   - **The Trim White gate rows** run on every fixture, the document
     cropped first so each page takes a measuring op. Since the review
     they're alone in `trim_white_on_the_7k` (each fixture in a process
     of its own, `run_parts`' "trim" part), not in `gates()`: a first,
     untimed walk counts the group engines it opened through a progress
     that looks at the pool's open engines at each page (`GroupsOpened`,
     a round trip to the worker a page), reading every page's facts cold
     as the app has by the time it trims; the second, timed with
     `NoProgress`, is the planner's alone and must find the same.
   - Step-level choices, each in its step's report: `Margins` moved to
     sheaf-edit's page.rs (a page-level type now); every box's margins
     come off the page as it showed before the op, so the four fields are
     independent; `set_boxes` records `Geom(p)` as a lowering read for
     every page, not only those it writes (the result depends on the
     page's boxes and turn); a run of crop clears is one line too
     ("Remove the crop from N pages"), a mixed run "Change the page boxes
     of N pages"; group_tests' `flush` helper reads `read_render(p,
     content_only)` as the app does (the same `Page(p)` read); the old
     Derive::Crop stale test went and step 1's SetPageBoxes test took its
     name (the rebase checks stand in `two_pages_shown_as_one_copy_of_a_
     page_conflict` and `a_dialog_on_v_keeps_an_ocr_amend_of_v`, now
     StripHeaderFooter); the dialog's `request()` (the plan's `spec()`)
     returns `crop_dialog::Request`; `TRIM_PAD` lived in crop_dialog.rs
     (the review moved it to `sheaf_ops::crop::PAD`);
     Trim White's label is "Crop N pages" for the pages it actually crops,
     and a trim with no crops still commits its empty transaction, so a
     stale measurement still conflicts; `draw_preview` takes `scale` and
     returns the cropped page's size, since a crop changes the aspect;

     open), `request()` keeping the "Every margin is zero" refusal; the

   Found while building:
   - **`sheaf_edit::tape::fmt_amount` panicked on a huge `decimals`**
     (step 1): two new `every_op` fixtures shifted the deterministic fuzz
     test's stream, and `fuzz_bodies_survive_mutated_fixtures` found a
     tape mark with `decimals: 4294967295` (from Op JSON, or a file's
     `/SheafAnnot`): `decimals as i32` wraps to -1 and divides by zero,
     and uncapped it would pad a 4 GB string. `fmt_amount` caps the
     places at the new `tape::MAX_DECIMALS` (15), with a test; the op
     isn't refused, only its display bounded, which protects files with
     such a mark too. No seed: the fuzz test is deterministic.
   - **An op's `Rect` doesn't round-trip every `f32` box** (step 2): a
     `Rect` carries a corner and a size, and the stored crop is
     `Rect::new(x, y, x + w, y + h)`, so where `x0 + (x1 − x0) != x1` in
     `f32` the measuring crop differs from the file's by about an ulp, and
     that page is drawn from its group overlay (the same pixels, a group
     engine's cost) rather than its base engine. About 2% of random
     decimal boxes; nudging w by an ulp fixed 1 of 4,335. Only pages sheaf
     cropped, with inset decimal `/CropBox`es, are affected; integer boxes
     and media boxes from the origin round-trip. An exact fix is a
     corners form of `BoxSpec::Rect`, an op-schema change for Greg.
   - **A fault check passed on a corner** (step 2): with the cropped-half
     test's crop keeping the page's top-left corner, the snapshot's
     `from_view` matched the measuring state's, so mapping through the
     snapshot's cropped geom passed; the crop now hides the top and the
     square's left half, and that fault fails.
   - **A fault slipped past the corpus tier on arrays** (step 6): the
     emitter writing a page's `/Contents` anew on a box change, done for
     a single reference only, passed on 3 sampled files whose `/Contents`
     is an array; widened to arrays, 15 of 29 sampled files fail ("not
     pages").
   - **One `SHEAF_CACHE_DIR` a test process** (step 6): every test in a
     binary sets the same shared value, and opening a file writes to the
     cache (file.rs converts other tools' `/Stamp`s through
     `import::convert_page`, which calls `generated::store`), so "no cache
     file" can only be seen in a process of its own:
     `common::own_cache(test, body)` re-runs the binary for that test with
     an empty cache directory and asserts it's still empty.
   - **`Crop` is a live name** (step 7): the retired rows for
     `Derive::Crop` and `CropEvent::Crop` hit describe's `Boxes::Crop`
     pattern (step 1's) by its last segment, so `Crop` is qualified-only,
     with its reason; both rows still hit their definitions and paths.

   The review of the slice's changes (12 findings, each checked against
   the code; fixed unless said):
   - **A derived flow uncropped its pages** (blocker): `set_base`, which
     Watermark / Background and Remove Header/Footer still use until
     slice 17, replaced a page's `Geom` with its copy's file geometry,
     keeping only the turn, and the watermark was placed on the copy's
     uncropped page. Before this slice the crop was baked into the copy's
     `/CropBox`; now it lives in `Geom` alone, so a watermark on any page
     dropped every rebased page's crop (and trim, bleed and art boxes).
     `set_base` now keeps the page's `Geom` whole (a copy is made of the
     page's base, with its media box and user space) and no longer writes
     it, and reads `Geom(p)`, so a flow planned before a crop made since
     conflicts (as its write over `Geom` did before); `derive::watermark`
     places the mark on each page's state `Geom`, its crop. Test:
     `a_derived_flow_keeps_the_crop` (above). Three sheaf-doc tests set a
     `/CropBox` in a derived copy and expected the page to show it; no
     derived flow changes a copy's boxes now, so untouched_tests' and
     materialize/tests.rs' `copied` make plain copies, and
     `a_derived_page_is_written_as_its_original_object_with_derived_
     content` and overlay_tests' `a_derived_copy_s_page_is_emitted_as_
     the_copy_has_it` keep the copy's `/CropBox` and assert the written
     page has the page's own boxes (no `/CropBox`), not the copy's.

     boxes** (two findings, one fix): its "no op" was decided by its

     since landed under Validate unseen, where a page it crops conflicts.

   For Greg:
   - **Trim White measures within the file's own crop box,** not the
     whole MediaBox §10.1 and the slice 13 and 14 notes said: the whole
     box would take what the file's `/CropBox` hides (printer's marks,
     bleed) for content and crop to about the media box. Switching is one
     line in `crop::measuring` and one test (Deviations).
   - **Op JSON stays 1.0** with `ops-1.0.json` regenerated in place (it
     only grew; nothing is persisted until slice 19). A minor bump would
     change the envelope and schema tests.
   - **A `Rect` box is a corner and a size,** so about 2% of decimal
     `/CropBox`es don't round-trip exactly in `f32` (Found); such a page
     measures from its group, with the same pixels. A corners form of
     `BoxSpec::Rect` would make it exact, at the cost of a schema change.
   - **Trim White re-plans at most three times;** an OCR flush on a page
     it measured makes it re-plan, so a long OCR run beside a Trim could
     use them up (the notice then says it changed the same data).
   - **Trim White at 7,000 pages takes 38–41 s** on the synthetic and

16. Done. Watermark, background and strip (proposals 30, 31 and 39; bugs
   16–18 and 28): a watermark or background is a generator, set and taken
   off by ops, laid out upright on each page's own boxes when a save
   writes the page or a view draws it, written as marked blocks around
   the page's isolated content, and found again when the file opens. It
   replaces what Acrobat, an older sheaf or another file drew of its kind
   and leaves the author's, and Remove Watermark says what it found by
   who drew it. A Clean Copy takes an older sheaf's settings out of what
   it drew. The derived copy, `watermark::install` and `read`, the
   per-page resources, the `/SheafWM*` names and `SheafSettings` writing
   are gone. A text watermark and an image background on 7,000 pages add
   one image, one font and one graphics state to the file and a
   resources dictionary for each distinct one the pages had (asserted on
   every 7k fixture); the strip fills at 413 and 344 pages a second with
   a watermark on every page (asserted ≥ 310), and the corpus counts
   hold.

   Deviations from the plan (the planner's list first, as resolved):
   - **The watermark carries its own z, `Scope` and `replaces`**
     (`GenSpec::Watermark(Arc<WatermarkGen>)`), and `Generator`'s
     accessors read them as §3.5's fields would be: hoisting them now
     meant rewriting about 40 header sites slice 17 rewrites anyway.
     `scope()` is a `Cow<Scope>` (the header's made from
     `HeaderFooter.pages`), `z()` is `Over` for the header, and
     `replaces()` none for it, its derived copies still stripping. A
     transitional ledger row (16 → 17) says so.
   - **An op names its file by `BlobSel`, optionally.** An op can't hold
     a `BlobRef`, so `Image { image }` and `Page { pdf, page }` take a
     `BlobSel`, resolved to `ImageRef::Blob` / `PageForm::Blob` as
     `NewMark.asset` is; a wrong kind is Invalid, a page past the end
     NotFound. Since step 4 both are `Option<BlobSel>` (`page` defaulting
     to 1): none keeps what the watermark at that z draws now, the only
     way to move a reopened image without embedding it again; nothing
     there is Invalid ("no image is drawn at its z to keep"). The schema
     changed by relaxations only.
   - **`FontChoice`, `GridPos` and `Z`,** named but never defined, are
     sheaf-edit's: `Z` and `GridPos` in watermark.rs, `FontChoice`
     beside `Color` (slice 17's `HeaderFooterSpec` takes it too), all
     `deny_unknown_fields`. Defaults: center, helvetica-bold, angle 0;
     an image's or page's scale is of the page's width (the legacy rule),
     in (0, 2].
   - **One `GenId`,** `content::blocks`', re-exported from `model`, so
     both paths stay valid and retired.rs has no row for it.
   - **1.4, not 1.7** (for Greg): §11.7 says artifact subtypes need 1.7,
     the slice's Check and `PdfVersion::ARTIFACTS` 1.4; the code follows
     the Check. ISO 32000-1 Table 330 marks `/Subtype` as PDF 1.7.
   - **`replaces` and Remove take Acrobat's, an older sheaf's and another
     file's** ({Acrobat, SheafLegacy, Sheaf}, `PagOrigin::REPLACED`), not
     §11.4's Acrobat alone: the old derived flow stripped every
     non-authored artifact of its kind, and an inserted sheaf file's
     unbacked watermark would draw beside ours. Backed blocks are set
     aside anyway (`Pagination::generator` keeps them out of counts).
   - **A page whose content can't be read gets no watermark** (for
     Greg): §3.4 fails the op that needs isolation, but SetWatermark
     lowers in O(1) and `All` covers later pages, so the page is written
     and realized without it, with one save Note naming the pages, and
     emit stays total. A `replaces` cut the splice refuses stays, with a
     Note too.
   - **The backed rule:** a block is backed when its `/G` is a
     generator of the state that covers its page, or, on a page of the
     opened primary (or a derived copy, until slice 17), a generator of
     the state or one recognized from the primary (`DocState::backs(g,
     page)`; the page-aware half is the review's). Backed blocks are
     always set aside, so a generator gone by Remove, a cascade, an
     extract, a Clean Copy or a print leaves none; unbacked ones
     (another file's, inserted, an earlier save of the same file's among
     them, since a `GenId` lasts across saves) are kept until a filter
     drops them, and isolation stays on pages that keep one.
   - **Recognition reads more than stream markers** (the review): a
     page with no block in a stream of its own, whose resources name a
     list with `/SheafGen`, has its ranges read (`Source::blocks`) for a
     block another tool merged into a stream, so a `pages` scope keeps
     that page and an Update re-lays it (§3.5); only such pages are
     read. An `all` generator that a page whose content can be read
     holds no block of (a page another tool added) is recognized as
     `Pages` of the pages that hold one, with a log line, so the screen,
     an Append and a Rewrite agree; a page that can't be read keeps
     `All`, as sheaf never drew on it. An image or page still binds
     only from a block in a stream of its own.
   - **SetWatermark keeps the replaced generator's `GenId`,** as
     `set_header_footer` does, so recognized blocks stay backed and an
     equal `/L` is used again.
   - **Effects by recipe:** a change of text, image or page, or a
     removal, is `REMOVES` (`REPLACES_TEXT` for text); a layout-only
     change is `CONTENT` and may append. Beyond §7.1, a watermark that
     leaves a page still in the document is `REMOVES` too, as Remove's
     narrowing is; `All` → `Pages` counts as narrowed when a page of the
     saved order is off the new scope; a page that left by being deleted
     isn't counted; a z change is layout. `RemovedKind` gained
     `Watermark { text }` and `Background { text }`, a text one reading
     as the header does ("1 watermark changed").
   - **StripLegacy came early** (for Greg): Clean Copy is slice 19's
     RemovePrivateData in the design, but the Check needs a Clean Copy
     without `SheafSettings`. `Filter::StripLegacy(LegacySel::Marked)`
     rewrites the inline lists of an older sheaf's watermark and
     background ranges without `LEGACY_KEYS`, lexically (comments,
     spacing and nested dicts kept byte for byte) and safe or refused (the
     result must read back as the list less the keys); a named list, one
     across streams, a non-name key or non-object value, or no `BDC` is
     refused and kept, with a Note. `LegacySel::Stream`, named lists'
     `/Properties` and renaming `/SheafWM*` are slice 19's. Print and
     page images without markup strip them too (`without_markup`, §16
     row 27). Adding the filter is `CONTENT | REMOVES` as
     `RemovedKind::OlderSettings`, so an Append can't leave the path in
     an earlier revision. A clean copy's former legacy range reads as
     `Authored` afterwards.
   - **`HeaderKept` and `derived_copy`'s `header` went,** their one live
     caller `derive::watermark`; the header-keeping copy tests ported to
     plain copies, and materialize/tests.rs's derived-copy case of
     `the_header_is_drawn_once_and_not_again_where_the_base_draws_it`
     (with `copied`) dropped, since no flow makes such a copy. `fix` lost
     its `&Geom` too.
   - **`stamps::strip` and `stripped` are header/footer-only;**
     strip_artifacts.rs, rewrite_tests.rs and content/corpus.rs ported,
     the last onto `PageBlocks::selected`, which `MarkedSel::Pagination`
     matches through.
   - **Keys** as their writers came: `ObjKey::Generators` (a root, as
     Labels and AcroForm are), `PageRes { base: u128, dropped: u64,
     added: u64 }` (the plan's `Option<ObjRef>` isn't `Copy`; three

     the legacy installers' unmarked `q` is an `ObjKey::Res` by digest,

   - **`BlobKind::Image(ImageFormat)`,** liveness by `BlobRef`.
   - **PageForm through a PDF:** the chooser takes a PDF and draws its
     page 1 (`Art::Pdf`); `model::PageForm` and stamp_lib's are
     qualified apart.
   - **`a_derived_flow_keeps_the_crop`'s watermark half:** a watermark
     planned before a later crop now lands (it reads no `Geom`), keeps
     the crop and is centred on it; a further crop and save re-centre it.

   - **Remove is a planner** (`run_planner`, `Actor::User`, `Validate` on
     the dialog's version), not a job; its per-origin counts and
     unreadable pages are computed at lowering into
     `ResolvedOp::RemoveWatermark.others` (`tx::OthersFound { acrobat,

   - **Layout from `Geom`** with the generator; `PageCtx` comes with

   - Step-level choices, each in its step's report:
     - Step 1: an empty `Pages` scope is Invalid ("the watermark is on no
       page") and an invariant; text is trimmed before the empty check;
       `remove_watermark` reads `Order` when it narrows `All`
       (`remove_header_footer` has the same hole, slice 17's); the replay

       `read_bytes` refuses a type it doesn't read before decoding.
     - Step 2: the property list is named `/Sh<base32>` like every added
       resource (`ContentWriter::fresh`), not `/ShP<n>`; `/L` and `/R`
       are 16-byte hex strings, `/G` a literal `g<hex>`; the JSON escapes
       all non-ASCII; added names clear of every name the base binds (a
       superset, pruning narrowing it from step 4); `Cx.arts` keyed by
       `(BlobId, Option<index>)`, not `Cx.stamps`; one Note for all
       unreadable pages (`describe::pages_text`, crate-visible);
       `SaveRecord.drawn` stays empty until slice 17.
     - Step 3: the PDF/A Note counts the legacy header too, a Rewrite
       every generator, an Append those its path changes; an overlay
       drawing generators but not OCR keeps the file's OCR layer; a
       covered page whose content can't be read isn't untouched; the
       census uses an Over text and an Under image at one opacity, so one
       ExtGState is checked across both; `source::tests` and
       `materialize::watermark_tests` crate-visible for their helpers.
     - Step 4: `Source::generators()` returns `&Arc<[Saved]>` and never
       fails (a source makes neither `ObjRef`s of itself nor `PageId`s),
       `Saved::generator` making the record at ready; `opened_generators`
       in the state, read through `backs`, and the key feeding the backed
       ids a base holds; `Placed { at, res, turns }`, the JSON `{"placed":
       "<ResId>", "turns": n}` (`v` stays 1; without turns a Placed JPEG
       drew sideways, without the id an unchanged image never laid out
       alike); covered-but-empty checked with a hand-emptied block;
       `intact` the shared rule, the realizer never decoding a store image
       for a digest; content_only views set backed blocks aside too;
       Remove's `DropMarked(SheafGen)` for merged ranges either way,
       `DropStreams` for unbacked streams; filters compared only while
       the base is the same; markers read for Derived blobs too.
     - Step 5: the cut goes with drawing the generators, so not under
       content_only (OCR can read a replaced Acrobat watermark's text);
       the classify row reads the blocks in `judge` only, so a step's
       History badge doesn't flag a replacement, the save plan does;
       another file's block of a replaced kind is left out whole; step
       4's refused `DropMarked` ranges count toward the Note; `in_forms`
       may over-report (the fact isn't per kind); Remove's origins only
       where a splice takes a range; the `foreign` recognized test uses a
       background, and a `replaced` test covers no doubling; the ignored
       tier allows StaleSignature, StaleSigFlags, XfaMismatch and
       EarlierValues, which these saves are told to cause.

   The review of the slice's changes (19 findings, each checked against
   the code; fixed unless said, each fix's test failing with the fix
   switched off):
   - **A file held as an attachment never drew as a watermark** (major):
     `Store::intern` hands back a live blob with the kind it was first
     interned as, and resolve judged that kind, so a PNG or a PDF already
     attached was Invalid. An image is an image, and a page a PDF's, by
     their bytes now (`BlobKind::image`; the PDF parsed).
     `a_file_held_as_an_attachment_draws_as_a_watermark`.
   - **A watermark found and removed came back in copies** (major):
     `subset` and `without_markup` built their states without the opened
     generators, so Clean Copy, extracts, prints and page images kept
     its blocks. `Builder::opened_as(st)` carries them.
     `a_found_watermark_removed_is_gone_from_copies`.
   - **A page another tool added under an `all` watermark** drew it on
     screen and in a Rewrite but not in an Append (minor): recognized as
     `Pages` of the pages holding a block (Deviations).
     `a_page_another_tool_added_has_no_watermark`.
   - **A merged block dropped its page from a `pages` scope** (minor), so
     an Update left the old drawing there: found by its ranges now
     (Deviations). `a_merged_block_keeps_its_page_in_scope` (both ways).
   - **An earlier save's page lost its watermark** (minor): `backs`
     matched the id alone, and a `GenId` lasts across saves; it reads the
     page now (Deviations). `a_page_from_an_earlier_save_keeps_its_
     background` (both ways).
   - **`replaces` was taken from the JSON unchecked** (minor): an entry
     whose `replaces` isn't its z's kind is passed over, and a found
     generator's is built from its z. A case in
     `what_sheaf_wouldn_t_write_isn_t_found`.
   - **An isolating stream was trusted by its dictionary** (minor, two
     findings): the rebuild set a stream marked `/Isolate` aside and the
     removal check said nothing of it whatever it held. One that holds
     more than `q`s or `Q`s (`content::isolates`, moved from the
     emitter) is the page's own content in both now.
     `an_isolating_stream_that_draws_is_the_page_s` (both ways) and
     removal_tests' `an_isolating_stream_that_draws_is_read`.
   - **A file whose catalog lost `/SheafGenerators`** (minor): the
     rebuild took its markers from `Source::markers`, which reads none
     for such a file, so a replacing watermark wrote its old block as an
     empty `Filtered` copy and nested the content once more. The
     rebuild reads each stream's marker from the dictionary it decodes
     anyway; `stack` and `intact` keep the catalog's O(1) gate.
     `blocks_a_catalog_doesn_t_name_are_left_out_whole` (both ways).
   - **Every Append decoded the image** (minor, two findings):
     `/SheafGenerators`' JSON, which needs an image's digest, was made
     before the Append knew it wrote it; it's made only then, the
     decision taken from whether any watermark is set. The bytes written
     are the same. `an_append_that_draws_nothing_makes_no_image`
     (`ARTS_MADE` 0 for a comment's Append, 1 for a move's).
   - **Background… with the Watermark dialog open closed it and opened
     nothing** (minor): the menu item toggles only its own z's dialog,
     and the other's closes as this one opens. No test: no headless
     test builds a `Workspace`.
   - **Setting the same watermark again said "Watermark"** (minor): it
     says "No change to the watermark" ("… background"), in
     `a_watermark_is_one_undo_step`.
   - **A rebuild digested a reopened page's layout three times**
     (minor): the rebuild uses `intact`'s digest; `drawn`'s layout is
     left for the perf pass (Left for later slices).
   - Quality: `a_pdfium_resave_keeps_the_watermark_found` removes its
     scratch directory (`watermark-resave`); untouched.rs' and

   For Greg:
   - **1.4, not 1.7:** a watermark needs `%PDF-1.4` here, as the slice's
     Check and `PdfVersion::ARTIFACTS` say; ISO 32000-1 Table 330 marks an
     artifact list's `/Subtype` as 1.7 (Deviations).
   - **`replaces` takes Acrobat's, an older sheaf's and another file's**
     of its kind, not Acrobat's alone (Deviations).
   - **Notes a save gives, wording yours:** "No watermark or background
     is drawn on page 3, whose content can't be read."; "1 watermark or
     background other programs or files drew stays on page 1: taking it
     out would change what else the page draws."; "1 watermark or
     background an older sheaf drew on page 1 keeps the settings it kept
     in it, which can't be taken out of it as it's written."; "This file
     claims PDF/A-2b; the watermark sheaf draws on it isn't made to
     conform, so the saved file no longer does".
   - **The backed rule** (Deviations): another file's sheaf watermark,
     inserted, stays until a filter or a `replaces` of its kind takes it,
     and so does an earlier save's of the same file on a page the
     document's watermark of that id doesn't cover; a page inserted from
     the very file the document opened is the document's, its blocks
     backed, as a duplicate's are.
   - **Dialogs show no counts** (proposal 31 and D61 say they do; the
     review): Remove's counts of others' artifacts are said only in its
     notice once it lands, and Set's never before the save, where a
     replacement shows as `Removes([Filtered n])` (a step's judging
     reads no blocks, so its commit says nothing of them). Counting the
     selected pages' replaced artifacts off the UI thread for the
     dialog, as Remove's planner does, is left; recommended with slice
     17's header dialog, which needs the same count.
   - **A page watermark comes from a PDF's page 1** in the dialog; the op
     takes any page.
   - **StripLegacy came early** for Clean Copy's Check; after a clean
     copy an older sheaf's range reads as the author's, so `replaces` and
     Remove leave it unless asked; one Word list in the corpus can't be
     rewritten (it crosses streams), and an older sheaf's always can.
   - **Remove's line and the app's notices:** "Remove the watermark from
     pages 1, 2 (2 made in Acrobat; 12 the author's left in place)",
     "No watermark to remove"; the Remove button always shown, removing
     from every page; the menu item toggling the dialog; the ported
     conflict test's "Strip" label.
   - **OCR reads a replaced Acrobat watermark:** the `replaces` cut goes
     with drawing generators, so under `content_only` an Acrobat
     watermark ours replaces is still the page's, and OCR can recognize
     its text.
   - **The manual Acrobat round trip** (Asks): open a file sheaf saved
     with a watermark and a background in Acrobat, see both drawn, edit
     Acrobat's own watermark there, save, and reopen in sheaf; whether
     Acrobat keeps or drops our marked blocks and `/SheafGenerators` is
     still inferred (PDFium's SaveAsCopy keeps them, the ignored test).

     realize_corpus's inventory name) taught it, or the old names back;
