   Deviations from the plan (the planner's list first, as resolved):
   - **`WatermarkGen` keeps its name,** holding its content and position,
     rather than becoming §3.5's `WatermarkSpec`, which is
     `sheaf_edit::WatermarkSpec`'s. `Generator`'s z, scope and `replaces`
     moved; nothing was retired for them.
   - **`HeaderFooterSpec` takes the font** (§3.5 has none):
     `#[serde(default)]` to Helvetica, the legacy face, where
     `FontChoice`'s default is HelveticaBold. The dialog has family and
     style chips for it.
   - **`stamps::HeaderFooter` stayed `pub` until step 2 deleted it,**
     not crate-visible: `open::Facts` exposed it in a pub field that
     sheaf-ops builds with `..Default::default()`.
   - **No `impl Feed for Frozen`:** `recipe_digest(g, page)` feeds this
     page's fixed values (date, file, its number) inline; the whole map
     would cost O(n) a key. `CtxNeeds::any()` went, its one caller using
     `order()` and `label`; a Bates-only header reads neither `Order` nor
     `Labels`, its numbers being fixed. `Frozen::bates_number(page)` is
     named apart from the retired `bates_of`.
   - **A header on an empty `Pages` scope is Invalid,** as a watermark
     is, since the invariant forbids one; a legacy catalog header whose
     page indexes were all gone opened as none (step 1, before step 2
     deleted the legacy read).
   - **The page.generators cascade counts** the larger of the scope
     pages and the Bates entries gone, so for `All` it's the entries.
   - **`page_ctx` returns a `PageCtx`,** a missing label empty;
     `model_layout_digest(st, g, page, geom)` builds it, and
     `model_digest(g, &PageCtx)` serves the fuzz target, which has no
     `DocState`.
   - **`every_fact` carries a header sheaf draws today,** recognized from
     `/SheafGenerators`, since an older sheaf's catalog header opens as
     none now; the legacy fixture serves blocks_tests, fuzz's op_json
     document, others_tests and header_tests.
   - **`render_reads` reads `Order` and `Labels` whenever a generator's
     tokens need them,** intact or not: whether a page's base still
     matches depends on its place now, and the intact-only rule would
     miss a conflicting reorder.
   - **The reading order on a page with OCR and a header** is its own
     text, the header, then the recognized words, where the legacy header
     came last: the legacy OCR installer leaves `3 Tr` set without
     isolating it, so it goes after the generator blocks (putting it
     first made their text invisible; watermark.rs and watermark_tests
     caught it). sheaf-ops' text.rs search test moved its header to the
     cropped page, and the app's find test expects "page 5\nDraft\nTotal
     42". Slice 18 restores §11.4's order (a ledger row).
   - **`page_res` writes the resources inline when the OCR installer runs
     after the stack** (a bug fix): the installer copied them inline and
     left a `PageRes` placeholder naming an object never written, latent
     since slice 16 (a watermark plus OCR), found by an overlay test once
     the header joined the stack.
   - **A page whose content can't be read gets no header,** as watermarks
     don't, with the save's Note; the legacy writer installed it anyway.
     `SetHeaderFooter` refuses what `header::unfit` refuses, as
     recognition passes it over.
   - **deps' rescoped rule counts a Bates number's change** as a page's,
     so only the renumbered pages are written when nothing else changed.
   - **The header preview lowers `SetHeaderFooter` alone,** not
     `RemoveHeaderFooter` + `SetHeaderFooter` as the ledger row said: the
     header set again replaces its own old blocks, and its `replaces`
     (`{Header, Footer}` over `PagOrigin::REPLACED`) takes others' off the
     pages it covers, so the preview equals the result. The old strip
     took headers off every page, outside the scope too; Set replaces
     only on covered pages, as §3.5 says.
   - **`replaces` takes `PagOrigin::REPLACED`** (Acrobat's, an older
     sheaf's, another file's), as slice 16's watermark does, not §11.4's
     Acrobat alone.
   - **`/SheafHeaderFooter` is read by nothing:** §17 deletes
     `from_catalog`, its only reader. An older sheaf's header is told by
     the classifier (`/SheafHF`, `/SheafStamp` as `SheafLegacy`); Set
     replaces it and Remove counts and takes it, but nothing prefills
     from its settings, and `CATALOG_OWNED` keeps the key, so a save
     drops it (For Greg).
   - **`SaveRecord.drawn`'s value is `DrawnBlock { layout, recipe, key }`,**
     not §9.1's `(u128, u128)`: an `ObjKey::Block` is the `ResId` of the
     whole stream, `/SheafBlock` dictionary included, so the emitter
     can't recompute the old block's key; the key is the record map's
     `ObjKey::Block` or `ObjKey::Base { blob, obj, copy: 0 }` for the
     opened file's block. `Emission.drawn` is a flat map; an Append
     replaces the entries of the pages it wrote, read from its
     `ObjKey::Page` objects.
   - **`drawn` is filled in `Document::opened`,** from
     `facts.generators`, not `SaveRecord::opened`, which runs before
     recognition and has no `PageId`s; the test helpers fill it from the
     primary's generators. Kept blocks are noted with their own markers,
     and a kept block is an allowed drop too when the prior entry is
     another block of the recipe drawn now (a layout restored after an
     Append).
   - **Allowed drops cover a block laid out again for its boxes** (a crop
     or a turn) under the same recipe, as §3.5 lists; `LIVE_REDRAW` is set
     for `Order` and `Labels` only (§7.1), and on a step's `Order`
     classification too (information).
   - **The removal check leaves an allowed generator's old words out** on
     a page whose other blocks are judged: a restyled watermark and a
     renumbered header on one page gave a false derived veto without it.
     From the review, allowed drops are per page, since blocks are
     content-addressed and pages laid out alike share one:
     `Emission.allowed_drops` is `emit::AllowedDrops { keys, redrawn }`,
     `redrawn` the `(PageId, GenId)` pairs that drew a generator again
     from their saved block's recipe (whose old words are left out on
     that page alone), `keys` the blocks whose every page did so or is
     gone (not judged, and not read); the walk judges a shared block on
     each page that held it.
   - **The live closure memo is keyed by `(GenId, layout_reads(needs,
     ctx))`,** a digest of the geometry and only the context the tokens
     read.
   - **The reorder row moves the first half after the second:** one
     `MovePages` keeps its pages in document order, so it can't reverse
     them (a reverse was Unchanged); this renumbers every page. In
     session the "Page k of N" blocks are content-addressed and reused
     from other pages, so the section is page dicts and tree nodes.
   - **recovery.rs' encrypted Full-sidecar test** reaches Full through a
     record that can't take updates (`sound: false`), the header rule
     gone; plan_tests' `a_claim_what_sheaf_draws_breaks_gets_a_note`
     replaces the watermark's text for its Rewrite.
   - **`remove_watermark` and `remove_header_footer` stay as thin
     wrappers** over `remove_generated`; `narrow` takes kinds, a
     generator picked when `Generator::kinds()` overlaps them, and
     `header::kinds()` is the one definition of `{Header, Footer}` (Set's
     `replaces` and recognition use it).
   - **`others_on` narrows a clone first:** a block of the document's
     own header brought in from another revision of its file counts 0
     before a removal and 1 after without it (a fault run confirms the
     test catches it).
   - **What a page's filters take out already isn't counted again,** for
     Remove Watermark too: an artifact an earlier `include_authored`
     Remove filtered is cut with the rest to tell whether it's out. Pages
     without filters (every earlier test and corpus file) count and cut
     as slice 16 did; the dialogs' counts must be right after an unsaved
     Remove.
   - **Remove Watermark reports per-page progress and can be cancelled**
     (`pages_done`), on the shared lowering; a run of Remove
     Header/Footer steps sums its counts in one line, where it repeated
     the last step's.
   - **A Word-style head can't be taken by any splice** (font, colour or
     `gs` set outside a `q`): even `include_authored` leaves it, counted
     "left in place". The taken case uses heads each in their own `q`
     (`others_tests::RUNNING`).
   - **No `EditError::Content`:** no op of this slice fails on content
     (Set reads none, Remove counts an unreadable page), so slice 18 has
     it, as slice 16 left it.
   - **The dialogs' shared code is a module of its own,**
     `generator_dialog` (the faces moved, so no rows); the count runs
     `others_on` twice in one background task, without and with the
     author's own, so the line can say how many of the author's Remove
     can take; once a dialog opens, never a keystroke; checked against
     the opened snapshot by `(Snapshot.instance, version)` and unit-tested
     through `Count::take` (no headless test builds a dialog window). "The
     selection" is Crop's rule (more than one page selected), now
     `DocView::selected_indexes()`; Remove still removes from every page.
   - **Header & Footer… and Bates Numbering… toggle one dialog slot,** as
     `toggle_watermark` toggles the two z's; opening it doesn't close a
     Watermark dialog, as slice 16's didn't. Its Remove button is always
     shown. The dialog builds the op itself, so `header_footer_op` went;
     empty texts can't be applied ("Type something in at least one
     place"). Notices are each commit's line ("Set the header and
     footer"; the "shown now, written when you save" suffix went).
   - **`sheaf_ops::was_cancelled` knows `EditError::Cancelled`,** which
     the shared lowering's `pages_done` returns: a planner stopped part
     way said "… failed: canceled".
   - **Content-change tests use `ReplacePages`,** not `SetOcrText` or a
     filter-adding Remove as planned: those don't change a page's base,
     and the tests are about bases (two pages taking one copy, a stale
     base, a revert conflict, a page shown as another).
     `append_rewrite_a_page_replaced_by_its_own_page_is_a_form_of_its_own`
     asserts copy 2 (ReplacePages brings the form as an instance of its
     own); the two "rebased" tests are "replaced", the second's Rewrite
     now from OtherTarget plus Removes.
   - **`crop.rs`' corner tolerance is 3 pt:** PDFium's glyph box for
     "HEAD" tops out 2.25 pt above the cap height; a layout on the
     uncropped box would be 50–72 pt off.

     stay, the Rewrite graph's and stamp_lib's. rewrite_tests'

   Found while building:
   - **Proposal 8's redraw misses on the heavy, and the reorder isn't
     why** (step 8's probe): a page drawn in a group none drew before
     costs 3.7 ms for the view (the group's 128 members and keys), 15.5
     ms realizing the group's 128 deltas (each page 87 µs: 60 µs of it
     the header's content, its page classified for `replaces`, about half
     of that cold, then laid out, digested and compressed; 14 µs
     annotations; 14 µs the root and catalog every delta emits and
     `Part::page` drops) and about 15 ms for PDFium's open and cold
     render. Any header on every page costs that for a
     group not drawn before, frozen numbers too (32 ms with Bates alone);
     what live tokens add is that a reorder makes every visible group new
     (39 ms for a page drawn before the move, where Bates alone redrew it
     from its engine in 10.5 ms). A prototype emitting a group's deltas
     on 16 threads (scratch only, restored and checked with `cmp`) drew a
     moved page in 28 ms: not enough, and a threading change to the
     realizer besides.
   - **Bates apply cost nothing but its classify:** one `SetHeaderFooter`
     on a fresh open is 0.62–0.64 ms (slice 16: 157, 211 and 85 ms
     through `strip_stamps`).
   - **realize_corpus's header drew `<<n>>` literally** since slice 13
     (step 7): not a token.
   - **`append::Refused::Held` has no test now:** its only one was the
     derived-copy pair. A probe (the first page deleted and brought in

   The review (13 findings on the slice's changes, each checked against
   the code; all fixed):
   - **Proposal 8's gate measured the best case:** in the session that
     saved the header, the blocks a reorder draws are numbered in the
     file already (another page's before), so the section was page
     dictionaries and the tree. gate_7k now also opens the work copy
     afresh, moves the same half and saves: every block is written anew
     (3.33 MB on the heavy, within 8 MB, asserted) in 1.43 s (gate run;
     1.65–1.95 s in a probe), past 1 s. The probe's breakdown on the
     heavy: deps 60 ms; the emission about 1.1 s, of it 0.31 s
     classifying each page's content cold for others' headers to replace
     (`replacing`, `Source::blocks`) and 0.53 s rebuilding each page's
     content around its new block (`rebuilt`, its streams read and
     counted); the removal check 0.36 s (0.39 s before the change below);
     the rest numbering, the read-back and writing. Tried: the check
     skips an allowed block before reading it (safe: such a block was
     never judged); not tried, as each needs its own proof of identical
     output: classifying the written pages in parallel ahead of the
     emission, and a fast path for a page whose blocks alone change.
     The time is asserted only with `SHEAF_GATE_PROPOSAL_8`: Greg
     accepted the miss and kept live tokens (2026-10-22; the follow-up
     below).
   - **Allowed drops were per key, not per page** (two findings, one
     fix): a header's block is content-addressed, so a count-only header
     is one object on every page it covers, and one page's live redraw
     let it go everywhere, the words of a page that lost the header in
     the same save never judged. Now per page (Deviations); test:
     `a_shared_block_drawn_again_elsewhere_is_judged_where_it_went` (a
     page added where the header isn't, the header narrowed off one of
     five, misjudged: a derived veto and a Rewrite).
   - **A block was kept for its layout alone:** `intact` and `rebuilt`'s
     kept block compared `/L` but not `/R`, so a change that lays out
     alike (a centered slot's side margins, Bates numbers no text draws)
     kept blocks whose recipe and number were stale, and the record and a
     reopen read them: a false derived veto on the next reorder, and old
     Bates numbers back after a renumber. Both now require the recipe
     drawn there now (`recipe_digest`, the page's number in it); the
     realizer asks `intact` too, so such a page draws itself. Tests:
     `a_change_laid_out_alike_draws_its_blocks_again` and
     `bates_numbers_not_drawn_are_saved_as_renumbered`.
   - **Bates numbers could run past `u64::MAX`** (a panic in debug, 0
     after the largest in release): `header::numbered` is checked and
     returns None, and `set_header_footer` refuses it (Invalid). Test:
     `bates_numbers_never_run_past_the_largest`.
   - **The merged-header save note** searched `Saved::unnumbered`
     linearly for each page (O(pages²) for a file another tool merged
     every page of): it's in page order, so a binary search.
   - **Dead and stale code:** `header::draws` (its test reads `slots`),
     header.rs' own `CAP_HEIGHT` (its parent's, documented as one
     approximation for every Std14 face), `ResolvedOp::name`'s doc naming
     `set-page-base`, and retired.rs' qualified-only `rebase` (the tests'
     helper is `replaced` now; `page_insert::DocView::rebase` is checked
     bare again).
   - **The fuzz target and dictionaries** say headers: the target's doc,
     pdf.dict's `"header-footer"` and `"frozen":` (`/N` was there),
     op.dict's `"font":`, `"bates":`, `<<label>>`, `<<bates>>` and
     `<<N>>`.
   - **Comments re-wrapped** where the slice left them ragged or long

   - **The count dialogs' "page N" line** couldn't be reached

18. Done. OCR as content (proposal 26; bug 14): a page's recognized text
   is a §11.4 block, a `Layer` with a `BlockId` on its stack, drawn as a
   stream of its own, `/SheafBlock << /K /Ocr /B (b…) >>`, after the
   page's isolated content (`QClose`) and before the generators drawn
   over it, its text `/ShOCR /Sh… BDC q BT 3 Tr … ET Q EMC` with the list
   `<< /SheafOcrBlock (b…) >>` and the one glyphless font a file under
   fresh `/Sh…` names. The legacy installer went (`text_layer::install`,
   `strip`, `has_layer`, `to_content`, `/SheafOcrLayer` and `/SheafOcr`
   as written names) with the emitter's special cases for it
   (`replaced`, `fresh_balance`, `page_res`' inline resources), and the
   reading order is §11.4's again: the page's own text, the recognized
   words, then the header. Saved layers are removable: `SetOcrText` and
   `ClearOcrText` read the page's blocks as they lower and add
   `DropStreams(StreamSel::SheafOcr)` (a block that's a stream, or an
   older sheaf's `q` and layer, both or neither) and
   `DropMarked(MarkedSel::SheafOcr)` (a block another tool merged into a
   stream), so a re-OCR or a Clear over a saved layer plans a Rewrite
   (`REMOVES | REPLACES_TEXT`, `RemovedKind::OcrLayers`) with the old
   words gone; a page whose content can't be read fails the op with the
   new `EditError::Content { op, page, why }`. In a reopened file a saved
   block is found by its marker (`Marker::Ocr`) and kept in the
   static-over slot, so nesting never grows, a file saved with OCR alone
   included. An OCR run reads a page that changed during it again, in
   rounds in the run's group (twice at most), and counts a page it can't
   read as failed. The plugin API's 0.3 lost `ocr.page-text-layer`; 0.2's
   answers none until slice 20. Also: an ignored OCR corpus tier
   (`SHEAF_OCR_ONLY`), pdf.js and qpdf checks of the blocks, the 7k
   harness's OCR rows with an asserted census, retired.rs, the ledgers
   and the docs. The corpus counts hold, and every asserted gate holds.

     `BlockId::draw(rng, taken)` (random in [1, 2^53)) and `Display`
     (`b{:x}`), round-tripped by `BlockId::parse`. records.rs:

   Deviations from the plan (the planner's list first, as resolved):
   - **No `BlockKind`:** `Layer { id, body }`, the `Static` variant its
     kind. `Flattened` has no producer until slice 19's
     `FlattenAnnotations` (no unproduced variants); `BlockKind` comes
     with it.
   - **Two selectors only:** `StreamSel::SheafOcr` and
     `MarkedSel::SheafOcr`. §3.4's `StreamSel::SheafBlock(BlockId)` and
     `Isolation` have no producer.
   - **`/Sh…` names, not `/ShP<n>`:** `ContentWriter`'s namer names the
     list (`/Sh` and a digest), as slices 16 and 17's blocks are named.
   - **The block has a `q` of its own:** `/ShOCR <list> BDC q BT 3 Tr …
     ET Q EMC`, which §11.4 doesn't say; without it `3 Tr` reaches the
     generator blocks after it, which is why slice 17 put the legacy
     layer last.
   - **`EditError::Content { op, page, why }`** carries the
     `ContentError`'s text (`on_page`), not the error, whose sources
     aren't `Eq`; `EditError` stays `Clone + Eq`.
   - **Ids kept on replace:** a layer replacing the stack's, saved or
     not, keeps its id; a new one draws one. `BlockId::draw` takes
     `taken`, which `Lower::block_id` gives as the ids this op drew (no
     global scan); a pinned id is replayed as is.
   - **The merged-range check is `cut_together`:** `content::splice` on
     all the page's merged OCR ranges at once, which holds exactly when
     `splice_each` takes each, and gives the `SpliceError` for
     `ContentError::Unsafe`.
   - **`put_ocr` reads `Page(p)`** as `remove_generated` does, so a Set
     or Clear that changes nothing still conflicts under `Validate` with
     a concurrent change to the page (before, an empty layer always
     wrote, with the same conflict); an empty layer means none, so the
     tests that told versions apart by empty layers use one word.
   - **Re-queue rounds in the app,** not sheaf-ocr: the job takes a
     fixed list from one snapshot, so when a round finishes (not
     cancelled, undone or Esc'd after Finished) the queued pages still
     there start a new job on the current snapshot, in the run's group,
     with a new task and receiver, by `PageId` (`ReplacePages` keeps
     ids). Each page at most twice, then counted as changed; pages gone
     before their round and left when the run stops are counted as
     changed too. `Requeue` holds the bookkeeping so it's tested without
     GPUI; `Landed.stopped` lets `page_by_page` return the changes made
     before a stop with the stop. "read again", not "recognized again":
     a page read again can still be skipped or fail. A page that changed
     since its base and can't be read on it is failed, not re-queued
     (Content is lowered before Validate looks); OCR run again reads it.
   - **The plugin split for 0.2, no WIT bump:** `ocr::Host` is in
     v02.rs and v03.rs over `api::shared::recognized`; 0.2's
     `page-text-layer` answers none until slice 20 (a ledger row, 18 to
     20); 0.3.0 keeps its version though it lost a function (For Greg).
     The render interface's docs say "now … saved or not" as the text
     interface's do.
   - **Files saved with OCR alone are routed through `wrapped`'s
     `PageBlocks`:** `Source::markers` stays gated on `/SheafGenerators`;
     `stack`'s unmarked case reads the page's blocks (the read
     `wrapped` made, moved) and sends a page with sheaf's isolation or a
     stream-level block to `rebuilt`, which reads markers from what it
     decodes. `intact`, `untouched` and the render key stay on the gated
     read, so the base engine draws such a page when nothing is drawn on
     it, which is right.
   - **`intact` and `rebuilt` treat saved OCR as static-over content**
     after `QClose`; `rebuilt` leaves the kept blocks out of base′'s
     balance and puts back the names they draw with by one
     `names_used` pass over those streams, so the `QClose` count is
     exact even where another tool changed an OCR stream.
   - **Set fails on unreadable content** (§3.4: a base that can't be
     lexed fails the op that needs isolation), where the installer drew
     without lexing; Clear too, even over a stack layer alone. The app's
     flush counts such a page as failed and goes on.
   - **A saved layer's re-OCR plans a Rewrite from the effects**
     (`ReplacesText([OcrLayers n])`), not through the removal check's
     veto: kept::tests' `re_ocr_reopened` ports its reason;
     removal_tests' `a_re_ocr_over_a_saved_layer_is_a_rewrite` forces an
     Append, so its `ObjKey::Base` veto stands. History marks such a
     step as removing.
   - **A lone legacy layer stream stays and is counted,** in a Note of
     its own ("Recognized text sheaf wrote earlier stays on {pages}:
     taking it out would change what else the page draws.",
     `Cx.text_stayed`), not the stayed note, which names others'
     watermarks and headers. It's counted only where the page also holds
     saved text a filter takes out: lowering adds `DropStreams(SheafOcr)`
     for a block or a pair only (Found).
   - **The CID_FONTS version raise moved into `stack()`,** after a
     successful draw, so an unreadable page's text doesn't raise it;
     `needs()` stays for `needs_after`. `Sink::array` stays
     (`content_entries`); only `add` and `stream_dict` went, and
     `Cx::sym_dict` lost all but one caller and was inlined (no retired
     row: `Closure::sym_dict` is live under that name).
   - **Tests moved and merged:** the OCR tests of rewrite_tests.rs and
     materialize/tests.rs are materialize/ocr_tests.rs, save.rs
     importing its helpers (no retired rows for helpers that moved);
     `reinstall_replaces_previous_layer` and
     `a_re_ocr_over_a_base_layer_leaves_one_layer` became
     `replacing_a_saved_layer_rewrites_without_the_old_words`;
     `one_font_set_per_file` merged into `ocr_pages_share_one_font`;
     `empty_layer_writes_nothing` runs both ways. The reading-order test
     in sheaf-doc checks the streams' order, each stream's words through
     `text_bag` (a multiset); PDFium's order is sheaf-ops' text.rs's and
     the app's find test's.
   - **The PDFium word-box check of a saved block over an unbalanced
     base** is sheaf-ops' text.rs (`a_saved_block_over_an_unbalanced_
     base_stays_in_place`, both ways, through the text service under
     screen inputs before saving too): sheaf-doc's tests have no PDFium.
   - **The job-level unsaved-header check** is in sheaf-ops' realize.rs
     with its `Blind` engine: sheaf_ocr's `FakeSource` has no document to
     hold a header. The header is "Draft, for the board's review", over
     `HAS_TEXT_MIN_CHARS`, and a skip-pages-with-text job reads both
     pages.
   - **The corpus tier appends where the file takes one**
     (`appended_or_not`) for its adding saves, not `save()` as planned:
     planned, 893 files would Rewrite on the first save (817
     RemovalCheck, 46 BaseObjectsMissing, 30 BaseUnsound), 2 of them
     into the pre-existing form-check bug (Found). It asserts the
     effects instead (`CONTENT`, neither `REMOVES` nor `REPLACES_TEXT`).
     The form check runs after every save, the re-OCR and Clear Rewrites
     included (the review; it ran only after the adding saves before):
     the re-OCR's Rewrite hits that bug on the 8 files, so the tier fails
     at the pre-merge run as the watermark and header tiers do. Stronger
     than asked: the re-OCR and Clear must be Rewrites for
     `ReplacesText`, the re-OCR must give text to exactly the pages the
     first did, and each new word is drawn once. The header pass uses a
     single-slot header (`fx_header`): it's about isolation and the kept
     block, not numbering.
   - **The 7k census is of the Append's file,** read before it's cut
     back (`planned_save`), where slice 17's Bates census is of a
     Rewrite; and it doesn't assert a resources dictionary for each the
     file's pages had: each block names its own list, so each page has
     its own (7,000 lists added, printed).

   The review (11 findings on the slice's changes, each checked against
   the code; 10 fixed, one fixed with no measurable gain):
   - **The OCR tier skipped the form check after its Rewrites** (the
     only saves on this slice's removal paths): `nothing_found` now runs
     after the re-OCR and the Clear too, as the watermark and header
     tiers run it. Over the whole corpus it finds exactly the 8 files of
     the pre-existing bug (Found), each with the header and watermark
     tiers' findings, line for line; no other file. Left to surface at
     the pre-merge run like those tiers' failures, not asserted against
     a list.
   - **The run's message counted dropped results as recognized** (three
     findings, one fix): `done` counted every result, and `again` took
     off only those read again, so a page past the cap, gone before its
     round, or left when the run stopped was counted both recognized
     and changed. A dropped result is now counted where it's dropped
     (`Tally.dropped`) and recognized is `done - dropped`: a page read
     again counts once, as its last read went, and one never read again
     only as changed; `again` is the message's clause alone, and the
     progress bar is unchanged.
   - **Nothing tested the run's wiring** (two findings, one fix): the
     event bookkeeping, the flush, the choice of the next round (its
     pages, base and total) and the message moved out of the view into
     `Tally`, which `Tally::take(ev, &mut Document, stopped) -> Taken {
     changes, notice, next: Next::{Wait, Round(ids), Over(msg),
     Aborted(msg)} }` drives; the view only starts the round's job
     (`round()` returns its handle and task) and follows the commits.
     Tests: `a_run_reads_a_replaced_page_again_in_its_next_round` (a
     ReplacePages during round 1, `Next::Round([p1])` on the new
     version, p1's second read landing in the run's one version, the
     message "3 pages recognized, 1 read again after a change") and
     `a_page_not_read_again_counts_as_changed` (stopped, gone, and the
     cap: "2 pages recognized, 1 changed …" twice and "0 pages
     recognized, 2 read again after a change, 1 changed …"). Not a
     headless GPUI run: `sheaf_ocr::job::start` takes no engine, and the
     flush's timing against a commit would be the test's. Deviation: a
     run whose document is opened again (no longer Ready) is dropped at
     its next event, its job cancelled, where it used to linger to
     Finished with its flushes skipped.
   - **"Skip pages with text" depended on whether the text was saved**
     (`ViewPages::text_len` under `content_only`, which keeps a saved
     block but not the stack's layer): it now reads with `ocr_over`, as
     blank detection does, and pixels stay `content_only`. Test:
     realize.rs' `ocr_skips_a_page_recognized_before_saved_or_not` (a
     page given 33 characters of text, skipped unsaved and on the file
     saved and opened again, both read alike); it fails with the old
     inputs. document-model.md's consumer tables and Text layers say so.
   - **"Unsaved header" wording** where `content_only` sets aside sheaf's
     header saved or not: the WIT's `recognize` (0.3 only; `wit/0.2` is
     frozen), docs/plugins.md's `ocr`, `RenderSource`, the app's
     `EngineRender`, `ViewPages`, `content_only` and blank.rs's module
     doc; document-model.md's flush paragraph names a ReplacePages as the
     Conflict, not slice 17's deleted header strip.
   - **`put_ocr` built a second stack** for `with_filters` with no
     filters, and looked its page up three times: it skips
     `with_filters` when there are none and passes its one `def` to
     `saved_ocr`. Output identical (the same stack either way). The
     history row's 7,000 lowered `SetOcrText`: 48.3 ms in the gate run
     after, five runs 48.0–52.1 ms (median 48.8 ms) against step 7's
     48.4 ms, so not the cause of the rise from 38 ms: that's the page's
     blocks read for the filters (`saved_ocr`), which correctness needs.
   - **Fixture builders copied** in tx/ocr_tests.rs and ocr_run.rs'

   Deviations from the plan (the planner's list first, as resolved):
   - **Export carries its `LowerCx`:** a `Snapshot` alone can't lower,
     so `ExportFrom { snap, cx: Arc<LowerCx> }` (`Document::export_from`)
     travels with the export, and what its transforms make draws ids
     from the document's allocator, not scratch ids. `save::rewrite` and
     `rewrite_to_path` take `&Document` for it; realize_corpus and the 7k
     AES row, which hold a modified snapshot, build an `ExportFrom`. The
     whole-document Rewrites answer what they ask as print does, as the
     old `written()` ignored the plan's asks; their bytes are unchanged
     (encrypted_corpus and the determinism tests).
   - **`BlockKind` is derived:** `Layer { id, body }` stays, and
     `Layer::kind()` gives `BlockKind::{Ocr, Flattened}` from the body.
   - **`PinnedAp` covers marks only,** as `MarkAp` (no AnnotId, author,
     dates or `/NM`; an attachment's file isn't drawn and isn't
     captured); a widget's pinned appearance is M10 slice 15's
     `FlattenFields`, and a flattened widget is a `Base` placement of its
     form. A pinned form is drawn by `annot::appearance`, the drawing
     emission uses, not by emission (which would build the dictionary
     and `/SheafAnnot` too); the identity matrix places it, its box its
     `/Rect`, and PDFium's grid snap leaves pixels within 2 a channel.
   - **`save_with` is the save core:** `save_with(doc, path, SaveHow,
     answers, p)` over the private `saved_as`; `SaveHow::Append` isn't
     `forced_append` (which asks nothing, so `-o --append` would silently
     break signatures) but the production planner `appending`, with
     `Refusal::Chosen` letting a Rewrite stand in only when the reader
     chose to break signatures. sheaf-ops' `common::planned`,
     forms_saves' `save` and gate_7k's reorder save call
     `save_with(Planned)`, the app's planned Save As, which `SaveTo` can't
     say by design.
   - **save.rs keeps `rewrite` and `rewrite_to_path`** as a fixtures-only
     `whole` module over `export::run(Export::whole)`, beside the live
     `text_string` and `validate` (Found: `validate` has no caller):
     materialize_corpus's IDENTITY, encrypted_corpus and the both-ways
     harness read a save's bytes through them.
   - **`KeepPages`' Headings rule is `subset`'s outline rule,** not
     DeletePages' promotion: before the delete, a bookmark whose target
     isn't a kept page (`Target::Kept` included) stays only as a heading
     over kept descendants. Connectors, fields shown only on pages left
     out and labels follow the delete's cascades, as `subset` did; the
     recorded MaxBytes parts and the CLI's part sizes are unchanged (the
     sheaf-ops fixture's three rows confirmed in review against main
     3c72df2's split, ten runs alike).
   - **RemoveMarkup's emission option is a Profile field,**
     `unheld: Unheld { Keep, Only(MarkupKeep) }`, set by the `ExportTx`
     and copied by `run` (§12's Profile has three fields); two
     RemoveMarkups keep only what both keep. No post-pass and no model
     field.
   - **The asks come from the plan,** in `run`, not `preflight`: `Gate`
     holds refusals only (`OwnFile`, `Exists`, `Refused { transform, cap
     }`). The Signatures ask is limited to signatures whose field the
     exported state still holds (a certification always counts).
     **Print answers its own** (`PRINT_ANSWERS`: break signatures, drop
     XFA). **Print without markup gets `RemovePrivateData`** (§16 row 27)
     and `Private::Scrub` (review): written as Strip writes it, but what
     the filters can't take out (a page whose content can't be read, a
     list that can't be written again) is a note (`verify::private_left`),
     not a failure, so printing, page images and text never fail on an
     older sheaf's leftovers; Clean Copy keeps Strip, failing closed. A
     transform's Strip raises only a Keep profile. With markup print keeps
     them.
   - **The preview doesn't stay on view inputs alone:** the plan kept
     print preview as `ViewInputs::print(markup)`, with a test that it
     equals the Print preset's bytes. That test found 136 px different
     with markup (PDFium's form filler draws a box for a check box with
     states and no `/AS`, which the print flatten draws as nothing, M10
     bug 10), so with markup the preview realizes the print's state,
     the page's printed annotations flattened as print flattens them
     (`export::print_preview`, memoized a page in `PrintContext.printed`),
     under print's inputs; without markup it's the version under
     `ViewInputs::print`. 0 px differ both ways; the dialog no longer
     paints marks with GPUI over the preview.
   - **The schema grew in place** at 1.0 (`SHEAF_SCHEMA_UPDATE=1`):
     `PageSource::{Blank, Images}`, `Fit` and `FlattenAnnotations`, safe
     because nothing persisted Op JSON before `sheaf edit`. From this
     slice an addition bumps the minor. `Transform` is outside the
     envelope and its schema.
   - **Combine's outline and labels; generators extend:** on a full open
     the opened outline's roots are deleted and its labels cleared in the
     transaction, then each file's bookmarks re-added from its source's
     flat outline, so the output's outline and labels are today's. The
     generators stay, so a first file's All-scope header covers the pages
     combined after it (For Greg). The app fills the origin window when
     it has no document, else a new one; its dialog refuses an output
     open in a window (`workspace::is_open`). The hand-off is a
     `Cell<Option<Box<…>>>` taken once, not `Arc<Mutex<Option<
     Document>>>`: events go by reference on the UI thread, and the
     Session carries its view facts (`Session.view`), without which the
     adopted window would lose the first file's attachments, portfolio,
     layers and form facts.
   - **`open::read`:** `open::file` has 104 callers; `open::read(path,
     pw, p)` holds its body with progress, `Session::open` calls it, and
     `open::file` calls it with `NoProgress`.
   - **The integration-test lint allows:** an integration test is a
     crate of its own, and the crate root's `cfg_attr(test, allow(…))`
     doesn't reach it, so each one that calls a banned method (all
     `std::env::temp_dir`, for scratch files) has its own
     `#![allow(clippy::disallowed_methods)]`: sheaf-ops' `append_corpus`,
     `blank`, `comments`, `crop`, `forms_open`, `gate_7k`, `progress`,
     `scan_blanks` and `tests/common` (a module allow covering every test
     that includes it), and sheaf-render's `appended_pages`, `flatten`,
     `markup_appearance` and `ocr_layer`. sheaf-cli has no `clippy.toml`
     and needs none.
   - **No text export exists** as an export: slice 14's "print and text
     export" left print and page images; text (`sheaf export -f text`)
     reads the text service and writes durably. The app's exports run as
     jobs (review): `DocView::write_export` is `start_job` and `drive`,
     one at a time with page progress and Escape, for Extract, Export
     Flattened, Clean Copy and Save as PDF; Split and page images were
     jobs already.
   - **The writer is `write_built`,** not `full::write`, a retired name
     (slice 9's old writer); `ObjKey::Built(ObjectId)` (tag 20) names its
     bodies and is never used for encryption.
   - **`Fit` moved into sheaf-edit** (`images::PageFit` retired), the
     types ops carry living there (§6.1); `images::files_to_pdf` lost its
     only caller and went.
   - **`Tx::check` builds nothing:** a memory source's check stands the
     primary in for it; Blank's range is checked against `count`, and an
     images insert's `pages` are taken on trust (a TIFF's page count is
     known only once decoded), so a check of an undecodable image passes
     where applying it is `Invalid` (tested). The resolved op's `Src`
     holds the blob from resolve into the step, so there's no separate
     `Tx::pin`; the callers pin the image blobs.
   - **Images are accepted by their bytes** (`BlobKind::image(bytes)`), as
     a watermark's image is, since a blob keeps the kind it was first
     interned as.
   - **Adopted stamps hold their file's form:** without the cache an
     adopted Acrobat stamp would be `NotFound`, so `ForeignAnnot.stamp`
     names its `/AP /N` when its conversion is a page stamp and the
     held-stamp index lists it; `find_stamp` finds `FormRef::Base`, and
     nothing is interned.
   - **`LegacySel::Streams` and `Resources`,** not `Stream(StreamSel)`: a
     strip takes every marker, never a subset; `StreamSel` would need
     variants `DropStreams` never takes; resource names belong to the
     page; and the old flatten's `/SheafFlat<n>` stream has no marker to
     select it by. `private_filters(def)` is pure, rather than
     `strip_private(lw, page)`. Markers and lists the file holds are the
     filters'; the profile covers what the emitter writes anew, so Strip
     without the filters fails its post-condition.
   - **`sheaf-anon:` is a KEYS row** (the `/NM` sheaf gives a comment with
     none when a reply made in sheaf names it), which §15 doesn't list.
     The neutral `/NM` is a UUID-shaped xxh3-128 digest of the sheaf name.
   - **OCR and generator lists under Strip** are `/ShOCR BMC` with no
     list and `<< /Type /Pagination /Subtype … >>`, the header's layout
     digest not cached.
   - **The post-condition reads the Rewrite's graph,** not the bytes:
     plaintext, and what a Dense export writes. Deferred streams are
     empty there; the rest of their page is read (tested on a flattened
     page).
   - **Artifacts are `BMC`, not `BDC`:** no property list or artifact
     `/Type` fits a flattened annotation; `PlaceTag::Artifact` when the
     page's source has a `StructTreeRoot`. They need PDF 1.4, so
     `needs_after` walks pages for files below 1.4 (it walked below 1.2).
   - **Removed annotations reach `keep_only` through
     `Emission::removed_annots`,** which the emitter computes, so a
     delete's OBJRs in tagged files are pruned too.
   - **What flatten takes:** Hidden and NoView (and under Printable the
     unprinted) are neither drawn nor removed; annotations the records
     don't hold (printer's marks, media, widgets outside the form) stay,
     where the old flatten drew them; a frame with no area draws nothing
     (it drew at scale 1); an unreadable page is `EditError::Content`.
   - **Deferred bodies are always deflated,** their dictionary saying
     `/FlateDecode` before the data exists (lopdf's `compress` skips
     data that doesn't shrink). They are the codebase's first `Deferred`
     producers; the Rewrite, Append and realizer took them unchanged.
   - **`RemovedKind::Flattened`** is new ("page's flattened
     annotations"), and `PrivateData` replaced `OlderSettings`.
   - **The presets are constructors** carrying `from` and `out`; the
     app's ask dialog generalized to `Asking::{Save, Export}` with export
     wording; a split checks every part's asks before it writes any
     (`export::check`, `run`'s plan without the write, review), so one
     that asks writes nothing and runs again with the answer, and Remove
     Blanks checks its rejects file before it writes the kept one, as
     proposal 40 says (`sheaf split` exited 3 with parts written); Remove
     Blanks' rejects file is an export (Dense, outline
     dropped, labels kept), the document unchanged. A TIFF export still
     streams to `.tif.part` and renames (7,000 pages in memory could take
     gigabytes); page images and split parts give the export a
     zero-weight child progress.
   - **Transform caps** (the caps table has no row): `KeepPages` is
     Plugin (a delete's), `RemoveMarkup` and `RemovePrivateData`
     Approval; `Transform` is `non_exhaustive`, so a later one needs User
     until it has a row. Transform JSON is externally tagged.
   - **A scan inserts one `Memory(Images)` blob** made by `images::to_pdf`
     (`scan::made_pages`), not an image blob a page: 18.0 ms made once
     against 23.2 ms written to PNG and read back (a 2550×3300 bitonal
     page, release, median of 5), and nothing held twice. Images to PDF
     takes the same path, since `--dpi` overrides the images' resolution
     and no op field says that.
   - **The summary** is a Session (`new_empty` and an insert of a
     `Memory(Summary)` blob), its `/Info` the empty primary's; its Pages
     layout still builds an eager graph through `ResObjects` and
     `stamp_lib::page_forms` (which trims a clone of an eager document),
     written by `write_built`. So the to_lopdf.rs and Objects-seam rows'
     slice-19 parts are deleted in parts (the ledger says what remains,
     for slice 20).
   - **Session's API beyond §14.2's sketch:** `From<Document>`, `hold`,
     `tx(actor)` with the names granted, `commit_as`, `export_from`
     (`from()` clashed with `From::from`), `view`; `export` returns
     `Exported` (no `ExportReport`). `Session::edit` and `preview(&
     Envelope)` take envelopes and alone set `ops_from_file`; Combine,
     scan, Images to PDF and the summary commit by id. There's no
     `Preview.consequences`: the dry run's are computed in sheaf-ops
     (`effects::judge` and `sig_impact`), as putting `judge` in every
     `Tx::preview` would cost the app's dialogs at 7k pages.
   - **`Tx::ops_from_file()`,** not `from_file()`: clippy's
     `wrong_self_convention` fails a `from_*` method taking self.
   - **Output shapes and CLI JSON:** `created` is `{"ops": […], "locals":
     {…}}`, `version` the label or null, `strategy` "append", "rewrite"
     or null; commit notices and save notes go to stderr as `note:`
     lines. Every CLI JSON is printed with sorted keys (`print_json`):
     GPUI turns on serde_json's `preserve_order`, so the app's `sheaf
     edit` and `sheaf-cli` printed keys in different orders and the
     goldens failed under `cargo test --workspace`.
   - **Progress off a terminal prints plain lines** (`editing…`, a line a
     message) where indicatif printed nothing, for every subcommand: the
     130 golden needs a first line, and warnings were lost on a pipe.
     The Ctrl-C handler cancels before it prints "stopping…".
   - **The 130 golden holds its edits on standard input:** SIGINT after
     `editing…`, then the edits written, so it doesn't race a fast edit
     (20,000 blank pages finished first under the workspace run).
   - **`--with NAME=PATH[:PASSWORD_ENV]`:** a value naming an existing
     file is taken whole, so `C:\a.pdf` stays a path. `--dry-run`
     conflicts with `-o`, `--in-place` and `--force`; `--append` needs
     `-o`; `--schema` is exclusive; `inspect` needs `--json`.
   - **`--force` audit:** comments csv, text and data export gained
     `--force` (they overwrote silently); every other subcommand already
     replaced only with it.
   - **Clipboard:** a Base or Pinned stamp becomes a one-page PDF blob at
     copy, not paste, so the cache never holds a file's `Src`; `by_stem`,
     since `stems` is a retired bare name.
   - **Every way out:** Save As both ways uses `How::save` (the Session's
     `SaveHow::Append` correctly refuses this document: the Bates header
     drops `/Perms /UR3`); the Full sidecar is forced unsound; Combine is
     the file and a blank page (a self-combine's renamed copy repeats the
     file's own findings under new names); the form check runs last, so
     each behavior's fault trips its own assertion. `export_round_trips`
     asserts its one known failure, as the watermark tier asserts 0112530.
   - **Renamed tests:** `a_stamp_resolves_from_the_store_a_source_or_the_
     cache` is `…_from_the_store_or_a_source`, and `stamps_and_
     attachments_survive_an_empty_cache(_appended)` is `stamps_and_
     attachments_are_read_from_the_file(_appended)`; earlier notes name
     the old ones.
   - **Flattened annotations draw last** (review): §11.4's `[… QClose
     static-over… gen-over…]` drew a flatten's block under the
     generators over the page, so a flattened page put its annotations
     under an Over watermark and the header, where every viewer draws
     annotations over all of a page's content (ISO 32000-1 12.5) and the
     old flatten drew them last. Recognized text keeps the static-over
     slot; Flat blocks, the file's and new ones, go after the generators:
     `[gen-under… QOpen base′… QClose ocr… gen-over… flat…]`, and
     `content::intact` reads the trailing Flat blocks off first
     (`flats_last`), so a page opened again is written as it is and
     nesting doesn't grow as it's flattened again.
   - **The comment exports refuse the open file** (review): §12.1's gate
     is `export::not_its_file`, which `preflight` asks, and so do
     sheaf-ops' `comments::summary_to` and `comments::write_to`, which the
     Comments panel's exports and `sheaf comments summary|csv|text|export`
     write through (they replaced the open PDF given its path and
     `--force` or the OS's overwrite prompt).
   - **Blank pages stop at the page tree's limit** (review):
     `PageSource::Blank`'s count is refused past
     `Limits::DEFAULT.page_tree.pages` (0xFFFFF − 1), what `Source::open`
     reads back, in the shared resolve, so `Tx::check` and apply refuse
     it before any is made (`sheaf edit --dry-run` of 2,000,000 took 24.6
     s and 4.8 GB, debug, before failing; now 0.10 s and 18 MB). An
     insert's total with the document's pages isn't
     checked: a replacement adds none.
   - **The private-data read fails closed a stream at a time** (review):
     `private::found` reads a page whose content can't be read whole one
     stream at a time, so one stream that can't be decoded no longer
     hides an older sheaf's list in another; a stream that can't be
     decoded counts when its bytes say `/Sheaf`, and one past the content
     limit counts. lopdf hands back what of a broken deflated stream
     inflates, so only other filters and the limit reach that path.
   - **The print preview keeps a page it can't make** (review):
     `PrintContext.printed` holds `Option<DocState>`, so a page whose
     flatten fails is lowered and logged once; the lowering stays on the
     UI thread (one page's flatten on an `ExportTx`).

     apart by the two strategies, so the reopened pages' resources
     differed by that name (`/ShTIUIYP` against `/ShSVPKPP`). `StampForm`
     carries the name it's drawn by (`res`, `StampForm::written` for a
     number's, as before), and `emit::annots`' `pinned` names the stamp's
     page by its `FormRef::digest`; every other appearance is written as
     before. The property's seed is kept (`crates/sheaf-doc/proptest-
     regressions/materialize/append_rewrite_tests.txt`, a real failure),
     so the default 32-case run replays it; it fails without the fix.
     Marks written outside a flatten still name a library stamp's page by

   For Greg:
   - **The flattened export's RSS gate is unattainable by construction**
     (`FlattenAnnotations { All }` on the heavy 7k at a peak of at most
     1.5× the file + 200 MB, 220.5 MB, in the flatten's own process). Five
     runs, each in a process of its own on a quiet machine: opening the
     heavy alone peaks at 221 MB (216 MB added, all still held when the
     export starts), so any flatten in that process starts at the limit;
     the export then peaks at 513–515 MB (median 514 MB; 292–295 MB added,
     median 293). Most of that is the Rewrite's: a plain Rewrite of the
     heavy adds 252 MB (the gates' own Rewrite part), the primary loaded
     eagerly to copy it (`materialize::graph::eager`), which no slice of
     M10.5 makes lazy. It takes 1.25–1.52 s (median 1.29 s; slice 2's
     flatten, which kept the 7,000 widgets, 3.49 s and 420 MB). What the
     export adds misses too (293 MB against 220.5). The row is measured on
     every run with the open's peak printed beside it, and asserted only
     with `SHEAF_GATE_FLATTEN` (a ledger row, as proposal 8's misses
     are). Meeting it needs a Rewrite that copies the primary's objects
     without loading the file whole (a streaming copy, its pruning and
     `keep_only` included) and a gate on what the export adds rather
     than the process's peak; your ruling: keep the gate and plan that
     work, or restate it.
   - **B5 reaches the exports' and the command line's signature ask:**
     an export asks about every signature in what it exports whenever
     the opened file has one, judged by `/V` and permissions
     (`sig_impact`), not by whether it validates, so a signature already
     invalid when opened still asks. In the corpus,
     signatures/safedocs/0008830.pdf and 0010094.pdf, whose signatures
     pyHanko finds neither intact nor valid, exit 3 on a mark add (37
     unencrypted files have such a signature), and a file written with
     `--signatures break` still asks on its next edit (`append_anyway:
     true`, "… removed since the last save"). Not fixed here (B5).
   - **The Op schema grew in place at 1.0** (`PageSource::{Blank,
     Images}`, `Fit`, `FlattenAnnotations`): nothing was persisted
     before `sheaf edit`, which persists from now on, so a later addition
     bumps the minor.
   - **The neutral `/NM` is an unkeyed digest** of the sheaf name:
     anyone holding both files can match a clean copy's marks to the
     source's ids, which are random and say nothing else.
   - **`new_empty`'s primary is a file of no pages** (`Memory(Blank)`,
     the only origin `Source::open` accepts with none); a scan, Images to
     PDF and the summary insert into it. The summary's `/Info` (Title,
     Producer, CreationDate) is gone with it: no op sets document info.
   - **Combine keeps the first file's generators,** so its All-scope
     header covers the pages combined after it (pinned by a test); it
     fills the origin window when that's empty; the adopted window keeps
     the first file's form facts as opened, and `xfa_values_dropped`
     isn't set from Combine's `PRINT_ANSWERS`, so a hybrid first file
     whose XFA held values could still show the "XFA part holds values"
     bar after the combine dropped it.
   - **Print answers its own asks** (`PRINT_ANSWERS`: signatures broken,
     XFA dropped) for print, page images and Save as PDF; print with
     markup flattens widgets by their `/AS`, so a check box with states
     and no `/AS` prints nothing (M10 bug 10), where print kept widgets
     live before.
   - **A non-widget with states and no `/AS`:** PDFium shows nothing (it
     falls back to `/V`, then `/Off`), but flatten keeps the plan's
     first-state fallback for non-widgets, as the old flatten did, so
     flattening such a comment draws what no viewer showed.
   - **The command line's `-o` on a signed file asks** (exit 3) where it
     copy-appended; `--append` copy-appends any file on request, and
     `--signatures break` rewrites.
   - **A clean copy fails closed** ("it would hold sheaf's private data:
